Create `internal/dockerstacks/fakeengine_test.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"path"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
	"aurago/internal/testutil"
)

// fakeEngine is an httptest server that speaks the part of the Docker Engine
// API the stacks service uses, with state: containers (create, start, inspect,
// logs, kill, remove), images (inspect, pull, save, load, tag), an in-memory
// file tree behind the archive API, volumes and the system df.
//
// dockerutil's version transport probes GET /version first and rewrites
// "/v1.45/" paths to the negotiated version, so the fake answers /version with
// the configured API and serves every other route under /v1.45/ (any /v1.NN/
// request maps onto it).
//
// Helper containers behave by role when they are started:
//
//   - lister: prints the files of the fake file tree that `find` would list and
//     exits 0;
//   - runner: prints runnerLines (each as stdout) and exits with runnerExit, but
//     only after runnerGate is closed when it is set;
//   - anything else: stays running until the test finishes it.
type fakeEngine struct {
	t      *testing.T
	server *httptest.Server
	mux    *http.ServeMux

	mu         sync.Mutex
	api        string
	os, arch   string
	containers map[string]*fakeContainer // by id
	order      []string                  // container ids in creation order
	images     map[string]string         // reference -> image id
	files      map[string][]byte
	modes      map[string]int64
	dirs       map[string]bool
	volumes    []fakeVolume
	log        []string

	pullFails   string // non-empty: POST /images/create answers 500 with this message
	pulled      []string
	loadedBody  []byte
	loadReply   string
	savedRefs   []string
	runnerLines []string
	runnerExit  int
	runnerGate  chan struct{}
	runnerErr   string // written to stderr before the exit
	listerExit  int
	listerErr   string
	startFails  string // non-empty: POST .../start of a lister answers 500
	dfStatus    int    // non-zero: GET /system/df answers this status
	putQueries  []string
	nextID      int
}

type fakePort struct {
	IP      string
	Private int
	Public  int
	Proto   string
}

type fakeVolume struct {
	Name, Driver string
	Project      string
	Size         int64
}

type fakeContainer struct {
	id, name string
	image    string
	labels   map[string]string
	spec     map[string]any
	state    string // created | running | exited
	status   string // list status text; derived when empty
	health   string
	exitCode int
	ports    []fakePort
	created  int64
	logs     []byte
	done     chan struct{}
	tty      bool
}

const fakeStacksDir = "/opt/stacks"

func newFakeEngine(t *testing.T) *fakeEngine {
	t.Helper()
	fe := &fakeEngine{
		t:          t,
		api:        "1.45",
		os:         "linux",
		arch:       "amd64",
		containers: map[string]*fakeContainer{},
		images:     map[string]string{},
		files:      map[string][]byte{},
		modes:      map[string]int64{},
		dirs:       map[string]bool{fakeStacksDir: true},
		loadReply:  `{"stream":"Loaded image ID: sha256:loadedimage\n"}` + "\n",
	}
	fe.mux = http.NewServeMux()
	fe.routes()
	fe.server = testutil.NewHTTPServer(t, http.HandlerFunc(fe.serve))
	t.Cleanup(fe.server.Close)
	return fe
}

var reFakeAPIPrefix = regexp.MustCompile(`^/v1\.\d+/`)

func (fe *fakeEngine) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	entry := r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path
	if r.URL.RawQuery != "" {
		entry += "?" + r.URL.RawQuery
	}
	fe.mu.Lock()
	fe.log = append(fe.log, entry)
	fe.mu.Unlock()
	if r.URL.Path != "/version" {
		r2 := r.Clone(r.Context())
		r2.URL.Path = reFakeAPIPrefix.ReplaceAllString(r.URL.Path, "/v1.45/")
		r = r2
	}
	fe.mux.ServeHTTP(w, r)
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) routes() {
	m := fe.mux
	m.HandleFunc("GET /version", fe.handleVersion)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/version", fe.handleVersion)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/containers/json", fe.handleList)
	m.HandleFunc("POST /v1.45/containers/create", fe.handleCreate)
	m.HandleFunc("POST /v1.45/containers/{id}/start", fe.handleStart)
	m.HandleFunc("POST /v1.45/containers/{id}/kill", fe.handleKill)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/containers/{id}/json", fe.handleInspect)
	m.HandleFunc("DELETE /v1.45/containers/{id}", fe.handleRemove)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/containers/{id}/logs", fe.handleLogs)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/containers/{id}/archive", fe.handleArchiveGet)
	m.HandleFunc("PUT /v1.45/containers/{id}/archive", fe.handleArchivePut)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/images/{ref}/json", fe.handleImageInspect)
	m.HandleFunc("POST /v1.45/images/create", fe.handleImagePull)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/images/{ref}/get", fe.handleImageSave)
	m.HandleFunc("POST /v1.45/images/load", fe.handleImageLoad)
	m.HandleFunc("POST /v1.45/images/{ref}/tag", fe.handleImageTag)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/volumes", fe.handleVolumes)
	m.HandleFunc("GET /v1.45/system/df", fe.handleDF)
}

func fakeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, body any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(body)
}

func fakeMessage(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, format string, args ...any) {
	fakeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"message": fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)})
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) handleVersion(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	fakeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{
		"Version": "27.3.1", "ApiVersion": fe.api, "MinAPIVersion": "1.24", "Os": fe.os, "Arch": fe.arch,
	})
}

// ---- test-side helpers -------------------------------------------------------

func (fe *fakeEngine) host() dockerhost.Host {
	return dockerhost.Host{ID: "h_fake", Name: "fake", Kind: dockerhost.KindTCP, Address: "127.0.0.1", Port: 1,
		StacksDir: fakeStacksDir, HostSocketPath: dockerhost.DefaultHostSocketPath, Color: "blue"}
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) client(t *testing.T) *dockerutil.Client {
	t.Helper()
	port := fe.server.Listener.Addr().String()
	c := dockerutil.NewClient("tcp://"+port, 5*time.Second)
	t.Cleanup(c.CloseIdleConnections)
	return c
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) requests() []string {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	return slices.Clone(fe.log)
}

// requestCount counts the logged requests that start with prefix ("POST /containers/create").
func (fe *fakeEngine) requestCount(prefix string) int {
	n := 0
	for _, r := range fe.requests() {
		method, rest, _ := strings.Cut(r, " ")
		rest = reFakeAPIPrefix.ReplaceAllString(rest, "/")
		if strings.HasPrefix(method+" "+rest, prefix) {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) setVersion(api, os, arch string) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	fe.api, fe.os, fe.arch = api, os, arch
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) addImage(ref, id string) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	fe.images[ref] = id
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) hasImage(ref string) bool {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	_, ok := fe.images[ref]
	return ok
}

// prepared gives the fake a host that is already prepared: the runner image and
// a matching IO container.
func (fe *fakeEngine) prepared() {
	fe.addImage(RunnerImage, "sha256:runnerimage")
	h := fe.host()
	fe.addContainer(IOContainerName, ioSpec(RunnerImage, h), "created", 0)
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) putFile(p, content string) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	fe.files[p] = []byte(content)
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) file(p string) (string, bool) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	b, ok := fe.files[p]
	return string(b), ok
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) mode(p string) int64 {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	return fe.modes[p]
}

// addContainer registers a container with the payload it would have been created from.
func (fe *fakeEngine) addContainer(name string, spec containerSpec, state string, exit int) *fakeContainer {
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(spec)
	var generic map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &generic)
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	fc := fe.newContainerLocked(name, generic)
	fc.state, fc.exitCode = state, exit
	if state == "exited" {
		close(fc.done)
	}
	return fc
}

// addProjectContainer registers a compose project container of the fake host.
func (fe *fakeEngine) addProjectContainer(name, project, service, state, status, health string, created int64, ports ...fakePort) *fakeContainer {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	fc := fe.newContainerLocked(name, map[string]any{"Image": service + ":latest"})
	fc.labels = map[string]string{
		"com.docker.compose.project":             project,
		"com.docker.compose.service":             service,
		"com.docker.compose.project.working_dir": path.Join(fakeStacksDir, project),
	}
	fc.image, fc.state, fc.status, fc.health, fc.created, fc.ports = service+":latest", state, status, health, created, ports
	if state == "exited" {
		fc.exitCode = 1
		close(fc.done)
	}
	return fc
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) container(name string) *fakeContainer {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	for _, fc := range fe.containers {
		if fc.name == name {
			return fc
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) containersWithRole(role string) []*fakeContainer {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	var out []*fakeContainer
	for _, id := range fe.order {
		if fc := fe.containers[id]; fc != nil && fc.labels[LabelRole] == role {
			out = append(out, fc)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) specOf(fc *fakeContainer) map[string]any {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	return fc.spec
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) newContainerLocked(name string, spec map[string]any) *fakeContainer {
	fe.nextID++
	id := fmt.Sprintf("%012x%052x", fe.nextID, fe.nextID)
	labels := map[string]string{}
	if raw, ok := spec["Labels"].(map[string]any); ok {
		for k, v := range raw {
			labels[k], _ = v.(string)
		}
	}
	image, _ := spec["Image"].(string)
	fc := &fakeContainer{id: id, name: name, image: image, labels: labels, spec: spec, state: "created",
		created: time.Now().Unix(), done: make(chan struct{})}
	fe.containers[id] = fc
	fe.order = append(fe.order, id)
	return fc
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) lookupLocked(ref string) *fakeContainer {
	if fc := fe.containers[ref]; fc != nil {
		return fc
	}
	for _, fc := range fe.containers {
		if fc.name == ref || (len(ref) >= 4 && strings.HasPrefix(fc.id, ref)) {
			return fc
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// emit appends text to the container's log (stream 1 = stdout, 2 = stderr).
func (fe *fakeEngine) emit(fc *fakeContainer, stream byte, text string) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	header := make([]byte, 8)
	header[0] = stream
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(header[4:], uint32(len(text)))
	fc.logs = append(append(fc.logs, header...), text...)
}

// finish marks a running container as exited.
func (fe *fakeEngine) finish(fc *fakeContainer, exit int) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	if fc.state == "exited" {
		return
	}
	fc.state, fc.exitCode = "exited", exit
	close(fc.done)
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) isRunning(fc *fakeContainer) bool {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	return fc.state == "running"
}
```

```go
package dockerstacks

	"context"

	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// The Hosts implementation over fake engines, and the small waiting and comparing helpers of the tests.

// ---- hosts -------------------------------------------------------------------

// fakeHosts satisfies Hosts over fake engines.
type fakeHosts struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	hosts   map[string]dockerhost.Host
	clients map[string]*dockerutil.Client
	down    map[string]bool
}

func newFakeHosts() *fakeHosts {
	return &fakeHosts{hosts: map[string]dockerhost.Host{}, clients: map[string]*dockerutil.Client{}, down: map[string]bool{}}
}

// add registers an engine under the host's id (fe.host() unless id differs).
func (f *fakeHosts) add(t *testing.T, id string, fe *fakeEngine) dockerhost.Host {
	t.Helper()
	h := fe.host()
	h.ID = id
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.hosts[id] = h
	f.clients[id] = fe.client(t)
	return h
}

func (f *fakeHosts) setDown(id string, down bool) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.down[id] = down
}

func (f *fakeHosts) Host(_ context.Context, id string) (dockerhost.Host, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	h, ok := f.hosts[id]
	if !ok {
		return dockerhost.Host{}, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound
	}
	return h, nil
}

func (f *fakeHosts) Client(_ context.Context, id string) (*dockerutil.Client, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	if f.down[id] {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused")
	}
	c, ok := f.clients[id]
	if !ok {
		return nil, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound
	}
	return c, nil
}

// waitFor polls cond every few milliseconds until it holds or the timeout passes.
func waitUntil(t *testing.T, what string, timeout time.Duration, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		if cond() {
			return
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	t.Fatalf("timed out after %s waiting for %s", timeout, what)
}

// assertSameJSON compares two JSON documents by value, so field order does not matter.
func assertSameJSON(t *testing.T, got any, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	gotRaw, err := json.Marshal(got)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("marshal: %v", err)
	}
	var g, w any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(gotRaw, &g); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("unmarshal got: %v", err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(want), &w); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("golden is not valid JSON: %v", err)
	}
	gotCanon, _ := json.MarshalIndent(g, "", "  ")
	wantCanon, _ := json.MarshalIndent(w, "", "  ")
	if string(gotCanon) != string(wantCanon) {
		t.Fatalf("JSON differs.\ngot:\n%s\nwant:\n%s", gotCanon, wantCanon)
	}
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/engineapi.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// engine wraps the Engine calls the stacks service makes on one host. Plain
// calls keep the client's 30 s timeout; streaming calls (logs follow, image
// pull, save and load) use a copy of the client with Timeout 0 and are bounded
// by their context instead. Every non-2xx answer is a *dockerhost.StatusError,
// so callers classify by dockerhost.StatusOf.
type engine struct{ c *dockerutil.Client }

func newEngine(c *dockerutil.Client) engine { return engine{c: c} }

// streamClient is the client without a total timeout.
func (e engine) streamClient() *http.Client {
	hc := *e.c.HTTPClient()
	hc.Timeout = 0
	return &hc
}

// statusError turns a non-2xx response into a *dockerhost.StatusError carrying
// the Engine's message (one printable line).
func statusError(resp *http.Response) error {
	message := dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(dockerutil.EngineErrorMessage(dockerutil.ReadErrorBody(resp.Body)), 512)
	return &dockerhost.StatusError{
		Status: resp.StatusCode,
		Err:    fmt.Errorf("Docker API returned %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, message),
	}
}

// request sends one Engine request, with an optional body and content type,
// and returns the open response of a 2xx answer; the caller closes it.
func (e engine) request(ctx context.Context, method, path string, body io.Reader, contentType string, stream bool) (*http.Response, error) {
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, dockerutil.Endpoint(path), body)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("create Docker request: %w", err)
	}
	if contentType != "" {
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", contentType)
	}
	client := e.c.HTTPClient()
	if stream {
		client = e.streamClient()
	}
	resp, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("Docker request: %w", err)
	}
	if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		return nil, statusError(resp)
	}
	return resp, nil
}

// json is DoJSON with a *dockerhost.StatusError for a non-2xx answer.
func (e engine) json(ctx context.Context, method, path string, in, out any) error {
	status, err := e.c.DoJSON(ctx, method, path, in, out)
	if err != nil && status != 0 && (status < 200 || status >= 300) {
		return &dockerhost.StatusError{Status: status, Err: err}
	}
	return err
}

func isNotFound(err error) bool { return dockerhost.StatusOf(err) == http.StatusNotFound }

// engineVersion is the part of GET /version the stacks service reads.
type engineVersion struct {
	Version    string `json:"Version"`
	APIVersion string `json:"ApiVersion"`
	OS         string `json:"Os"`
	Arch       string `json:"Arch"`
}

// version reads GET /version.
func (e engine) version(ctx context.Context) (engineVersion, error) {
	var v engineVersion
	err := e.json(ctx, http.MethodGet, "version", nil, &v)
	return v, err
}

// apiMinor reads the minor number of an Engine API version such as "1.45".
func apiMinor(version string) (int, bool) {
	major, minor, found := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(version), ".")
	if !found || major != "1" {
		return 0, false
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(minor)
	return n, err == nil
}

// supportsStacks reports an Engine API of 1.41 (Docker 20.10) or newer.
func supportsStacks(apiVersion string) bool {
	minor, ok := apiMinor(apiVersion)
	return ok && minor >= MinAPIMinor
}

// containerState is the part of a container's inspect document the stacks
// service reads.
type containerState struct {
	ID        string
	Name      string
	Image     string // Config.Image
	Labels    map[string]string
	Status    string // created, running, paused, restarting, removing, exited, dead
	Running   bool
	ExitCode  int
	OOMKilled bool
	Error     string // State.Error
}

// inspectContainer reads GET /containers/<ref>/json. A missing container is a
// 404 *dockerhost.StatusError.
func (e engine) inspectContainer(ctx context.Context, ref string) (containerState, error) {
	var raw struct {
		ID     string `json:"Id"`
		Name   string `json:"Name"`
		Config struct {
			Image  string            `json:"Image"`
			Labels map[string]string `json:"Labels"`
		} `json:"Config"`
		State struct {
			Status    string `json:"Status"`
			Running   bool   `json:"Running"`
			ExitCode  int    `json:"ExitCode"`
			OOMKilled bool   `json:"OOMKilled"`
			Error     string `json:"Error"`
		} `json:"State"`
	}
	if err := e.json(ctx, http.MethodGet, "containers/"+url.PathEscape(ref)+"/json", nil, &raw); err != nil {
		return containerState{}, err
	}
	return containerState{
		ID:        raw.ID,
		Name:      strings.TrimPrefix(raw.Name, "/"),
		Image:     raw.Config.Image,
		Labels:    raw.Config.Labels,
		Status:    raw.State.Status,
		Running:   raw.State.Running,
		ExitCode:  raw.State.ExitCode,
		OOMKilled: raw.State.OOMKilled,
		Error:     raw.State.Error,
	}, nil
}

// createContainer sends POST /containers/create?name=<name> and returns the id.
func (e engine) createContainer(ctx context.Context, name string, spec containerSpec) (string, error) {
	var out struct {
		ID string `json:"Id"`
	}
	if err := e.json(ctx, http.MethodPost, "containers/create?name="+url.QueryEscape(name), spec, &out); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return out.ID, nil
}

// startContainer starts a container; the Engine's 304 (already started) is success.
func (e engine) startContainer(ctx context.Context, ref string) error {
	return dockerhost.ContainerAction(ctx, e.c, ref, "start")
}

// killContainer sends SIGKILL; the Engine's 409 (not running) is not an error here.
func (e engine) killContainer(ctx context.Context, ref string) error {
	err := dockerhost.ContainerAction(ctx, e.c, ref, "kill")
	if dockerhost.StatusOf(err) == http.StatusConflict || isNotFound(err) {
		return nil
	}
	return err
}

// removeContainer force-removes a container together with its anonymous
// volumes; a container that is already gone is success.
func (e engine) removeContainer(ctx context.Context, ref string) error {
	err := dockerhost.RemoveContainer(ctx, e.c, ref, true)
	if isNotFound(err) {
		return nil
	}
	return err
}

// followLogs streams the logs of a non-TTY container (stdout and stderr, no
// timestamps) into the writers until the stream ends, which for a running
// container is when it exits. since is a unix time in seconds (0 = from the
// start). Either writer may be nil.
func (e engine) followLogs(ctx context.Context, ref string, since int64, stdout, stderr io.Writer) error {
	path := "containers/" + url.PathEscape(ref) + "/logs?follow=true&stdout=true&stderr=true"
	if since > 0 {
		path += "&since=" + strconv.FormatInt(since, 10)
	}
	resp, err := e.request(ctx, http.MethodGet, path, nil, "", true)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	return dockerhost.DemuxStreams(resp.Body, stdout, stderr)
}

// imageInfo is the part of an image's inspect document the stacks service reads.
type imageInfo struct {
	ID   string `json:"Id"`
	OS   string `json:"Os"`
	Arch string `json:"Architecture"`
}

// inspectImage reads GET /images/<ref>/json; found is false for a 404.
func (e engine) inspectImage(ctx context.Context, ref string) (info imageInfo, found bool, err error) {
	err = e.json(ctx, http.MethodGet, "images/"+url.PathEscape(ref)+"/json", nil, &info)
	if isNotFound(err) {
		return imageInfo{}, false, nil
	}
	return info, err == nil, err
}

// jsonMessage is one line of the JSON message streams of image pull and load.
type jsonMessage struct {
	ID       string `json:"id"`
	Status   string `json:"status"`
	Stream   string `json:"stream"`
	Progress struct {
		Current int64 `json:"current"`
		Total   int64 `json:"total"`
	} `json:"progressDetail"`
	Error       string `json:"error"`
	ErrorDetail struct {
		Message string `json:"message"`
	} `json:"errorDetail"`
}

// readJSONMessages decodes a JSON message stream line by line and hands every
// message to fn (which may be nil). An error event ends the read with a
// *dockerutil.JSONMessageError. Lines that are not JSON are skipped.
func readJSONMessages(r io.Reader, fn func(jsonMessage)) error {
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(r)
	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), dockerutil.MaxJSONMessageLine)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := bytes.TrimSpace(scanner.Bytes())
		if len(line) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		var msg jsonMessage
		if json.Unmarshal(line, &msg) != nil {
			continue
		}
		if text := strings.TrimSpace(msg.ErrorDetail.Message); text != "" {
			return &dockerutil.JSONMessageError{Message: text}
		}
		if text := strings.TrimSpace(msg.Error); text != "" {
			return &dockerutil.JSONMessageError{Message: text}
		}
		if fn != nil {
			fn(msg)
		}
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read Docker message stream: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// pullImage pulls fromImage:tag (tag may be a digest) and hands every message
// of the pull stream to fn.
func (e engine) pullImage(ctx context.Context, fromImage, tag string, fn func(jsonMessage)) error {
	path := "images/create?fromImage=" + url.QueryEscape(fromImage) + "&tag=" + url.QueryEscape(tag)
	resp, err := e.request(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, nil, "", true)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	return readJSONMessages(resp.Body, fn)
}

// saveImage opens GET /images/<ref>/get, the image as a tar stream.
func (e engine) saveImage(ctx context.Context, ref string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
	resp, err := e.request(ctx, http.MethodGet, "images/"+url.PathEscape(ref)+"/get", nil, "", true)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return resp.Body, nil
}

// loadImage sends a tar stream to POST /images/load and returns what the
// Engine reported as loaded ("sha256:..." image id or a reference), "" when it
// said nothing recognizable.
func (e engine) loadImage(ctx context.Context, tarStream io.Reader) (string, error) {
	resp, err := e.request(ctx, http.MethodPost, "images/load?quiet=1", tarStream, "application/x-tar", true)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	loaded := ""
	err = readJSONMessages(resp.Body, func(m jsonMessage) {
		const idPrefix, refPrefix = "Loaded image ID: ", "Loaded image: "
		text := strings.TrimSpace(m.Stream)
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(text, idPrefix):
			loaded = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(text, idPrefix))
		case strings.HasPrefix(text, refPrefix) && loaded == "":
			loaded = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(text, refPrefix))
		}
	})
	return loaded, err
}

// tagImage sends POST /images/<ref>/tag?repo=...&tag=....
func (e engine) tagImage(ctx context.Context, ref, repo, tag string) error {
	path := "images/" + url.PathEscape(ref) + "/tag?repo=" + url.QueryEscape(repo) + "&tag=" + url.QueryEscape(tag)
	return e.json(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, nil, nil)
}

// projectVolumes lists the volumes that carry the compose project label.
func (e engine) projectVolumes(ctx context.Context, project string) ([]ProjectVolume, error) {
	filters, _ := json.Marshal(map[string][]string{"label": {"com.docker.compose.project=" + project}})
	var out struct {
		Volumes []struct {
			Name   string `json:"Name"`
			Driver string `json:"Driver"`
		} `json:"Volumes"`
	}
	if err := e.json(ctx, http.MethodGet, "volumes?filters="+url.QueryEscape(string(filters)), nil, &out); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	volumes := make([]ProjectVolume, 0, len(out.Volumes))
	for _, v := range out.Volumes {
		volumes = append(volumes, ProjectVolume{Name: v.Name, Driver: v.Driver, Size: -1})
	}
	return volumes, nil
}

// volumeSizes reads GET /system/df?type=volume (API 1.42 and newer): the size
// in bytes of every volume the Engine measured, by name. A volume the Engine
// could not measure (it reports -1) is left out.
func (e engine) volumeSizes(ctx context.Context) (map[string]int64, error) {
	var out struct {
		Volumes []struct {
			Name      string `json:"Name"`
			UsageData *struct {
				Size int64 `json:"Size"`
			} `json:"UsageData"`
		} `json:"Volumes"`
	}
	if err := e.json(ctx, http.MethodGet, "system/df?type=volume", nil, &out); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	sizes := make(map[string]int64, len(out.Volumes))
	for _, v := range out.Volumes {
		if v.UsageData != nil && v.UsageData.Size >= 0 {
			sizes[v.Name] = v.UsageData.Size
		}
	}
	return sizes, nil
}

// engineMessage is the one-line text of an Engine failure for an operation's
// error field. Engine answers keep their message; anything else its error text.
func engineMessage(err error) string {
	var jsonErr *dockerutil.JSONMessageError
	if errors.As(err, &jsonErr) {
		return dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(jsonErr.Message, 300)
	}
	return dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(err.Error(), 300)
}
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"fmt"
	"path"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
)

// containerSpec is the JSON body of POST /containers/create for the helper
// containers (runner, lister, IO). Field names are the Engine's.
type containerSpec struct {
	Image           string            `json:"Image"`
	Entrypoint      []string          `json:"Entrypoint"`
	Cmd             []string          `json:"Cmd,omitempty"`
	WorkingDir      string            `json:"WorkingDir,omitempty"`
	Env             []string          `json:"Env,omitempty"`
	Labels          map[string]string `json:"Labels"`
	Tty             bool              `json:"Tty"`
	NetworkDisabled bool              `json:"NetworkDisabled"`
	HostConfig      hostConfig        `json:"HostConfig"`
}

type hostConfig struct {
	Binds          []string          `json:"Binds"`
	NetworkMode    string            `json:"NetworkMode"`
	CapDrop        []string          `json:"CapDrop"`
	CapAdd         []string          `json:"CapAdd,omitempty"`
	ReadonlyRootfs bool              `json:"ReadonlyRootfs"`
	Tmpfs          map[string]string `json:"Tmpfs"`
	SecurityOpt    []string          `json:"SecurityOpt"`
	LogConfig      logConfig         `json:"LogConfig"`
	RestartPolicy  restartPolicy     `json:"RestartPolicy"`
	AutoRemove     bool              `json:"AutoRemove"`
}

type logConfig struct {
	Type   string            `json:"Type"`
	Config map[string]string `json:"Config"`
}

type restartPolicy struct {
	Name string `json:"Name"`
}

// Container names of the helpers.
const (
	runnerNamePrefix = "aurago-dm-op-"
	listerNamePrefix = "aurago-dm-ls-"
	socketInRunner   = "/var/run/docker.sock"
)

func runnerName(operationID string) string { return runnerNamePrefix + operationID }

// hardenedHostConfig is the host configuration all helpers share: no network,
// every capability dropped, a read-only root file system with a small tmpfs,
// no privilege escalation, a bounded json-file log and no restart.
func hardenedHostConfig(binds []string) hostConfig {
	return hostConfig{
		Binds:          binds,
		NetworkMode:    "none",
		CapDrop:        []string{"ALL"},
		ReadonlyRootfs: true,
		Tmpfs:          map[string]string{"/tmp": "rw,nosuid,nodev,size=64m"},
		SecurityOpt:    []string{"no-new-privileges:true"},
		LogConfig:      logConfig{Type: "json-file", Config: map[string]string{"max-size": "8m", "max-file": "1"}},
		RestartPolicy:  restartPolicy{Name: "no"},
	}
}

// stackDir is <stacks dir>/<name> as the host sees it (and the helpers, which
// bind the stacks directory at the same path).
func stackDir(h dockerhost.Host, name string) string { return path.Join(h.StacksDir, name) }

// runnerSpec is the runner container of one operation: it runs the kind's
// script with `sh -ec <script> aurago-docker-manager <args>`. composeFile is the
// file name inside the stack folder (unused by delete, which works by project
// name). Delete runs in the stacks directory, so a broken compose file in the
// folder it removes cannot stop the compose down, and it alone gets the
// capabilities to remove files that belong to other users.
func runnerSpec(image string, h dockerhost.Host, op Operation, composeFile string) (containerSpec, error) {
	script, ok := runnerScript(op.Kind, op.Options.Volumes)
	if !ok {
		return containerSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("operation kind %q has no runner script", op.Kind)
	}
	dir := stackDir(h, op.Stack)
	cmd := []string{script, "aurago-docker-manager"}
	workingDir := dir
	if op.Kind == KindDelete {
		workingDir = h.StacksDir
	} else {
		cmd = append(cmd, "-p", op.Stack, "-f", path.Join(dir, composeFile), "--progress", "json")
	}
	cfg := hardenedHostConfig([]string{h.StacksDir + ":" + h.StacksDir, h.HostSocketPath + ":" + socketInRunner})
	if op.Kind == KindDelete {
		cfg.CapAdd = []string{"DAC_OVERRIDE", "FOWNER"}
	}
	return containerSpec{
		Image:      image,
		Entrypoint: []string{"sh", "-ec"},
		Cmd:        cmd,
		WorkingDir: workingDir,
		Env:        []string{"HOME=/tmp", "DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/.docker", "STACK_DIR=" + dir, "PROJECT=" + op.Stack},
		Labels: map[string]string{
			LabelRole:      RoleRunner,
			LabelOperation: op.ID,
			LabelStack:     op.Stack,
			LabelStacksDir: h.StacksDir,
		},
		NetworkDisabled: true,
		HostConfig:      cfg,
	}, nil
}

// listerSpec is the short-lived container that lists the compose files and
// .env files one level below the stacks directory. The directory is bound
// read-only and the Docker socket is not bound at all.
func listerSpec(image string, h dockerhost.Host) containerSpec {
	cmd := []string{h.StacksDir, "-mindepth", "2", "-maxdepth", "2", "-type", "f", "("}
	for i, name := range ComposeFileNames {
		if i > 0 {
			cmd = append(cmd, "-o")
		}
		cmd = append(cmd, "-name", name)
	}
	cmd = append(cmd, "-o", "-name", EnvFileName, ")")
	return containerSpec{
		Image:           image,
		Entrypoint:      []string{"find"},
		Cmd:             cmd,
		Labels:          map[string]string{LabelRole: RoleLister, LabelStacksDir: h.StacksDir},
		NetworkDisabled: true,
		HostConfig:      hardenedHostConfig([]string{h.StacksDir + ":" + h.StacksDir + ":ro"}),
	}
}

// ioSpec is the parked IO container: created, never started. The Engine's
// archive API reads and writes files of a container's mounts without running
// it, which gives stack file access on every host type.
func ioSpec(image string, h dockerhost.Host) containerSpec {
	return containerSpec{
		Image:           image,
		Entrypoint:      []string{"true"},
		Labels:          map[string]string{LabelRole: RoleIO, LabelStacksDir: h.StacksDir},
		NetworkDisabled: true,
		HostConfig:      hardenedHostConfig([]string{h.StacksDir + ":" + h.StacksDir}),
	}
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/scripts.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

// Runner scripts, one per operation kind. They run as
//
//	sh -ec <script> aurago-docker-manager "$@"
//
// where "$@" is `-p <name> -f <dir>/<name>/<compose file> --progress json`, and
// with STACK_DIR and PROJECT in the environment. No user-controlled value is
// ever part of a script's text: stack names, paths and compose file names reach
// it only through the positional arguments or the environment.
const (
	scriptConfig      = `docker compose "$@" config --quiet`
	scriptUp          = `docker compose "$@" config --quiet && docker compose "$@" up -d --remove-orphans`
	scriptDown        = `docker compose "$@" down --remove-orphans`
	scriptDownVolumes = `docker compose "$@" down --remove-orphans --volumes`
	scriptStop        = `docker compose "$@" stop`
	scriptRestart     = `docker compose "$@" restart`
	scriptPull        = `docker compose "$@" pull`
	scriptUpdate      = `docker compose "$@" pull && docker compose "$@" up -d --remove-orphans`
	scriptDelete      = `docker compose -p "$PROJECT" down --remove-orphans && rm -rf -- "$STACK_DIR"`
	scriptDeleteVols  = `docker compose -p "$PROJECT" down --remove-orphans --volumes && rm -rf -- "$STACK_DIR"`
)

// runnerScript returns the script of an operation kind; volumes selects the
// `--volumes` variant of down and delete. ok is false for kinds without a
// runner (prepare) and for unknown kinds.
func runnerScript(kind string, volumes bool) (script string, ok bool) {
	switch kind {
	case KindConfig:
		return scriptConfig, true
	case KindUp:
		return scriptUp, true
	case KindDown:
		if volumes {
			return scriptDownVolumes, true
		}
		return scriptDown, true
	case KindStop:
		return scriptStop, true
	case KindRestart:
		return scriptRestart, true
	case KindPull:
		return scriptPull, true
	case KindUpdate:
		return scriptUpdate, true
	case KindDelete:
		if volumes {
			return scriptDeleteVols, true
		}
		return scriptDelete, true
	}
	return "", false
}
```

### Task A4: Operation journal and compose progress parsing

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/journal.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/progress.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/journal_test.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/progress_test.go`

- `journal.go`: table `docker_operations` (exactly the contract's schema, created with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), `insert`, `save`, `get`, `list` (newest first, filters, limit 20/100, **without the output column**), `active` (rows to adopt after a restart) and `prune` (keeps the newest 50 finished rows of a host and stack, never touches an active row). Times are stored in a fixed-width UTC layout so that the text column sorts in time order.
- `progress.go`: `lineWriter` (splits the demultiplexed stream into lines across writes), `parseProgressLine` (a JSON object becomes a `Progress`; fields mapped by name: `id`, `parent_id` or `parent`, `status`, `text`, `current`, `total`, `percent`; numbers may be numeric strings; unknown fields ignored — **the live test of Task A11 confirms the names against Compose 5.6.1**), `progressText` (`<id> <status> <text>`), `isByteTick` (an item with a byte count updates the bar but gets no output line), `errorScan` (finds the line that explains a failure: the last plain line naming an error, else a compose error item, else the last plain line; ANSI stripped) and `errorLineOf` ("yaml: line 12: …" gives 12).

```go
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.State != StateFailed || got.RunnerID != "runner-id" || got.ExitCode == nil || *got.ExitCode != 17 ||
		got.Code != "runner_failed" || got.Error != "yaml: line 12: boom" || got.ErrorLine != 12 ||
		got.Warning != "db is unhealthy" || got.Output != "line one\nline two\n" ||
		len(got.Ports) != 1 || got.Ports[0].PublicPort != 8080 {
		t.Fatalf("saved row = %+v", got)
	}
	if !got.CreatedAt.Equal(created) || got.StartedAt == nil || !got.StartedAt.Equal(started) || got.FinishedAt == nil || !got.FinishedAt.Equal(finished) {
		t.Fatalf("times = %v %v %v", got.CreatedAt, got.StartedAt, got.FinishedAt)
	}
	if !got.Done() {
		t.Fatal("a failed operation must report Done")
	}

	if _, err := j.get(ctx, "op_missing"); CodeOf(err) != CodeOperationNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("get of an unknown id = %v, want %s", err, CodeOperationNotFound)
	}
}

func TestJournalListFiltersAndOrdersNewestFirst(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	j := newTestJournal(t)
	base := time.Date(2026, 10, 27, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	rows := []Operation{
		testOp("op_01", "h_1", "web", KindUp, StateSucceeded, base),
		testOp("op_02", "h_1", "web", KindDown, StateRunning, base.Add(time.Second)),
		testOp("op_03", "h_1", "db", KindUp, StateQueued, base.Add(2*time.Second)),
		testOp("op_04", "h_2", "web", KindUp, StateHealthWait, base.Add(3*time.Second)),
		testOp("op_05", "h_1", "", KindPrepare, StateFailed, base.Add(4*time.Second)),
	}
	for _, op := range rows {
		op.Output = "must not be listed"
		if err := j.insert(ctx, op); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	ids := func(f OperationFilter) string {
		ops, err := j.list(ctx, f)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		s := ""
		for _, op := range ops {
			if op.Output != "" {
				t.Fatalf("list returned the output of %s", op.ID)
			}
			s += op.ID[3:] + " "
		}
		return s
	}
	if got := ids(OperationFilter{}); got != "05 04 03 02 01 " {
		t.Fatalf("all = %q, want newest first", got)
	}
	if got := ids(OperationFilter{HostID: "h_1", Stack: "web"}); got != "02 01 " {
		t.Fatalf("host+stack = %q", got)
	}
	if got := ids(OperationFilter{Active: true}); got != "04 03 02 " {
		t.Fatalf("active = %q, want queued, running and health_wait only", got)
	}
	if got := ids(OperationFilter{Limit: 2}); got != "05 04 " {
		t.Fatalf("limit 2 = %q", got)
	}
	active, err := j.active(ctx)
	if err != nil || len(active) != 3 || active[0].ID != "op_02" || active[0].Output != "must not be listed" {
		t.Fatalf("active() = (%v, %v), want three rows oldest first, with their output", active, err)
	}
}

func TestJournalPruneKeepsTheNewest50AndNeverActiveRows(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	j := newTestJournal(t)
	base := time.Date(2026, 10, 27, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	for i := 0; i < 60; i++ {
		state := StateSucceeded
		if i == 0 {
			state = StateRunning // the oldest row is still active and must survive
		}
		if err := j.insert(ctx, testOp(fmt.Sprintf("op_%02d", i), "h_1", "web", KindUp, state, base.Add(time.Duration(i)*time.Second))); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if err := j.insert(ctx, testOp("op_other", "h_1", "db", KindUp, StateSucceeded, base)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := j.prune(ctx, "h_1", "web", journalKeep); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var n int
	if err := j.db.QueryRow("SELECT count(*) FROM docker_operations WHERE host_id = 'h_1' AND stack = 'web'").Scan(&n); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if n != 51 { // the newest 50 plus the old active row
		t.Fatalf("rows after prune = %d, want 51", n)
	}
	if _, err := j.get(ctx, "op_00"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the active row was pruned: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := j.get(ctx, "op_09"); CodeOf(err) != CodeOperationNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("op_09 is older than the newest 50 and must be gone, got %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := j.get(ctx, "op_10"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("op_10 is the 50th newest and must stay: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := j.get(ctx, "op_other"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("another stack's row must be untouched: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestJournalSchemaIsIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
	db := openTestDB(t)
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if _, err := newJournal(db); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("newJournal #%d: %v", i+1, err)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

func TestParseProgressLine(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		line string
		want Progress
		ok   bool
	}{
		{"compose item", `{"id":"Container web-1","status":"Working","text":"Starting"}`,
			Progress{ID: "Container web-1", Status: "Working", Text: "Starting"}, true},
		{"parent_id is the parent", `{"id":"layer1","parent_id":"Image redis","status":"Working","text":"Downloading","current":512,"total":2048,"percent":25}`,
			Progress{ID: "layer1", Parent: "Image redis", Status: "Working", Text: "Downloading", Current: 512, Total: 2048, Percent: 25}, true},
		{"parent also works", `{"id":"layer1","parent":"Image redis","status":"Done"}`,
			Progress{ID: "layer1", Parent: "Image redis", Status: "Done"}, true},
		{"numbers as strings and a fractional percent", `{"id":"x","current":"10","total":"40","percent":"25.5"}`,
			Progress{ID: "x", Current: 10, Total: 40, Percent: 25.5}, true},
		{"percent is derived from current and total", `{"id":"x","current":1,"total":3}`,
			Progress{ID: "x", Current: 1, Total: 3, Percent: 33.3}, true},
		{"unknown fields and wrong types are ignored", `{"id":"x","dry-run":true,"tail":false,"details":{"a":1},"status":7}`,
			Progress{ID: "x"}, true},
		{"leading blanks", `   {"id":"x","text":"t"}`, Progress{ID: "x", Text: "t"}, true},
		{"plain text", `Network web_default  Created`, Progress{}, false},
		{"broken json", `{"id":"x","status":`, Progress{}, false},
		{"json that is not an object", `["a"]`, Progress{}, false},
		{"an object without id, status and text", `{"dry-run":true}`, Progress{}, false},
		{"empty", ``, Progress{}, false},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got, ok := parseProgressLine(c.line)
		if ok != c.ok || got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: parseProgressLine = (%+v, %v), want (%+v, %v)", c.name, got, ok, c.want, c.ok)
		}
	}
}

func TestProgressTextAndByteTicks(t *testing.T) {
	if got := progressText(Progress{ID: "Container web-1", Status: "Done", Text: "Started"}); got != "Container web-1 Done Started" {
		t.Fatalf("progressText = %q", got)
	}
	if got := progressText(Progress{ID: "x", Text: "Pulled"}); got != "x Pulled" {
		t.Fatalf("progressText without a status = %q", got)
	}
	if !isByteTick(Progress{Current: 1, Total: 10}) || !isByteTick(Progress{Current: 10, Total: 10}) || isByteTick(Progress{ID: "x", Status: "Done"}) {
		t.Fatal("isByteTick must be true exactly for items that carry a byte count")
	}

func TestLineWriterSplitsLinesAcrossWrites(t *testing.T) {
	var lines []string
	w := newLineWriter(func(l string) { lines = append(lines, l) })
	_, _ = w.Write([]byte("first\nsec"))
	_, _ = w.Write([]byte("ond\r\n\n   \nthird"))
	if strings.Join(lines, "|") != "first|second" {
		t.Fatalf("lines before Flush = %q, want the two complete ones (blank lines skipped)", lines)
	}
	w.Flush()
	if strings.Join(lines, "|") != "first|second|third" {
		t.Fatalf("lines after Flush = %q", lines)
	}
	w.Flush()
	if len(lines) != 3 {
		t.Fatal("a second Flush must add nothing")
	}

	long := strings.Repeat("x", maxLineBytes+10)
	lines = nil
	w = newLineWriter(func(l string) { lines = append(lines, l) })
	_, _ = w.Write([]byte(long))
	if len(lines) != 1 || len(lines[0]) != maxLineBytes+10 {
		t.Fatalf("an endless line must be handed on once it passes %d bytes, got %d lines", maxLineBytes, len(lines))
	}
}

func TestErrorScanPicksTheLineThatExplainsTheFailure(t *testing.T) {
	scan := func(lines ...string) string {
		var s errorScan
		for _, l := range lines {
			if p, ok := parseProgressLine(l); ok {
				s.observe(l, &p)
			} else {
				s.observe(l, nil)
			}
		}
		return s.message()
	}
	if got := scan(`{"id":"Container web-1","status":"Working","text":"Starting"}`, "yaml: line 12: did not find expected key"); got != "yaml: line 12: did not find expected key" {
		t.Fatalf("a plain error line = %q", got)
	}
	if got := scan("Network x Created", "Error response from daemon: Ports are not available", "exit status 1"); got != "Error response from daemon: Ports are not available" {
		t.Fatalf("the last plain line naming an error must win over a later bare line, got %q", got)
	}
	if got := scan("first error: a", "second error: b"); got != "second error: b" {
		t.Fatalf("the last error line wins, got %q", got)
	}
	if got := scan(`{"id":"Container db-1","status":"Error","text":"Error response from daemon: no such image"}`); got != "Container db-1: Error response from daemon: no such image" {
		t.Fatalf("an error item = %q", got)
	}
	if got := scan(`{"id":"Container db-1","status":"Error","text":"Error"}`); got != "Container db-1 Error Error" {
		t.Fatalf("an error item without details = %q", got)
	}
	if got := scan("\x1b[31mError\x1b[0m: bad thing\x1b[0m"); got != "Error: bad thing" {
		t.Fatalf("ANSI must be stripped, got %q", got)
	}
	if got := scan("something happened"); got != "something happened" {
		t.Fatalf("with no error word the last plain line is the message, got %q", got)
	}
	if got := scan(); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("no output = %q", got)
	}
}

func TestErrorLineOf(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]int{
		"yaml: line 12: did not find expected key":           12,
		"yaml: line 3: mapping values are not allowed":       3,
		"validating /opt/stacks/web/compose.yaml: Line 7: x": 7,
		"no line number here":                                0,
		"timeline 5 is not a line":                           0,
		"line 0: nothing":                                    0,
		"line 99999999999999999999: overflow":                0,
	}
	for msg, want := range cases {
		if got := errorLineOf(msg); got != want {
			t.Errorf("errorLineOf(%q) = %d, want %d", msg, got, want)
		}
	}
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/journal.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

const journalSchema = `
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS docker_operations (
    id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    host_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    stack       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    kind        TEXT NOT NULL,
    options     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    state       TEXT NOT NULL,
    runner_id   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    exit_code   INTEGER,
    code        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    error       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    error_line  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    warning     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    output      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    ports       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    finished_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_docker_operations_stack ON docker_operations(host_id, stack, created_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_docker_operations_state ON docker_operations(state);
`

// journalKeep is how many operations of one (host, stack) the journal keeps.
const journalKeep = 50

// journalTime is a fixed-width UTC layout, so that the text column sorts in time order.
const journalTime = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z"

const (
	journalColumns     = "id, host_id, stack, kind, options, state, runner_id, exit_code, code, error, error_line, warning, ports, created_at, started_at, finished_at"
	journalListLimit   = 20
	journalListMaxRows = 100
	activeStates       = "('" + StateQueued + "','" + StateRunning + "','" + StateHealthWait + "')"
)

// journal is the table docker_operations in docker_manager.db.
type journal struct{ db *sql.DB }

func newJournal(db *sql.DB) (*journal, error) {
	if _, err := db.Exec(journalSchema); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("create docker operations schema: %w", err)
	}
	return &journal{db: db}, nil
}

func formatJournalTime(t time.Time) string { return t.UTC().Format(journalTime) }

func parseJournalTime(s string) time.Time {
	t, _ := time.Parse(journalTime, s)
	return t
}

func optionalTime(t *time.Time) string {
	if t == nil || t.IsZero() {
		return ""
	}
	return formatJournalTime(*t)
}

// insert stores a new operation.
func (j *journal) insert(ctx context.Context, op Operation) error {
	options, _ := json.Marshal(op.Options)
	ports, _ := json.Marshal(nonNilPorts(op.Ports))
	var exit any
	if op.ExitCode != nil {
		exit = *op.ExitCode
	}
	_, err := j.db.ExecContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO docker_operations
		(id, host_id, stack, kind, options, state, runner_id, exit_code, code, error, error_line, warning, output, ports, created_at, started_at, finished_at)
		VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`,
		op.ID, op.HostID, op.Stack, op.Kind, string(options), op.State, op.RunnerID, exit, op.Code, op.Error, op.ErrorLine,
		op.Warning, op.Output, string(ports), formatJournalTime(op.CreatedAt), optionalTime(op.StartedAt), optionalTime(op.FinishedAt))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("store docker operation: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// save writes every mutable column of an operation.
func (j *journal) save(ctx context.Context, op Operation) error {
	ports, _ := json.Marshal(nonNilPorts(op.Ports))
	var exit any
	if op.ExitCode != nil {
		exit = *op.ExitCode
	}
	_, err := j.db.ExecContext(ctx, `UPDATE docker_operations SET state = ?, runner_id = ?, exit_code = ?, code = ?, error = ?,
		error_line = ?, warning = ?, output = ?, ports = ?, started_at = ?, finished_at = ? WHERE id = ?`,
		op.State, op.RunnerID, exit, op.Code, op.Error, op.ErrorLine, op.Warning, op.Output, string(ports),
		optionalTime(op.StartedAt), optionalTime(op.FinishedAt), op.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("update docker operation: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

func nonNilPorts(p []PortLink) []PortLink {
	if p == nil {
		return []PortLink{}
	}
	return p
}

type journalScanner interface{ Scan(dest ...any) error }

// scanOperation reads the columns of journalColumns, plus the output when withOutput.
func scanOperation(row journalScanner, withOutput bool) (Operation, error) {
	var op Operation
	var options, ports, created, started, finished string
	var exit sql.NullInt64
	dest := []any{&op.ID, &op.HostID, &op.Stack, &op.Kind, &options, &op.State, &op.RunnerID, &exit, &op.Code, &op.Error,
		&op.ErrorLine, &op.Warning, &ports, &created, &started, &finished}
	if withOutput {
		dest = append(dest, &op.Output)
	}
	if err := row.Scan(dest...); err != nil {
		return Operation{}, err
	}
	_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(options), &op.Options)
	_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(ports), &op.Ports)
	if exit.Valid {
		code := int(exit.Int64)
		op.ExitCode = &code
	}
	op.CreatedAt = parseJournalTime(created)
	if started != "" {
		t := parseJournalTime(started)
		op.StartedAt = &t
	}
	if finished != "" {
		t := parseJournalTime(finished)
		op.FinishedAt = &t
	}
	return op, nil
}

// get returns one operation with its output, or a CodeOperationNotFound error.
func (j *journal) get(ctx context.Context, id string) (Operation, error) {
	op, err := scanOperation(j.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT "+journalColumns+", output FROM docker_operations WHERE id = ?", id), true)
	if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
		return Operation{}, newError(CodeOperationNotFound, "no operation %q", id)
	}
	return op, err
}

// list returns operations newest first, without their output (use get for it).
func (j *journal) list(ctx context.Context, f OperationFilter) ([]Operation, error) {
	query := "SELECT " + journalColumns + " FROM docker_operations WHERE 1=1"
	var args []any
	if f.HostID != "" {
		query += " AND host_id = ?"
		args = append(args, f.HostID)
	}
	if f.Stack != "" {
		query += " AND stack = ?"
		args = append(args, f.Stack)
	}
	if f.Active {
		query += " AND state IN " + activeStates
	}
	limit := f.Limit
	if limit <= 0 {
		limit = journalListLimit
	}
	if limit > journalListMaxRows {
		limit = journalListMaxRows
	}
	query += " ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?"
	args = append(args, limit)
	rows, err := j.db.QueryContext(ctx, query, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("list docker operations: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	ops := []Operation{}
	for rows.Next() {
		op, err := scanOperation(rows, false)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		ops = append(ops, op)
	}
	return ops, rows.Err()
}

// active returns every queued, running or health_wait operation with its
// output, oldest first. Open uses it to reattach after a restart.
func (j *journal) active(ctx context.Context) ([]Operation, error) {
	rows, err := j.db.QueryContext(ctx, "SELECT "+journalColumns+", output FROM docker_operations WHERE state IN "+activeStates+" ORDER BY created_at, id")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("list active docker operations: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var ops []Operation
	for rows.Next() {
		op, err := scanOperation(rows, true)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		ops = append(ops, op)
	}
	return ops, rows.Err()
}

// prune deletes the finished operations of one (host, stack) beyond the newest keep.
func (j *journal) prune(ctx context.Context, hostID, stack string, keep int) error {
	_, err := j.db.ExecContext(ctx, `DELETE FROM docker_operations WHERE host_id = ? AND stack = ? AND state NOT IN `+activeStates+`
		AND id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM docker_operations WHERE host_id = ? AND stack = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?)`,
		hostID, stack, hostID, stack, keep)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("prune docker operations: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/progress.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"math"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// maxLineBytes bounds one buffered line; a longer one is handed on in pieces.
const maxLineBytes = 64 << 10

// lineWriter splits what is written to it into lines and hands every complete
// line (without its line ending, empty lines skipped) to fn. Flush hands on a
// last line that had no line ending.
type lineWriter struct {
	buf []byte
	fn  func(line string)
}

func newLineWriter(fn func(line string)) *lineWriter { return &lineWriter{fn: fn} }

func (w *lineWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	w.buf = append(w.buf, p...)
	for {
		i := bytes.IndexByte(w.buf, '\n')
		if i < 0 {
			break
		}
		w.emit(string(w.buf[:i]))
		w.buf = w.buf[i+1:]
	}
	if len(w.buf) > maxLineBytes {
		w.emit(string(w.buf))
		w.buf = nil
	}
	return len(p), nil
}

// Flush hands on the unterminated rest.
func (w *lineWriter) Flush() {
	if len(w.buf) > 0 {
		w.emit(string(w.buf))
		w.buf = nil
	}
}

func (w *lineWriter) emit(line string) {
	line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r")
	if strings.TrimSpace(line) != "" {
		w.fn(line)
	}
}

// parseProgressLine reads one line of `docker compose --progress json`: a JSON
// object with the fields id, parent_id (also parent), status, text, current,
// total and percent. Fields are mapped by name, unknown ones are ignored, and a
// number may arrive as a JSON number or a numeric string. A line that is not a
// JSON object, or an object with none of id, status and text, is not progress.
func parseProgressLine(line string) (Progress, bool) {
	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
	if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "{") {
		return Progress{}, false
	}
	var raw map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(trimmed), &raw); err != nil {
		return Progress{}, false
	}
	p := Progress{
		ID:      jsonStringField(raw, "id"),
		Parent:  jsonStringField(raw, "parent_id", "parent", "parentId"),
		Status:  jsonStringField(raw, "status"),
		Text:    jsonStringField(raw, "text"),
		Current: int64(jsonNumberField(raw, "current")),
		Total:   int64(jsonNumberField(raw, "total")),
		Percent: jsonNumberField(raw, "percent"),
	}
	if p.ID == "" && p.Status == "" && p.Text == "" {
		return Progress{}, false
	}
	if p.Percent == 0 && p.Total > 0 && p.Current > 0 {
		p.Percent = math.Round(float64(p.Current)*1000/float64(p.Total)) / 10
	}
	return p, true
}

func jsonStringField(raw map[string]any, names ...string) string {
	for _, name := range names {
		if v, ok := raw[name].(string); ok && v != "" {
			return v
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func jsonNumberField(raw map[string]any, name string) float64 {
	switch v := raw[name].(type) {
	case float64:
		return v
	case string:
		f, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(v), 64)
		return f
	}
	return 0
}

// progressText renders a progress item as a readable output line: "<id>
// <status> <text>" with the empty parts left out.
func progressText(p Progress) string {
	parts := make([]string, 0, 3)
	for _, part := range []string{p.ID, p.Status, p.Text} {
		if part != "" {
			parts = append(parts, part)
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
}

// isByteTick reports an item that carries a byte count of a download or an
// extraction. It updates the progress bar but is not worth a line of output;
// the items before and after it ("Pulling fs layer", "Pull complete") are.
func isByteTick(p Progress) bool { return p.Total > 0 }

var (
	reANSI       = regexp.MustCompile("\x1b\\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]")
	reErrorWord  = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)(\berror\b|\bfailed\b|\bdenied\b|\binvalid\b|\bcannot\b|\bunable\b|\brefused\b|not found|no such|required variable|\byaml:)`)
	reLineNumber = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\bline (\d+)\b`)
)

// stripANSI removes terminal escape sequences.
func stripANSI(s string) string { return reANSI.ReplaceAllString(s, "") }

// errorScan watches the lines of an operation for the one that explains a
// failure. Plain lines win over progress items, a plain line that names an
// error wins over the last plain line, and the last such line wins over earlier
// ones, because the compose CLI prints its final error last.
type errorScan struct {
	lastPlain   string
	lastErrWord string
	progress    string
}

// observe takes one line of output; p is its parsed progress item, if it is one.
func (e *errorScan) observe(line string, p *Progress) {
	line = strings.TrimSpace(stripANSI(line))
	if line == "" {
		return
	}
	if p != nil {
		if strings.EqualFold(p.Status, "error") && e.progress == "" {
			e.progress = progressErrorText(*p)
		}
		return
	}
	e.lastPlain = line
	if reErrorWord.MatchString(line) {
		e.lastErrWord = line
	}
}

// progressErrorText is the message of a compose error item: its text when it
// says more than "Error", else the readable line.
func progressErrorText(p Progress) string {
	if p.Text != "" && !strings.EqualFold(p.Text, "error") {
		if p.ID != "" {
			return p.ID + ": " + p.Text
		}
		return p.Text
	}
	return progressText(p)
}

// message is the one-line explanation of the failure, "" when nothing was seen.
func (e *errorScan) message() string {
	for _, candidate := range []string{e.lastErrWord, e.progress, e.lastPlain} {
		if candidate != "" {
			return dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(candidate, 300)
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// errorLineOf reads the compose file line a compose error names ("yaml: line
// 12: ...", "line 12:"), 0 when it names none.
func errorLineOf(message string) int {
	m := reLineNumber.FindStringSubmatch(message)
	if m == nil {
		return 0
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(m[1])
	if err != nil || n < 1 || n > 1_000_000 {
		return 0
	}
	return n
}
```

### Task A5: Service core: options, `Open`/`Close`, live operation runs, event fan-out, `Subscribe`

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/oprun.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/service.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/service_query.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/service_test.go`

- `service.go`: `Hosts`, `Options` (defaults: health wait 120 s, poll 2 s, maximum duration 60 min, list cache 30 s, local host `local`), the `Service` struct with all state the later tasks use (active runs and stack locks, folder-scan cache, ready-host cache, per-host and per-stack mutexes, sweep and parked-operation bookkeeping), `Open`/`Close`, `target` (host plus Engine client). `Open` only creates the journal table here; Task A9 adds the adoption of unfinished rows.
- `oprun.go`: `opRun` is the live state of one operation: the row it mirrors, the output tail (last 64 KiB, cut at a character boundary), the sequence-numbered event stream and its subscribers. `composeLine` turns a raw runner line into a `progress` event plus an output line; `finish` records the outcome, publishes `done`, ends every subscriber and frees the stack **in one step under the service lock, so whoever sees the operation done can start the next one**. A subscriber whose 256-event buffer is full is dropped and reconnects for a fresh snapshot. The row is rewritten at every state change and at most every 2 s for output.
- `service_query.go`: `Operation`, `Operations` (no output) and `Subscribe` (snapshot plus channel; an already closed channel for a finished operation).

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// fakeClock is a manually advanced clock for Options.Now.
type fakeClock struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	t  time.Time
}

func newFakeClock() *fakeClock {
	return &fakeClock{t: time.Date(2026, 10, 27, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)}
}

func (c *fakeClock) Now() time.Time {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return c.t
}

func (c *fakeClock) Advance(d time.Duration) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	c.t = c.t.Add(d)
}

// newTestService opens a service on a fresh database with short timings. tune
// may change the options.
func newTestService(t *testing.T, hosts Hosts, tune func(*Options)) *Service {
	t.Helper()
	opts := Options{
		Logger:       slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil)),
		HealthWait:   400 * time.Millisecond,
		HealthPoll:   10 * time.Millisecond,
		MaxDuration:  time.Minute,
		ListCacheTTL: time.Minute,
	}
	if tune != nil {
		tune(&opts)
	}
	s, err := Open(openTestDB(t), hosts, opts)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(s.Close)
	return s
}

// registerRun stores an operation row and registers its live run, as Start does.
func registerRun(t *testing.T, s *Service, op Operation) *opRun {
	t.Helper()
	if op.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
		op.CreatedAt = s.opts.Now().UTC()
	}
	if op.State == "" {
		op.State = StateQueued
	}
	if err := s.journal.insert(context.Background(), op); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	run := newOpRun(s, op)
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.runs[op.ID] = run
	s.locks[lockKey{op.HostID, op.Stack}] = op.ID
	s.mu.Unlock()
	return run
}

func drainEvents(ch <-chan Event) []Event {
	var events []Event
	for ev := range ch {
		events = append(events, ev)
	}
	return events
}

func TestSubscribeDeliversSnapshotThenEventsInOrderAndEndsWithDone(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestService(t, newFakeHosts(), nil)
	run := registerRun(t, s, Operation{ID: "op_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", HostID: "h_1", Stack: "web", Kind: KindUp})
	run.setState(StateRunning)
	run.line("before the subscriber")

	op, events, cancel, err := s.Subscribe("op_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer cancel()
	if op.State != StateRunning || op.Output != "before the subscriber\n" || op.StartedAt == nil {
		t.Fatalf("snapshot = %+v, want the running state with the output so far", op)
	}

	run.composeLine(`{"id":"Container web-1","status":"Working","text":"Starting"}`)
	run.composeLine(`{"id":"layer1","status":"Working","text":"Downloading","current":10,"total":100}`)
	run.composeLine("plain line")
	run.setState(StateHealthWait)
	exit := 0
	run.finish(outcome{state: StateSucceeded, exit: &exit, warning: "db is unhealthy", ports: []PortLink{{Service: "web", PublicPort: 8080, PrivatePort: 80, Protocol: "tcp"}}})

	got := drainEvents(events)
	types := make([]string, len(got))
	for i, ev := range got {
		types[i] = ev.Type
		// Seq numbers the events of the whole operation: the state change and the line
		// before the subscription took numbers 1 and 2.
		if ev.Seq != int64(i+3) {
			t.Fatalf("event %d has seq %d, want %d", i, ev.Seq, i+3)
		}
	}
	// Progress and output for the first item, progress only for the byte tick, the plain
	// line, the health_wait state, done.
	want := []string{EventProgress, EventOutput, EventProgress, EventOutput, EventState, EventDone}
	if strings.Join(types, ",") != strings.Join(want, ",") {
		t.Fatalf("event types = %v, want %v", types, want)
	}
	if got[0].Progress == nil || got[0].Progress.ID != "Container web-1" || got[1].Text != "Container web-1 Working Starting\n" {
		t.Fatalf("first item = %+v / %+v", got[0], got[1])
	}
	if got[2].Progress.Total != 100 || got[3].Text != "plain line\n" {
		t.Fatalf("byte tick / plain line = %+v / %+v", got[2], got[3])
	}
	if got[4].Operation == nil || got[4].Operation.State != StateHealthWait || got[4].Operation.Output != "" {
		t.Fatalf("state event = %+v, want health_wait without output", got[4])
	}
	done := got[5].Operation
	if done == nil || done.State != StateSucceeded || done.Warning != "db is unhealthy" || done.FinishedAt == nil ||
		done.ExitCode == nil || *done.ExitCode != 0 || !strings.Contains(done.Output, "plain line") || len(done.Ports) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("done event = %+v", done)
	}

	// The lock is released and the journal holds the final row.
	if s.activeRun("h_1", "web") != nil {
		t.Fatal("a finished operation must release its stack")
	}
	row, err := s.Operation(context.Background(), "op_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa")
	if err != nil || row.State != StateSucceeded || !strings.Contains(row.Output, "before the subscriber") {
		t.Fatalf("journal row = %+v, %v", row, err)
	}
	// A subscriber after the end gets the final snapshot and a closed channel.
	op2, ch2, _, err := s.Subscribe("op_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa")
	if err != nil || op2.State != StateSucceeded {
		t.Fatalf("late Subscribe = %+v, %v", op2, err)
	}
	if _, open := <-ch2; open {
		t.Fatal("the channel of a finished operation must already be closed")
	}
	if _, _, _, err := s.Subscribe("op_unknown"); CodeOf(err) != CodeOperationNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("Subscribe of an unknown id = %v, want %s", err, CodeOperationNotFound)
	}
}

func TestASubscriberThatFalls256EventsBehindIsDropped(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestService(t, newFakeHosts(), nil)
	run := registerRun(t, s, Operation{ID: "op_bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb", HostID: "h_1", Stack: "web", Kind: KindPull})
	_, slow, cancelSlow, _ := s.Subscribe("op_bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb")
	defer cancelSlow()
	_, fast, cancelFast, _ := s.Subscribe("op_bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb")
	defer cancelFast()

	fastCount := 0
	fastDone := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(fastDone)
		for range fast {
			fastCount++
		}
	}()
	for i := 0; i < 300; i++ {
		run.line("line")
		if i%50 == 49 {
			time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond) // let the fast reader keep up
		}
	}

	slowCount := 0
	for range slow { // closed by the drop, not by the end of the operation
		slowCount++
	}
	if slowCount != subscriberBuffer {
		t.Fatalf("the slow subscriber received %d events, want exactly the %d that fit its buffer", slowCount, subscriberBuffer)
	}
	run.finish(outcome{state: StateSucceeded})
	<-fastDone
	if fastCount != 301 { // 300 lines and the done event
		t.Fatalf("the fast subscriber received %d events, want 301", fastCount)
	}
}

	clock := newFakeClock()
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `internal/dockerstacks/oprun.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"sync"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// Event types of an operation's live stream.
const (
	EventOutput   = "output"
	EventProgress = "progress"
	EventState    = "state"
	EventDone     = "done"
)

const (
	// subscriberBuffer is how many events a subscriber may fall behind before it
	// is dropped; the client then reconnects and gets a fresh snapshot.
	subscriberBuffer = 256
	// flushInterval is how often the output of a running operation is written to its row.
	flushInterval = 2 * time.Second
	journalWrite  = 10 * time.Second
)

type subscriber struct{ ch chan Event }

// outcome is how an operation ended.
type outcome struct {
	state     string // StateSucceeded | StateFailed | StateInterrupted
	code      string
	message   string
	exit      *int
	errorLine int
	warning   string
	ports     []PortLink
	abandoned bool   // the service was closed: leave the operation as it is
	cleanup   func() // runs after the final state is recorded (removes the runner)
}

// opRun is the live state of one operation: the journal row it mirrors, the
// output tail, and the subscribers of its event stream.
type opRun struct {
	s *Service

	mu        sync.Mutex
	op        Operation
	tail      []byte
	seq       int64
	subs      map[*subscriber]struct{}
	closed    bool // finished or abandoned: no more events
	lastFlush time.Time
	lastLine  map[string]string // last output line per progress item id
	scan      errorScan
}

func newOpRun(s *Service, op Operation) *opRun {
	r := &opRun{s: s, op: op, subs: map[*subscriber]struct{}{}, lastLine: map[string]string{}, lastFlush: s.opts.Now()}
	r.tail = []byte(op.Output)
	r.trimTail(OutputTailBytes)
	r.op.Output = ""
	return r
}

// trimTail keeps at most limit bytes, cutting at a character boundary.
func (r *opRun) trimTail(limit int) {
	if len(r.tail) <= limit {
		return
	}
	cut := len(r.tail) - limit
	for cut < len(r.tail) && !utf8.RuneStart(r.tail[cut]) {
		cut++
	}
	r.tail = append(r.tail[:0], r.tail[cut:]...)
}

func (r *opRun) tailText() string {
	tail := r.tail
	if len(tail) > OutputTailBytes {
		cut := len(tail) - OutputTailBytes
		for cut < len(tail) && !utf8.RuneStart(tail[cut]) {
			cut++
		}
		tail = tail[cut:]
	}
	return string(tail)
}

// snapshot is a copy of the operation with the output so far.
func (r *opRun) snapshot() Operation {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	return r.snapshotLocked(true)
}

func (r *opRun) snapshotLocked(withOutput bool) Operation {
	op := r.op
	if withOutput {
		op.Output = r.tailText()
	} else {
		op.Output = ""
	}
	if op.ExitCode != nil {
		code := *op.ExitCode
		op.ExitCode = &code
	}
	op.Ports = append([]PortLink(nil), op.Ports...)
	return op
}

// publishLocked numbers an event and hands it to every subscriber without
// blocking. A subscriber whose buffer is full is dropped.
func (r *opRun) publishLocked(ev Event) {
	r.seq++
	ev.Seq = r.seq
	for sub := range r.subs {
		select {
		case sub.ch <- ev:
		default:
			delete(r.subs, sub)
			close(sub.ch)
		}
	}
}

// persistLocked writes the row; a failing journal is logged, never fatal.
func (r *opRun) persistLocked() {
	op := r.snapshotLocked(true)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), journalWrite)
	defer cancel()
	if err := r.s.journal.save(ctx, op); err != nil {
		r.s.log.Warn("docker operation could not be saved", "operation", op.ID, "error", err)
	}
	r.lastFlush = r.s.opts.Now()
}

// addOutput appends text to the output and publishes it. The row is rewritten
// at most every flushInterval.
func (r *opRun) addOutput(text string) {
	if text == "" {
		return
	}
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.addOutputLocked(text)
}

func (r *opRun) addOutputLocked(text string) {
	if r.closed {
		return
	}
	r.tail = append(r.tail, text...)
	r.trimTail(2 * OutputTailBytes)
	r.publishLocked(Event{Type: EventOutput, Text: text})
	if r.s.opts.Now().Sub(r.lastFlush) >= flushInterval {
		r.persistLocked()
	}
}

// line appends one line of AuraGo's own commentary to the output.
func (r *opRun) line(text string) { r.addOutput(text + "\n") }

// progress publishes one progress item.
func (r *opRun) progress(p Progress) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.progressLocked(p)
}

func (r *opRun) progressLocked(p Progress) {
	if r.closed {
		return
	}
	r.publishLocked(Event{Type: EventProgress, Progress: &p})
}

// composeLine takes one raw line of the runner's output. A line that is a
// JSON progress item becomes a progress event plus a readable output line
// (byte ticks and repeats of the same text for the same item stay out of the
// output); every other line goes to the output as it is.
func (r *opRun) composeLine(raw string) {
	if hook := r.s.rawLine; hook != nil {
		hook(r.op.ID, raw)
	}
	p, isProgress := parseProgressLine(raw)
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if !isProgress {
		r.scan.observe(raw, nil)
		r.addOutputLocked(raw + "\n")
		return
	}
	r.scan.observe(raw, &p)
	r.progressLocked(p)
	if isByteTick(p) {
		return
	}
	text := progressText(p)
	if r.lastLine[p.ID] == text {
		return
	}
	r.lastLine[p.ID] = text
	r.addOutputLocked(text + "\n")
}

// pullMessage turns one message of an image pull into a progress item and, for
// the messages that are not byte ticks, an output line.
func (r *opRun) pullMessage(m jsonMessage) {
	id := m.ID
	if id == "" {
		id = RunnerImageTag
	}
	p := Progress{ID: id, Parent: RunnerImageTag, Status: m.Status, Current: m.Progress.Current, Total: m.Progress.Total}
	if p.Total > 0 && p.Current > 0 {
		p.Percent = float64(p.Current*1000/p.Total) / 10
	}
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.progressLocked(p)
	if isByteTick(p) || m.Status == "" {
		return
	}
	text := m.Status
	if m.ID != "" {
		text = m.ID + ": " + m.Status
	}
	if r.lastLine[id] == text {
		return
	}
	r.lastLine[id] = text
	r.addOutputLocked(text + "\n")
}

// mutate changes the operation under the lock and writes the row.
func (r *opRun) mutate(fn func(op *Operation)) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if r.closed {
		return
	}
	fn(&r.op)
	r.persistLocked()
}

// setState records a state change and publishes it (without the output).
func (r *opRun) setState(state string) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if r.closed || r.op.State == state {
		return
	}
	r.op.State = state
	if state == StateRunning && r.op.StartedAt == nil {
		now := r.s.opts.Now().UTC()
		r.op.StartedAt = &now
	}
	r.persistLocked()
	snap := r.snapshotLocked(false)
	r.publishLocked(Event{Type: EventState, Operation: &snap})
}

// finish records the outcome, publishes the done event, ends every subscriber's
// stream and releases the stack's lock: its place among the active operations
// and the cached folder scan of its host (a stack operation may have changed the
// folders; prepare leaves the scan it just made). The service lock is taken
// before the run's, the order begin uses, so that the final state and the free
// stack become visible together: whoever sees the operation done can start the
// next one.
func (r *opRun) finish(out outcome) {
	s := r.s
	s.mu.Lock()
	r.mu.Lock()
	if r.closed {
		r.mu.Unlock()
		s.mu.Unlock()
		return
	}
	now := s.opts.Now().UTC()
	r.op.State = out.state
	r.op.Code, r.op.Error, r.op.ErrorLine, r.op.Warning = out.code, out.message, out.errorLine, out.warning
	if out.exit != nil {
		code := *out.exit
		r.op.ExitCode = &code
	}
	if out.ports != nil {
		r.op.Ports = out.ports
	}
	r.op.FinishedAt = &now
	r.persistLocked()
	done := r.snapshotLocked(true)
	r.closed = true
	r.publishLocked(Event{Type: EventDone, Operation: &done})
	r.closeSubscribersLocked()

	delete(s.runs, done.ID)
	if s.locks[lockKey{done.HostID, done.Stack}] == done.ID {
		delete(s.locks, lockKey{done.HostID, done.Stack})
	}
	if done.Stack != "" {
		delete(s.scans, done.HostID)
	}
	r.mu.Unlock()
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.pruneJournal(done.HostID, done.Stack)
}

// abandon ends the run without a result: the service is closing and the next
// Open reattaches. The output so far is saved.
func (r *opRun) abandon() {
	r.mu.Lock()
	if r.closed {
		r.mu.Unlock()
		return
	}
	r.persistLocked()
	r.closeSubscribersLocked()
	r.closed = true
	r.mu.Unlock()
}

func (r *opRun) closeSubscribersLocked() {
	for sub := range r.subs {
		close(sub.ch)
		delete(r.subs, sub)
	}
}

// subscribe returns the current state with the output so far and a channel of
// the events that follow. ok is false when the run has ended.
func (r *opRun) subscribe() (op Operation, events <-chan Event, cancel func(), ok bool) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	if r.closed {
		return Operation{}, nil, nil, false
	}
	sub := &subscriber{ch: make(chan Event, subscriberBuffer)}
	r.subs[sub] = struct{}{}
	cancel = func() {
		r.mu.Lock()
		defer r.mu.Unlock()
		if _, found := r.subs[sub]; found {
			delete(r.subs, sub)
			close(sub.ch)
		}
	}
	return r.snapshotLocked(true), sub.ch, cancel, true
}

// pruneJournal keeps the newest journalKeep finished operations of a stack.
func (s *Service) pruneJournal(hostID, stack string) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), journalWrite)
	defer cancel()
	if err := s.journal.prune(ctx, hostID, stack, journalKeep); err != nil {
		s.log.Warn("docker operation journal could not be pruned", "error", err)
	}
}
```
