```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// Hosts is satisfied by *dockerhost.Registry.
type Hosts interface {
	Host(ctx context.Context, id string) (dockerhost.Host, error)
	Client(ctx context.Context, id string) (*dockerutil.Client, error)
}

// Options configure a Service. Zero values take the defaults.
type Options struct {
	Logger       *slog.Logger
	Now          func() time.Time // default time.Now
	HealthWait   time.Duration    // default 120 s
	HealthPoll   time.Duration    // default 2 s
	MaxDuration  time.Duration    // default 60 min
	ListCacheTTL time.Duration    // default 30 s
	LocalHostID  string           // default dockerhost.LocalHostID; source for copying the runner image
}

func (o Options) withDefaults() Options {
	if o.Logger == nil {
		o.Logger = slog.Default()
	}
	if o.Now == nil {
		o.Now = time.Now
	}
	if o.HealthWait <= 0 {
		o.HealthWait = 120 * time.Second
	}
	if o.HealthPoll <= 0 {
		o.HealthPoll = 2 * time.Second
	}
	if o.MaxDuration <= 0 {
		o.MaxDuration = 60 * time.Minute
	}
	if o.ListCacheTTL <= 0 {
		o.ListCacheTTL = 30 * time.Second
	}
	if o.LocalHostID == "" {
		o.LocalHostID = dockerhost.LocalHostID
	}
	return o
}

// lockKey identifies what one operation or one file write owns: a stack on a
// host, or the host itself (stack "") for prepare.
type lockKey struct{ host, stack string }

// Service is the stacks service of the Docker Manager. It is safe for
// concurrent use.
type Service struct {
	db      *sql.DB
	journal *journal
	hosts   Hosts
	opts    Options
	log     *slog.Logger

	// baseCtx bounds every operation goroutine; Close cancels it. An operation
	// stopped that way stays in the journal as it is and is reattached by the
	// next Open.
	baseCtx context.Context
	cancel  context.CancelFunc
	wg      sync.WaitGroup

	mu        sync.Mutex
	closed    bool
	runs      map[string]*opRun       // active operations by id
	locks     map[lockKey]string      // (host, stack) -> id of the active operation
	scans     map[string]*scanCache   // folder scan per host
	ready     map[string]readyHost    // hosts last seen as prepared
	hostLocks map[string]*sync.Mutex  // serialize preparing a host
	fileLocks map[lockKey]*sync.Mutex // serialize read-compare-write of a stack's files
	swept     map[string]bool         // hosts whose leftover helper containers were cleaned up
	parked    map[string]*opRun       // adopted operations waiting for their host to answer, by id

	// rawLine, when set by a test, sees every raw line of a runner's output.
	rawLine func(operationID, line string)
}

// readyHost remembers that a host passed the helper check, and with which image.
type readyHost struct {
	at    time.Time
	image string
}

// scanFolder is what the lister found in one folder of the stacks directory.
type scanFolder struct {
	composeFile string // the first of ComposeFileNames present; "" when the folder has only a .env
	hasEnv      bool
}

// scanCache is the result of one lister run.
type scanCache struct {
	at      time.Time
	folders map[string]scanFolder // by folder name; valid stack names only
	ignored []IgnoredFolder
}

// cachedScan returns the host's folder scan when it is younger than ListCacheTTL.
func (s *Service) cachedScan(hostID string) (*scanCache, bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	c, ok := s.scans[hostID]
	if !ok || s.opts.Now().Sub(c.at) >= s.opts.ListCacheTTL {
		return nil, false
	}
	return c, true
}

func (s *Service) storeScan(hostID string, c *scanCache) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.scans[hostID] = c
}

// invalidateScan drops the cached folder scan of a host (our own writes and
// operations change the folders).
func (s *Service) invalidateScan(hostID string) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	delete(s.scans, hostID)
}

// readyImage returns the helper image of a host that passed the helper check
// less than ListCacheTTL ago.
func (s *Service) readyImage(hostID string) (string, bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	r, ok := s.ready[hostID]
	if !ok || s.opts.Now().Sub(r.at) >= s.opts.ListCacheTTL {
		return "", false
	}
	return r.image, true
}

func (s *Service) markReady(hostID, image string) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.ready[hostID] = readyHost{at: s.opts.Now(), image: image}
}

// Open creates the journal table in db (the shared docker_manager.db handle,
// see dockerhost.Store.DB) and returns a service.
func Open(db *sql.DB, hosts Hosts, opts Options) (*Service, error) {
	if db == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("dockerstacks: a database is required")
	}
	if hosts == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("dockerstacks: a host registry is required")
	}
	opts = opts.withDefaults()
	j, err := newJournal(db)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	s := &Service{
		db: db, journal: j, hosts: hosts, opts: opts, log: opts.Logger,
		baseCtx: ctx, cancel: cancel,
		runs:      map[string]*opRun{},
		locks:     map[lockKey]string{},
		scans:     map[string]*scanCache{},
		ready:     map[string]readyHost{},
		hostLocks: map[string]*sync.Mutex{},
		fileLocks: map[lockKey]*sync.Mutex{},
		swept:     map[string]bool{},
		parked:    map[string]*opRun{},
	}
	return s, nil
}

// Close stops the followers. Runner containers keep going; the next Open
// reattaches to them. Close returns when the service's goroutines have ended.
func (s *Service) Close() {
	s.mu.Lock()
	if s.closed {
		s.mu.Unlock()
		return
	}
	s.closed = true
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.cancel()
	s.wg.Wait()
}

func (s *Service) isClosed() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.closed
}

// target resolves a host and its Engine client.
func (s *Service) target(ctx context.Context, hostID string) (dockerhost.Host, engine, error) {
	h, err := s.hosts.Host(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return dockerhost.Host{}, engine{}, err
	}
	c, err := s.hosts.Client(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return dockerhost.Host{}, engine{}, err
	}
	return h, newEngine(c), nil
}

// newOperationID returns "op_" plus 16 lowercase hex characters.
func newOperationID() (string, error) {
	var b [8]byte
	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("generate operation id: %w", err)
	}
	return "op_" + hex.EncodeToString(b[:]), nil
}

// newShortID returns 8 lowercase hex characters (lister container names).
func newShortID() string {
	var b [4]byte
	_, _ = rand.Read(b[:])
	return hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
}

// hostLock returns the mutex that serializes preparing one host.
func (s *Service) hostLock(hostID string) *sync.Mutex {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	m, ok := s.hostLocks[hostID]
	if !ok {
		m = &sync.Mutex{}
		s.hostLocks[hostID] = m
	}
	return m
}

// fileLock returns the mutex that serializes the file writes of one stack.
func (s *Service) fileLock(hostID, stack string) *sync.Mutex {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	key := lockKey{hostID, stack}
	m, ok := s.fileLocks[key]
	if !ok {
		m = &sync.Mutex{}
		s.fileLocks[key] = m
	}
	return m
}

// activeRun returns the operation running on a stack, if any.
func (s *Service) activeRun(hostID, stack string) *opRun {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if id, ok := s.locks[lockKey{hostID, stack}]; ok {
		return s.runs[id]
	}
	return nil
}

// refuseWhileDeleting returns a BusyError when a delete is running on the stack.
func (s *Service) refuseWhileDeleting(hostID, stack string) error {
	if run := s.activeRun(hostID, stack); run != nil {
		if op := run.snapshot(); op.Kind == KindDelete {
			return &BusyError{OperationID: op.ID, Kind: op.Kind}
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/service_query.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"time"
)

// queryTimeout bounds a journal read.
const queryTimeout = 10 * time.Second

// activeRunByID returns the live run of an operation, if it has not finished.
func (s *Service) activeRunByID(id string) *opRun {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.runs[id]
}

// Operation returns one operation. A running one is answered from memory (with
// the output so far); a finished one from the journal.
func (s *Service) Operation(ctx context.Context, id string) (Operation, error) {
	if run := s.activeRunByID(id); run != nil {
		return run.snapshot(), nil
	}
	return s.journal.get(ctx, id)
}

// Operations lists journal entries newest first. Their Output is not filled in;
// Operation(id) has it.
func (s *Service) Operations(ctx context.Context, f OperationFilter) ([]Operation, error) {
	ops, err := s.journal.list(ctx, f)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// A running operation is newer in memory than in its row.
	for i := range ops {
		if !ops[i].Done() {
			if run := s.activeRunByID(ops[i].ID); run != nil {
				live := run.snapshot()
				live.Output = ""
				ops[i] = live
			}
		}
	}
	return ops, nil
}

// Subscribe returns the current state of an operation, with the output so far,
// and a channel of the events that follow. The channel is closed after the done
// event, on cancel, or when the subscriber falls 256 events behind (the client
// reconnects for a fresh snapshot). For a finished operation it returns the
// snapshot and an already closed channel.
func (s *Service) Subscribe(id string) (Operation, <-chan Event, func(), error) {
	if run := s.activeRunByID(id); run != nil {
		if op, events, cancel, ok := run.subscribe(); ok {
			return op, events, cancel, nil
		}
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), queryTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	op, err := s.journal.get(ctx, id)
	if err != nil {
		return Operation{}, nil, nil, err
	}
	closed := make(chan Event)
	close(closed)
	return op, closed, func() {}, nil
}
```

### Task A6: Host helpers and preparation, discovery, `List`

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/discovery.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/helpers.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/prepare.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/util.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/discovery_test.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/prepare_test.go`

- `helpers.go`: `Helpers` (read only: Engine API level, runner image present, IO container `ok`/`missing`/`mismatch` by its stacks-dir label) and `requirePrepared`, which every read uses: an unprepared host answers `host_not_prepared` with the helper status, API below 1.41 answers `api_too_old`, **nothing is pulled or created by a read**. The runner image counts as present under the pinned digest reference or under `RunnerLocalTag`.
- `prepare.go`: `ensureHost` — API check, then the runner image (pull with progress; if the pull fails on a remote host, copy it from the local engine with `GET /images/<ref>/get` into `POST /images/load` **only when both engines report the same OS and architecture**, then tag it `RunnerLocalTag`; otherwise `runner_image_missing` with the exact `docker pull docker:29.9.2-cli@sha256:…` command), then the IO container (recreated when its stacks-dir label differs; a container of that name without the IO role label is never touched). Concurrent calls for one host are serialized.
- `discovery.go`: the lister run (`find` two levels deep, the stacks directory read-only, no socket; exit 1 is fine as long as it printed stacks), `parseListerOutput` (first of `ComposeFileNames` wins; names that fail `ValidateName` become ignored folders), the 30 s folder-scan cache, and `List`. The cache holds the scan, **container status is read live on every call**. Helper containers never belong to a project; projects that are not stacks are the external ones.

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
)

// testEnv is a service over one fake engine, registered as host "h_fake".
type testEnv struct {
	t     *testing.T
	fe    *fakeEngine
	hosts *fakeHosts
	svc   *Service
	host  dockerhost.Host
	clock *fakeClock
}

const testHostID = "h_fake"

// newTestEnv returns a service with one fake host. prepared gives the host the
// runner image and the IO container.
func newTestEnv(t *testing.T, prepared bool) *testEnv {
	t.Helper()
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	if prepared {
		fe.prepared()
	}
	hosts := newFakeHosts()
	host := hosts.add(t, testHostID, fe)
	clock := newFakeClock()
	svc := newTestService(t, hosts, func(o *Options) { o.Now = clock.Now })
	return &testEnv{t: t, fe: fe, hosts: hosts, svc: svc, host: host, clock: clock}
}

func TestParseListerOutput(t *testing.T) {
	out := strings.Join([]string{
		"/opt/stacks/web/compose.yaml",
		"/opt/stacks/web/.env",
		"/opt/stacks/web/docker-compose.yml", // loses against compose.yaml
		"/opt/stacks/db/docker-compose.yaml",
		"/opt/stacks/db/compose.yml", // wins against docker-compose.yaml
		"/opt/stacks/envonly/.env",
		"/opt/stacks/My Stack/compose.yaml", // not a valid name, has a compose file: ignored
		"/opt/stacks/My Stack/.env",
		"/opt/stacks/Upper/.env", // not a valid name, no compose file: not reported
		"/opt/stacks/web/deeper/compose.yaml",
		"/elsewhere/other/compose.yaml",
		"/opt/stacks/web/README.md",
		"",
	}, "\n")
	folders, ignored := parseListerOutput("/opt/stacks", out)
	want := map[string]scanFolder{
		"web":     {composeFile: "compose.yaml", hasEnv: true},
		"db":      {composeFile: "compose.yml"},
		"envonly": {hasEnv: true},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(folders, want) {
		t.Fatalf("folders = %+v, want %+v", folders, want)
	}
	if len(ignored) != 1 || ignored[0] != (IgnoredFolder{Name: "My Stack", Reason: "name_invalid"}) {
		t.Fatalf("ignored = %+v", ignored)
	}
}

func TestHelpersReportWhatTheHostHas(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, false)
	ctx := context.Background()

	st, err := env.svc.Helpers(ctx, testHostID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := HelperStatus{APIVersion: "1.45", APISupported: true, RunnerImage: "docker:29.9.2-cli", IOContainer: "missing"}
	if st != want {
		t.Fatalf("unprepared host: %+v, want %+v", st, want)
	}

	env.fe.addImage(RunnerImage, "sha256:runnerimage")
	if st, _ = env.svc.Helpers(ctx, testHostID); !st.RunnerImagePresent || st.Prepared || st.IOContainer != "missing" {
		t.Fatalf("image only: %+v", st)
	}

	env.fe.addContainer(IOContainerName, ioSpec(RunnerImage, env.host), "created", 0)
	if st, _ = env.svc.Helpers(ctx, testHostID); !st.Prepared || st.IOContainer != "ok" {
		t.Fatalf("prepared: %+v", st)
	}

	// An IO container made for another stacks directory is a mismatch.
	env.fe.mu.Lock()
	for _, fc := range env.fe.containers {
		fc.labels[LabelStacksDir] = "/srv/other"
	}
	env.fe.mu.Unlock()
	if st, _ = env.svc.Helpers(ctx, testHostID); st.Prepared || st.IOContainer != "mismatch" {
		t.Fatalf("other stacks directory: %+v", st)
	}

	env.fe.setVersion("1.40", "linux", "amd64")
	st, err = env.svc.Helpers(ctx, testHostID)
	if err != nil || st.APISupported || st.Prepared || st.APIVersion != "1.40" {
		t.Fatalf("API 1.40: %+v, %v", st, err)
	}
	if _, err := env.svc.Helpers(ctx, "h_unknown"); !errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound) {
		t.Fatalf("unknown host = %v, want ErrHostNotFound", err)
	}
}

func TestHelpersFindACopiedImageByItsLocalTag(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, false)
	env.fe.addImage(RunnerLocalTag, "sha256:copied")
	env.fe.addContainer(IOContainerName, ioSpec(RunnerLocalTag, env.host), "created", 0)
	st, err := env.svc.Helpers(context.Background(), testHostID)
	if err != nil || !st.Prepared {
		t.Fatalf("a host that has the image only under the local tag is prepared, got %+v, %v", st, err)
	}
}

func TestReadsOnAnUnpreparedHostAnswerHostNotPreparedAndCreateNothing(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, false)
	_, err := env.svc.List(context.Background(), testHostID, false)
	var coded *Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != CodeHostNotPrepared {
		t.Fatalf("List = %v, want %s", err, CodeHostNotPrepared)
	}
	helpers, ok := coded.Fields["helpers"].(HelperStatus)
	if !ok || helpers.Prepared || helpers.RunnerImage != RunnerImageTag {
		t.Fatalf("fields = %+v, want the helper status", coded.Fields)
	}
	for _, prefix := range []string{"POST /containers/create", "POST /images/create"} {
		if n := env.fe.requestCount(prefix); n != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("a read made %d %s requests; reads never create or pull", n, prefix)
		}
	}

	env.fe.prepared()
	env.fe.setVersion("1.40", "linux", "amd64")
	_, err = env.svc.List(context.Background(), testHostID, false)
	if CodeOf(err) != CodeAPITooOld {
		t.Fatalf("List on API 1.40 = %v, want %s", err, CodeAPITooOld)
	}
	if errors.As(err, &coded); coded.Fields["api_version"] != "1.40" {
		t.Fatalf("fields = %+v, want api_version 1.40", coded.Fields)
	}
}

func seedStacks(env *testEnv) {
	fe := env.fe
	for _, f := range []string{
		"/opt/stacks/web/compose.yaml", "/opt/stacks/web/.env", "/opt/stacks/db/docker-compose.yml",
		"/opt/stacks/draft/compose.yaml", "/opt/stacks/My Stack/compose.yaml", "/opt/stacks/envonly/.env",
	} {
		fe.putFile(f, "x")
	}
	now := time.Now().Unix()
	fe.addProjectContainer("web-web-1", "web", "web", "running", "Up 2 hours (healthy)", "healthy", now-7200,
		fakePort{IP: "0.0.0.0", Private: 80, Public: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}, fakePort{IP: "::", Private: 80, Public: 8080, Proto: "tcp"})
	fe.addProjectContainer("web-cache-1", "web", "cache", "running", "Up 2 hours (unhealthy)", "unhealthy", now-7300)
	fe.addProjectContainer("db-db-1", "db", "db", "exited", "Exited (1) 3 minutes ago", "", now-600)
	fe.addProjectContainer("legacy-app-1", "legacy", "app", "running", "Up 1 day", "", now-86400,
		fakePort{IP: "0.0.0.0", Private: 3000, Public: 3000, Proto: "tcp"})
}

func TestListBuildsStacksExternalProjectsAndIgnoredFolders(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	seedStacks(env)
	listing, err := env.svc.List(context.Background(), testHostID, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if listing.HostID != testHostID || listing.StacksDir != "/opt/stacks" || listing.Cached {
		t.Fatalf("listing header = %+v", listing)
	}
	names := make([]string, len(listing.Stacks))
	for i, s := range listing.Stacks {
		names[i] = s.Name
	}
	if strings.Join(names, ",") != "db,draft,web" {
		t.Fatalf("stacks = %v, want db, draft, web sorted (envonly has no compose file)", names)
	}
	db, draft, web := listing.Stacks[0], listing.Stacks[1], listing.Stacks[2]
	if db.Status != StatusError || db.ComposeFile != "docker-compose.yml" || db.HasEnv || db.Dir != "/opt/stacks/db" {
		t.Fatalf("db = %+v", db)
	}
	if draft.Status != StatusDraft || draft.Created != 0 || len(draft.ContainerIDs) != 0 || draft.Ports == nil {
		t.Fatalf("draft = %+v", draft)
	}
	if web.Status != StatusPartial || web.Services.Total != 2 || web.Services.Running != 2 || !web.HasEnv || web.ComposeFile != "compose.yaml" {
		t.Fatalf("web = %+v", web)
	}
	if len(web.Ports) != 1 || web.Ports[0].PublicPort != 8080 || web.Ports[0].Service != "web" {
		t.Fatalf("web ports = %+v, want the IPv4 and IPv6 binding collapsed", web.Ports)
	}
	if len(web.ContainerIDs) != 2 || len(web.ContainerIDs[0]) != 12 || web.Created == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("web ids/created = %v / %d", web.ContainerIDs, web.Created)
	}
	if len(listing.External) != 1 || listing.External[0].Name != "legacy" || listing.External[0].Status != StatusRunning ||
		listing.External[0].WorkingDir != "/opt/stacks/legacy" || len(listing.External[0].Ports) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("external = %+v", listing.External)
	}
	if len(listing.Ignored) != 1 || listing.Ignored[0].Name != "My Stack" {
		t.Fatalf("ignored = %+v", listing.Ignored)
	}
	// The IO container carries a role label and must not show up anywhere.
	for _, s := range listing.Stacks {
		for _, id := range s.ContainerIDs {
			if strings.HasPrefix(env.fe.container(IOContainerName).id, id) {
				t.Fatalf("the IO container is listed in stack %s", s.Name)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestListCachesTheFolderScanButReadsStatusLive(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	seedStacks(env)
	ctx := context.Background()
	listerRuns := func() int { return env.fe.requestCount("POST /containers/create?name=aurago-dm-ls-") }

	first, err := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false)
	if err != nil || first.Cached || listerRuns() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("first List: cached=%v runs=%d err=%v", first.Cached, listerRuns(), err)
	}
	if left := env.fe.containersWithRole(RoleLister); len(left) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d lister containers left behind", len(left))
	}

	// A new folder is not seen within the TTL, a container state change is.
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/fresh/compose.yaml", "x")
	cache := env.fe.container("web-cache-1")
	env.fe.mu.Lock() // the first List started a background sweep that reads the same container
	cache.state = "exited"
	env.fe.mu.Unlock()
	second, err := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false)
	if err != nil || !second.Cached || listerRuns() != 1 || len(second.Stacks) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("second List: cached=%v runs=%d stacks=%d err=%v", second.Cached, listerRuns(), len(second.Stacks), err)
	}
	if !second.ScannedAt.Equal(first.ScannedAt) {
		t.Fatal("a cached listing keeps the time of its scan")
	}
	if web := second.Stacks[2]; web.Services.Running != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("status must be live, web = %+v", web)
	}

	refreshed, err := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, true)
	if err != nil || refreshed.Cached || listerRuns() != 2 || len(refreshed.Stacks) != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("refresh: cached=%v runs=%d stacks=%d err=%v", refreshed.Cached, listerRuns(), len(refreshed.Stacks), err)
	}

	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/later/compose.yaml", "x")
	env.clock.Advance(31 * time.Minute)
	if expired, _ := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false); expired.Cached || len(expired.Stacks) != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("after the TTL the scan must run again, cached=%v stacks=%d", expired.Cached, len(expired.Stacks))
	}

	env.svc.invalidateScan(testHostID)
	if again, _ := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false); again.Cached {
		t.Fatal("invalidateScan must force a new scan")
	}
}

func TestListerFailures(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()

	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	env.fe.startFails = "invalid mount config for type \"bind\": bind source path does not exist"
	_, err := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false)
	var coded *Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != CodeStacksDirInvalid || !strings.Contains(coded.Message, "/opt/stacks") ||
		!strings.Contains(coded.Message, "invalid mount config") || dockerhost.StatusOf(err) != http.StatusInternalServerError {
		t.Fatalf("a refused bind = %v, want %s naming the directory and the Engine's reason", err, CodeStacksDirInvalid)
	}
	if left := env.fe.containersWithRole(RoleLister); len(left) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("a failed lister must still be removed")
	}

	env = newTestEnv(t, true)
	env.fe.listerExit, env.fe.listerErr = 1, "find: '/opt/stacks': Permission denied\n"
	if _, err = env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false); CodeOf(err) != CodeStacksDirInvalid || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "Permission denied") {
		t.Fatalf("find that found nothing and complained = %v, want %s with find's message", err, CodeStacksDirInvalid)
	}

	env = newTestEnv(t, true)
	seedStacks(env)
	env.fe.listerExit, env.fe.listerErr = 1, "find: '/opt/stacks/web/data': Permission denied\n"
	listing, err := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false)
	if err != nil || len(listing.Stacks) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("find that exits 1 after printing stacks is not a failure, got %v / %v", listing.Stacks, err)
	}
}
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
)

// twoHostEnv has the local engine ("local") and a remote one ("h_remote").
type twoHostEnv struct {
	local, remote *fakeEngine
	runs          int
	svc           *Service
	remoteHost    dockerhost.Host
}

func newTwoHostEnv(t *testing.T) *twoHostEnv {
	t.Helper()
	local, remote := newFakeEngine(t), newFakeEngine(t)
	hosts := newFakeHosts()
	hosts.add(t, "local", local)
	remoteHost := hosts.add(t, "h_remote", remote)
	return &twoHostEnv{local: local, remote: remote, svc: newTestService(t, hosts, nil), remoteHost: remoteHost}
}

// ensureResult is what ensureHost returned together with the operation's output
// and progress events.
type ensureResult struct {
	image    string
	err      error
	output   string
	progress []Progress
}

func mustJSON(v any) string {
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return string(b)
}

// ensure runs ensureHost for a host as an operation would.
func (e *twoHostEnv) ensure(t *testing.T, hostID string, verbose bool) ensureResult {
	t.Helper()
	e.runs++
	id := fmt.Sprintf("op_%016x", e.runs)
	run := registerRun(t, e.svc, Operation{ID: id, HostID: hostID, Kind: KindPrepare})
	_, events, cancel, err := e.svc.Subscribe(id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer cancel()
	h, eng, err := e.svc.target(context.Background(), hostID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	image, ensureErr := e.svc.ensureHost(context.Background(), run, eng, h, verbose)
	out := run.snapshot().Output
	run.finish(outcome{state: StateSucceeded})
	var progress []Progress
	for _, ev := range drainEvents(events) {
		if ev.Type == EventProgress {
			progress = append(progress, *ev.Progress)
		}
	}
	return ensureResult{image: image, err: ensureErr, output: out, progress: progress}
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/discovery.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

const (
	listerStdoutMax = 4 << 20
	listerStderrMax = 4 << 10
)

// parseListerOutput reads the lines `find` printed (one path per line, two
// levels below the stacks directory dir) into the folders that hold a compose
// file or a .env. Of several compose files in one folder the first of
// ComposeFileNames wins. A folder whose name cannot be a stack name is ignored
// when it holds a compose file.
func parseListerOutput(dir, stdout string) (map[string]scanFolder, []IgnoredFolder) {
	folders := map[string]scanFolder{}
	invalid := map[string]bool{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(stdout, "\n") {
		rel, ok := strings.CutPrefix(strings.TrimRight(line, "\r"), dir+"/")
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		name, file, ok := strings.Cut(rel, "/")
		if !ok || file == "" || strings.Contains(file, "/") {
			continue
		}
		rank := composeFileRank(file)
		if file != EnvFileName && rank < 0 {
			continue
		}
		if ValidateName(name) != nil {
			if rank >= 0 {
				invalid[name] = true
			}
			continue
		}
		f := folders[name]
		switch {
		case file == EnvFileName:
			f.hasEnv = true
		case f.composeFile == "" || rank < composeFileRank(f.composeFile):
			f.composeFile = file
		}
		folders[name] = f
	}
	ignored := make([]IgnoredFolder, 0, len(invalid))
	for name := range invalid {
		ignored = append(ignored, IgnoredFolder{Name: name, Reason: "name_invalid"})
	}
	sort.Slice(ignored, func(i, j int) bool { return ignored[i].Name < ignored[j].Name })
	return folders, ignored
}

// runLister runs the short-lived lister container on the host and returns what
// `find` printed. The container is removed again whatever happens. find exits 1
// when it cannot read a data folder of some stack; that is no failure as long as
// it found something. An Engine that refuses the container (a stacks directory
// it cannot bind) or a find that found nothing and complained is
// CodeStacksDirInvalid.
func (s *Service) runLister(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, image string) (string, error) {
	name := listerNamePrefix + newShortID()
	id, err := e.createContainer(ctx, name, listerSpec(image, h))
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer s.removeQuietly(e, id)
	if err := e.startContainer(ctx, id); err != nil {
		if dockerhost.StatusOf(err) >= 400 {
			return "", stacksDirError(h, err)
		}
		return "", err
	}
	stdout := &limitedBuffer{max: listerStdoutMax}
	stderr := &limitedBuffer{max: listerStderrMax}
	if err := e.followLogs(ctx, id, 0, stdout, stderr); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	st, err := e.waitExited(ctx, id)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	switch {
	case st.ExitCode == 0:
		return stdout.String(), nil
	case st.ExitCode == 1 && len(stdout.buf) > 0:
		return stdout.String(), nil
	}
	reason := firstNonBlankLine(stderr.String())
	if reason == "" {
		reason = "find exited with code " + strconv.Itoa(st.ExitCode)
	}
	return "", newError(CodeStacksDirInvalid, "the stacks directory %s could not be listed: %s", h.StacksDir, dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(reason, 200))
}

// removeQuietly removes a helper container with a context of its own (the
// caller's may be cancelled) and logs a failure.
func (s *Service) removeQuietly(e engine, id string) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), cleanupTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	if err := e.removeContainer(ctx, id); err != nil {
		s.log.Warn("docker manager helper container could not be removed", "container", id, "error", err)
	}
}

// scanFolders lists the stacks directory with the lister and caches the result.
func (s *Service) scanFolders(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, image string) (*scanCache, error) {
	stdout, err := s.runLister(ctx, e, h, image)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	folders, ignored := parseListerOutput(h.StacksDir, stdout)
	c := &scanCache{at: s.opts.Now(), folders: folders, ignored: ignored}
	s.storeScan(h.ID, c)
	return c, nil
}

// discover returns the folder scan of a host: the cached one when it is younger
// than ListCacheTTL (and refresh is false), else a fresh lister run. A host
// that is not prepared is an error and nothing is created.
func (s *Service) discover(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, refresh bool) (*scanCache, bool, error) {
	if !refresh {
		if c, ok := s.cachedScan(h.ID); ok {
			return c, true, nil
		}
	}
	image, err := s.requirePrepared(ctx, e, h)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, false, err
	}
	c, err := s.scanFolders(ctx, e, h, image)
	return c, false, err
}

// operationRefs maps the stacks of a host that have an operation to it.
func (s *Service) operationRefs(hostID string) map[string]OperationRef {
	s.mu.Lock()
	runs := make([]*opRun, 0, len(s.runs))
	for _, run := range s.runs {
		runs = append(runs, run)
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	refs := map[string]OperationRef{}
	for _, run := range runs {
		run.mu.Lock()
		op := run.op
		run.mu.Unlock()
		if op.HostID == hostID && op.Stack != "" {
			refs[op.Stack] = OperationRef{ID: op.ID, Kind: op.Kind, State: op.State}
		}
	}
	return refs
}

// projectGroups groups the compose containers of a host by project. The
// Docker Manager's own helper containers never belong to a project.
func projectGroups(containers []dockerhost.ContainerSummary) map[string][]dockerhost.ContainerSummary {
	groups := map[string][]dockerhost.ContainerSummary{}
	for _, c := range containers {
		if c.ComposeProject == "" || isHelperContainer(c) {
			continue
		}
		groups[c.ComposeProject] = append(groups[c.ComposeProject], c)
	}
	return groups
}

// List returns the stacks of a host (the folders of the stacks directory that
// hold a compose file), the compose projects that are not stacks, and the
// folders that were ignored. The folder scan runs a lister container and is
// cached for ListCacheTTL; refresh bypasses the cache. Container status is read
// live on every call. A host without the helpers answers CodeHostNotPrepared.
func (s *Service) List(ctx context.Context, hostID string, refresh bool) (Listing, error) {
	h, e, err := s.target(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return Listing{}, err
	}
	scan, cached, err := s.discover(ctx, e, h, refresh)
	if err != nil {
		return Listing{}, err
	}
	containers, err := dockerhost.ListContainers(ctx, e.c)
	if err != nil {
		return Listing{}, err
	}
	return s.buildListing(h, scan, cached, containers), nil
}

func (s *Service) buildListing(h dockerhost.Host, scan *scanCache, cached bool, containers []dockerhost.ContainerSummary) Listing {
	groups := projectGroups(containers)
	refs := s.operationRefs(h.ID)

	names := make([]string, 0, len(scan.folders))
	for name, f := range scan.folders {
		if f.composeFile != "" {
			names = append(names, name)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(names)

	listing := Listing{
		HostID:    h.ID,
		StacksDir: h.StacksDir,
		Stacks:    make([]StackSummary, 0, len(names)),
		External:  []ProjectSummary{},
		Ignored:   append([]IgnoredFolder{}, scan.ignored...),
		ScannedAt: scan.at,
		Cached:    cached,
	}
	for _, name := range names {
		f := scan.folders[name]
		members := groups[name]
		status, count := DeriveStatus(members)
		summary := StackSummary{
			Name:         name,
			HostID:       h.ID,
			Dir:          stackDir(h, name),
			ComposeFile:  f.composeFile,
			HasEnv:       f.hasEnv,
			Status:       status,
			Services:     count,
			Ports:        portLinks(members),
			ContainerIDs: shortIDs(members),
			Created:      oldestCreated(members),
		}
		if ref, ok := refs[name]; ok {
			summary.Operation = &ref
		}
		listing.Stacks = append(listing.Stacks, summary)
	}

	projects := make([]string, 0, len(groups))
	for project := range groups {
		if f, isStack := scan.folders[project]; !isStack || f.composeFile == "" {
			projects = append(projects, project)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(projects)
	for _, project := range projects {
		members := groups[project]
		status, count := DeriveStatus(members)
		listing.External = append(listing.External, ProjectSummary{
			Name:         project,
			WorkingDir:   workingDirOf(members),
			Status:       status,
			Services:     count,
			Ports:        portLinks(members),
			ContainerIDs: shortIDs(members),
		})
	}
	return listing
}

// workingDirOf is the compose working directory label of the first container that has one.
func workingDirOf(members []dockerhost.ContainerSummary) string {
	i := slices.IndexFunc(members, func(c dockerhost.ContainerSummary) bool { return c.ComposeWorkingDir != "" })
	if i < 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return members[i].ComposeWorkingDir
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/helpers.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
)

// resolveRunnerImage finds the reference under which the host has the runner
// image: the pinned digest reference, or the local tag of an image that was
// copied from another engine (a saved digest reference loses its name on load).
func (e engine) resolveRunnerImage(ctx context.Context) (ref string, present bool, err error) {
	for _, candidate := range []string{RunnerImage, RunnerLocalTag} {
		_, found, err := e.inspectImage(ctx, candidate)
		if err != nil {
			return "", false, err
		}
		if found {
			return candidate, true, nil
		}
	}
	return "", false, nil
}

// IO container states.
const (
	ioOK       = "ok"
	ioMissing  = "missing"
	ioMismatch = "mismatch"
)

// ioStatus inspects the IO container of a host. "ok" means a container of that
// name with the IO role label that was created for this host's stacks
// directory; "mismatch" means a container of that name that is not (the stacks
// directory of the host changed, or the name is taken by something else). The
// container's inspect document is returned when there is one.
func (e engine) ioStatus(ctx context.Context, h dockerhost.Host) (string, containerState, error) {
	st, err := e.inspectContainer(ctx, IOContainerName)
	if isNotFound(err) {
		return ioMissing, containerState{}, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return "", containerState{}, err
	}
	if st.Labels[LabelRole] != RoleIO || st.Labels[LabelStacksDir] != h.StacksDir {
		return ioMismatch, st, nil
	}
	return ioOK, st, nil
}

// waitExited inspects a container until it is no longer running and returns
// its final state. The log stream of a container ends when it exits, but the
// state can lag by a moment.
func (e engine) waitExited(ctx context.Context, ref string) (containerState, error) {
	for {
		st, err := e.inspectContainer(ctx, ref)
		if err != nil {
			return containerState{}, err
		}
		if !st.Running && st.Status != "created" && st.Status != "restarting" {
			return st, nil
		}
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return containerState{}, ctx.Err()
		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
		}
	}
}

// apiTooOldError is the error of a host whose Engine API is below 1.41.
func apiTooOldError(apiVersion string) *Error {
	return newError(CodeAPITooOld,
		"Docker Engine API %q is too old: stacks need API 1.%d (Docker 20.10) or newer", apiVersion, MinAPIMinor).
		withFields(map[string]any{"api_version": apiVersion})
}

// notPreparedError is the error of a read on a host without the helpers.
func notPreparedError(st HelperStatus) *Error {
	return newError(CodeHostNotPrepared, "this Docker host is not prepared for stacks: the helper image %s is needed", RunnerImageTag).
		withFields(map[string]any{"helpers": st})
}

// helpers reports what the host has of the helpers and the image reference to
// create helper containers from. Nothing is created or pulled.
func (s *Service) helpers(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host) (HelperStatus, string, error) {
	st := HelperStatus{RunnerImage: RunnerImageTag, IOContainer: ioMissing}
	v, err := e.version(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return st, "", err
	}
	st.APIVersion = v.APIVersion
	st.APISupported = supportsStacks(v.APIVersion)
	if !st.APISupported {
		return st, "", nil
	}
	ref, present, err := e.resolveRunnerImage(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return st, "", err
	}
	st.RunnerImagePresent = present
	io, _, err := e.ioStatus(ctx, h)
	if err != nil {
		return st, "", err
	}
	st.IOContainer = io
	st.Prepared = st.APISupported && st.RunnerImagePresent && st.IOContainer == ioOK
	return st, ref, nil
}

// Helpers reports what a host has of the helper image and the IO container.
// It only reads.
func (s *Service) Helpers(ctx context.Context, hostID string) (HelperStatus, error) {
	h, e, err := s.target(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return HelperStatus{}, err
	}
	st, _, err := s.helpers(ctx, e, h)
	return st, err
}

// requirePrepared returns the helper image of a host that is ready for stacks.
// A host that is not gets CodeHostNotPrepared (with the helper status) or
// CodeAPITooOld; reads never pull or create anything.
func (s *Service) requirePrepared(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host) (string, error) {
	if image, ok := s.readyImage(h.ID); ok {
		return image, nil
	}
	st, ref, err := s.helpers(ctx, e, h)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	switch {
	case !st.APISupported:
		return "", apiTooOldError(st.APIVersion)
	case !st.Prepared:
		return "", notPreparedError(st)
	}
	s.markReady(h.ID, ref)
	return ref, nil
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/prepare.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
)

// pullCommand is the command that puts the runner image on a host by hand.
const pullCommand = "docker pull " + RunnerImageTag + "@" + RunnerImageDigest

// imageMissingError says that the runner image is neither on the host nor
// obtainable, and names the exact command that fixes it.
func imageMissingError(reason string) *Error {
	return newError(CodeRunnerImageMissing,
		"The helper image %s is not on this Docker host and could not be pulled or copied (%s). Run `%s` on the host, then prepare it again.",
		RunnerImageTag, reason, pullCommand).
		withFields(map[string]any{"command": pullCommand})
}

// ensureHost makes a host ready for stacks, step by step: the Engine API must be
// 1.41 or newer, the runner image must be on the host (pulled, or copied from the
// local engine when the pull fails), and the IO container must exist for the
// host's stacks directory. It returns the image reference to create helper
// containers from. Every step that does work is reported in the operation's
// output; verbose also reports the steps that find everything in place.
// Concurrent calls for one host are serialized.
func (s *Service) ensureHost(ctx context.Context, run *opRun, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, verbose bool) (string, error) {
	lock := s.hostLock(h.ID)
	lock.Lock()
	defer lock.Unlock()

	v, err := e.version(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if !supportsStacks(v.APIVersion) {
		return "", apiTooOldError(v.APIVersion)
	}
	if verbose {
		run.line(fmt.Sprintf("Docker Engine %s, API %s", v.Version, v.APIVersion))
	}

	ref, present, err := e.resolveRunnerImage(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if present {
		if verbose {
			run.line("Helper image " + RunnerImageTag + " is present")
		}
	} else {
		run.line("Pulling the helper image " + RunnerImageTag + " (about 64 MB)")
		if ref, err = s.acquireRunnerImage(ctx, run, e, h); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}

	if err := s.ensureIOContainer(ctx, run, e, h, ref, verbose); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	s.markReady(h.ID, ref)
	return ref, nil
}

// acquireRunnerImage pulls the runner image. When the pull fails on a host
// other than the local one, the image is copied from the local engine, but only
// if both engines report the same OS and architecture. Otherwise the error is
// CodeRunnerImageMissing with the exact pull command.
func (s *Service) acquireRunnerImage(ctx context.Context, run *opRun, e engine, h dockerhost.Host) (string, error) {
	pullErr := e.pullImage(ctx, runnerImageRepo, runnerImagePullTag, run.pullMessage)
	if pullErr == nil {
		return RunnerImage, nil
	}
	if ctx.Err() != nil {
		return "", ctx.Err()
	}
	reason := engineMessage(pullErr)
	if h.ID == s.opts.LocalHostID {
		return "", imageMissingError(reason)
	}
	run.line("The pull failed (" + reason + "); trying to copy the image from the local engine")
	return s.copyRunnerImage(ctx, run, e, reason)
}

// copyRunnerImage streams the runner image from the local engine to the target
// (GET /images/<ref>/get into POST /images/load) and tags it with RunnerLocalTag.
func (s *Service) copyRunnerImage(ctx context.Context, run *opRun, target engine, pullReason string) (string, error) {
	local, err := s.hosts.Client(ctx, s.opts.LocalHostID)
	if err != nil {
		return "", imageMissingError(pullReason + "; the local engine is not reachable")
	}
	source := newEngine(local)
	info, found, err := source.inspectImage(ctx, RunnerImage)
	if err != nil {
		return "", imageMissingError(pullReason + "; the local engine could not be asked: " + engineMessage(err))
	}
	if !found {
		return "", imageMissingError(pullReason + "; the local engine does not have the image either")
	}
	sv, err := source.version(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return "", imageMissingError(pullReason + "; the local engine could not be asked: " + engineMessage(err))
	}
	tv, err := target.version(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if sv.OS != tv.OS || sv.Arch != tv.Arch {
		return "", imageMissingError(fmt.Sprintf("%s; the local engine is %s/%s but this host is %s/%s", pullReason, sv.OS, sv.Arch, tv.OS, tv.Arch))
	}

	run.line(fmt.Sprintf("Copying the helper image from the local engine (%s/%s)", sv.OS, sv.Arch))
	body, err := source.saveImage(ctx, RunnerImage)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	defer body.Close()
	loaded, err := target.loadImage(ctx, body)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if ref, present, err := target.resolveRunnerImage(ctx); err != nil {
		return "", err
	} else if present {
		return ref, nil // a store that keeps the digest name needs no tag
	}
	if loaded == "" {
		loaded = info.ID
	}
	repo, tag, _ := strings.Cut(RunnerLocalTag, ":")
	if err := target.tagImage(ctx, loaded, repo, tag); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return RunnerLocalTag, nil
}

// ensureIOContainer creates the IO container of the host's stacks directory,
// or recreates it when it was made for another directory. A container of that
// name without the IO role label is never touched.
func (s *Service) ensureIOContainer(ctx context.Context, run *opRun, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, image string, verbose bool) error {
	state, st, err := e.ioStatus(ctx, h)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	switch state {
	case ioOK:
		if verbose {
			run.line("IO container " + IOContainerName + " is in place")
		}
		return nil
	case ioMismatch:
		if st.Labels[LabelRole] != RoleIO {
			return newError(CodeStacksDirInvalid,
				"a container named %s already exists and is not a Docker Manager helper; rename or remove it, then prepare the host again", IOContainerName)
		}
		run.line("Recreating the IO container for the stacks directory " + h.StacksDir)
		if err := e.removeContainer(ctx, IOContainerName); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	default:
		run.line("Creating the IO container " + IOContainerName)
	}
	if _, err := e.createContainer(ctx, IOContainerName, ioSpec(image, h)); err != nil {
		if dockerhost.StatusOf(err) == http.StatusConflict { // another preparation was faster
			if again, _, ioErr := e.ioStatus(ctx, h); ioErr == nil && again == ioOK {
				return nil
			}
		}
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

// stacksDirError explains that a helper container could not use the stacks
// directory (the Engine refused the bind mount, for example because Docker
// Desktop does not share the path).
func stacksDirError(h dockerhost.Host, cause error) *Error {
	e := newError(CodeStacksDirInvalid, "the Docker host cannot use the stacks directory %s: %s", h.StacksDir, engineMessage(cause))
	e.Err = cause
	return e
}

// limitedBuffer keeps at most max bytes and drops the rest.
type limitedBuffer struct {
	max int
	buf []byte
}

func (b *limitedBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if room := b.max - len(b.buf); room > 0 {
		if len(p) < room {
			room = len(p)
		}
		b.buf = append(b.buf, p[:room]...)
	}
	return len(p), nil
}

func (b *limitedBuffer) String() string { return string(b.buf) }
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// cleanupTimeout bounds the removal of a helper container, which runs on a
// context of its own because the caller's may already be cancelled.
const cleanupTimeout = 30 * time.Second

// firstNonBlankLine returns the first non-blank line of s, trimmed.
func firstNonBlankLine(s string) string {
	for _, line := range strings.Split(s, "\n") {
		if line = strings.TrimSpace(line); line != "" {
			return line
		}
	}
	return ""
}
```

### Task A7: Stack files through the IO container: `Get`, `Create`, `WriteFiles`

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/fileio.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/stacks.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/stacks_test.go`

- `fileio.go`: the archive API on the parked IO container. `HEAD` answers existence (a stack's `./data` can hold gigabytes, so a directory is never fetched), `GET` reads one regular file of at most `MaxFileBytes`, `PUT` extracts a tar owned by uid 0 (compose 0644, `.env` 0600) with `noOverwriteDirNonDir=true`. The Engine answers 404 for a missing path and for a missing container; only its message tells them apart (the same rule `tools.DockerGetArchiveContext` uses), and a bodiless `HEAD` 404 is rechecked against the helpers before a stack is declared missing.
- `stacks.go`: `Get` (files with revisions, services in compose-file order, then stray containers; a file that does not parse gives `ParseError` and services from the containers), `Create` (`stack_exists` when a compose file exists in the folder; a folder with only data is used as it is), `WriteFiles` (revision check under one mutex per host and stack, **all files checked before any is written**, `*ConflictError` with what is on the host, refused with `*BusyError` while a delete runs). A new folder travels in the archive as a 0755 entry; an existing folder gets only its files, extracted inside it, so its owner and mode stay (see Deviations).

```go
package dockerstacks

import (

const stacksTestCompose = "services:\n  web:\n    image: nginx:1.27\n    ports:\n      - \"8080:80\"\n  db:\n    image: postgres:16\n"

func TestParseComposeServices(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		content string
		want    string // "name=image,name=image"
		wantErr bool
	}{
		{"file order", stacksTestCompose, "web=nginx:1.27,db=postgres:16", false},
		{"no services key", "name: x\n", "", false},
		{"empty file", "", "", false},
		{"a service without image", "services:\n  app:\n    build: .\n  api:\n    image: x\n", "app=,api=x", false},
		{"extension fields and anchors are not services", "x-common: &c\n  restart: always\nservices:\n  a:\n    <<: *c\n    image: a:1\n", "a=a:1", false},
		{"services that is not a mapping", "services: []\n", "", false},
		{"top level list", "- a\n- b\n", "", true},
		{"yaml syntax error", "services:\n  web:\n   image: [nginx\n", "", true},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got, err := parseComposeServices([]byte(c.content))
		if (err != nil) != c.wantErr {
			t.Errorf("%s: err = %v, wantErr %v", c.name, err, c.wantErr)
			continue
		}
		parts := make([]string, len(got))
		for i, s := range got {
			parts[i] = s.name + "=" + s.image
		}
		if strings.Join(parts, ",") != c.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: services = %q, want %q", c.name, strings.Join(parts, ","), c.want)
		}
	}
}

	}
	if strings.Join(names, ",") != "web:running,db:missing,worker:exited" {
		t.Fatalf("service list = %v, want the file's services in order (db has no container) and then the stray worker", names)
	}
	web, db, worker := detail.ServiceList[0], detail.ServiceList[1], detail.ServiceList[2]
	if web.Image != "nginx:1.27" || web.Health != "healthy" || len(web.Ports) != 1 || web.ContainerID == "" || web.ExitCode != nil {
		t.Fatalf("web = %+v", web)
	}
	if db.Image != "postgres:16" || db.ContainerID != "" || db.Ports == nil {
		t.Fatalf("db = %+v", db)
	}
	if worker.Image != "worker:latest" || worker.ExitCode == nil || *worker.ExitCode != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("worker = %+v, want the container's image and exit code 2", worker)
	}
}

func TestGetUsesDockgesLookupOrderAndReportsAParseError(t *testing.T) {

}

func TestGetOnAHostWhoseIOContainerVanishedAnswersNotPrepared(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/a/compose.yaml", "services: {}\n")
	if _, err := env.svc.Get(context.Background(), testHostID, "a"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Someone removes the IO container while the service still believes the host is ready.
	env.fe.mu.Lock()
	for id, fc := range env.fe.containers {
		if fc.name == IOContainerName {
			delete(env.fe.containers, id)
		}
	}
	env.fe.mu.Unlock()
	_, err := env.svc.Get(context.Background(), testHostID, "a")
	var coded *Error
	if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != CodeHostNotPrepared {
		t.Fatalf("Get = %v, want %s", err, CodeHostNotPrepared)
	}
	if h, ok := coded.Fields["helpers"].(HelperStatus); !ok || h.IOContainer != "missing" || h.Prepared {
		t.Fatalf("fields = %+v, want the IO container reported missing", coded.Fields)
	}
}

func TestCreateWritesTheFolderWithTheRightModesAndOwner(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, err := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false); err != nil { // fills the scan cache
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	envText := "TOKEN=abc\n"
	detail, err := env.svc.Create(ctx, testHostID, CreateInput{Name: "blog", Compose: stacksTestCompose, Env: &envText})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if detail.Status != StatusDraft || detail.ComposeFile != "compose.yaml" || !detail.HasEnv || detail.Compose.Content != stacksTestCompose || detail.Env.Content != envText {
		t.Fatalf("detail = %+v", detail)
	}
	if got, _ := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/blog/compose.yaml"); got != stacksTestCompose {
		t.Fatalf("compose on the host = %q", got)
	}
	if env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/blog/compose.yaml") != 0o644 || env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/blog/.env") != 0o600 || env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/blog/") != 0o755 {
		t.Fatalf("modes: compose %o env %o dir %o, want 644, 600 and 755",
			env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/blog/compose.yaml"), env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/blog/.env"), env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/blog/"))
	}
	env.fe.mu.Lock()
	queries := append([]string(nil), env.fe.putQueries...)
	env.fe.mu.Unlock()
	if len(queries) != 1 || queries[0] != "path=%2Fopt%2Fstacks&noOverwriteDirNonDir=true" {
		t.Fatalf("PUT queries = %v, want one extraction into the stacks directory with noOverwriteDirNonDir", queries)
	}
	// The write invalidated the scan: the next List sees the new stack at once.
	listing, _ := env.svc.List(ctx, testHostID, false)
	if listing.Cached || len(listing.Stacks) != 1 || listing.Stacks[0].Name != "blog" {
		t.Fatalf("listing after Create = %+v", listing)
	}

	// No .env when none is given.
	if _, err := env.svc.Create(ctx, testHostID, CreateInput{Name: "plain", Compose: stacksTestCompose}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/plain/.env"); ok {
		t.Fatal("Create without Env must not write a .env")
	}
}

func TestCreateRefusesAnExistingStackAndKeepsAnExistingFolder(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	ctx := context.Background()
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/taken/docker-compose.yaml", "services: {}\n")
	_, err := env.svc.Create(ctx, testHostID, CreateInput{Name: "taken", Compose: stacksTestCompose})
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrStackExists) || CodeOf(err) != CodeStackExists {
		t.Fatalf("Create over an existing stack = %v, want %s", err, CodeStackExists)
	}
	if got, _ := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/taken/docker-compose.yaml"); got != "services: {}\n" {
		t.Fatal("an existing stack must not be touched")
	}
	if _, ok := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/taken/compose.yaml"); ok {
		t.Fatal("no second compose file may appear next to the existing one")
	}

	// A folder with data but no compose file is reused, and its own entry stays out of the archive.
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/data-only/data/db.sqlite", "bytes")
	if _, err := env.svc.Create(ctx, testHostID, CreateInput{Name: "data-only", Compose: stacksTestCompose}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Create in a folder without a compose file: %v", err)
	}
	if got, _ := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/data-only/data/db.sqlite"); got != "bytes" {
		t.Fatal("existing data must survive")
	}
	env.fe.mu.Lock()
	last := env.fe.putQueries[len(env.fe.putQueries)-1]
	env.fe.mu.Unlock()
	if last != "path=%2Fopt%2Fstacks%2Fdata-only&noOverwriteDirNonDir=true" {
		t.Fatalf("PUT query = %q, want the files extracted inside the existing folder so its owner and mode stay", last)
	}
	if env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/data-only/") != 0 {
		t.Fatal("an existing folder must not get a directory entry")
	}
}

func TestWriteFilesChecksRevisionsBeforeWritingAnything(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	ctx := context.Background()
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/app/docker-compose.yml", "v1\n")
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/app/.env", "A=1\n")
	revCompose, revEnv := Revision([]byte("v1\n")), Revision([]byte("A=1\n"))

	// A matching revision writes the file under its existing name.
	revs, err := env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Compose: &FileWrite{Content: "v2\n", Revision: revCompose}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if revs.Compose != Revision([]byte("v2\n")) || revs.Env != "" {
		t.Fatalf("revisions = %+v", revs)
	}
	if got, _ := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/app/docker-compose.yml"); got != "v2\n" {
		t.Fatalf("compose = %q", got)
	}
	if _, ok := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/app/compose.yaml"); ok {
		t.Fatal("the compose file keeps its name")
	}
	if env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/app/docker-compose.yml") != 0o644 {
		t.Fatalf("mode = %o", env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/app/docker-compose.yml"))
	}

	// The old revision is now stale: a conflict that carries what is on the host.
	_, err = env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Compose: &FileWrite{Content: "mine\n", Revision: revCompose}})
	var conflict *ConflictError
	if !errors.As(err, &conflict) || conflict.File != "compose" || conflict.Current.Content != "v2\n" ||
		conflict.Current.Revision != Revision([]byte("v2\n")) || !conflict.Current.Exists || conflict.Current.Name != "docker-compose.yml" {
		t.Fatalf("stale compose write = %v, want a ConflictError with the host's version", err)
	}
	if CodeOf(err) != CodeRevisionConflict {
		t.Fatalf("code = %s", CodeOf(err))
	}

	// One stale file stops the whole request: the other file is not written either.
	_, err = env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{
		Compose: &FileWrite{Content: "v3\n", Revision: Revision([]byte("v2\n"))},
		Env:     &FileWrite{Content: "A=changed\n", Revision: "stale"},
	})
	if !errors.As(err, &conflict) || conflict.File != "env" || conflict.Current.Content != "A=1\n" || conflict.Current.Revision != revEnv {
		t.Fatalf("stale env write = %v", err)
	}
	if got, _ := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/app/docker-compose.yml"); got != "v2\n" {
		t.Fatalf("compose = %q, nothing may be written when a file conflicts", got)
	}

	// Both files at once, with the current revisions; .env keeps mode 600.
	revs, err = env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{
		Compose: &FileWrite{Content: "v3\n", Revision: Revision([]byte("v2\n"))},
		Env:     &FileWrite{Content: "A=2\n", Revision: revEnv},
	})
	if err != nil || revs.Compose != Revision([]byte("v3\n")) || revs.Env != Revision([]byte("A=2\n")) {
		t.Fatalf("two-file write = %+v, %v", revs, err)
	}
	if env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/app/.env") != 0o600 {
		t.Fatalf(".env mode = %o", env.fe.mode("/opt/stacks/app/.env"))
	}
	// Writing into an existing stack never sends a directory entry (owner and mode stay).
	env.fe.mu.Lock()
	last := env.fe.putQueries[len(env.fe.putQueries)-1]
	env.fe.mu.Unlock()
	if last != "path=%2Fopt%2Fstacks%2Fapp&noOverwriteDirNonDir=true" {
		t.Fatalf("PUT query = %q", last)
	}
}

func TestWriteFilesCreatesAMissingEnvOnlyWithAnEmptyRevision(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	ctx := context.Background()
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/app/compose.yaml", "v1\n")

	_, err := env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Env: &FileWrite{Content: "A=1\n", Revision: "some-revision"}})
	var conflict *ConflictError
	if !errors.As(err, &conflict) || conflict.File != "env" || conflict.Current.Exists || conflict.Current.Revision != "" {
		t.Fatalf("env write based on a revision of a file that does not exist = %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Env: &FileWrite{Content: "A=1\n", Revision: ""}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("creating .env: %v", err)
	}
	if got, _ := env.fe.file("/opt/stacks/app/.env"); got != "A=1\n" {
		t.Fatalf(".env = %q", got)
	}
	// Now "must not exist yet" is wrong.
	if _, err := env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Env: &FileWrite{Content: "A=2\n", Revision: ""}}); !errors.As(err, &conflict) {
		t.Fatalf("a second creation = %v, want a conflict", err)
	}
	// An empty .env is a file with a revision of its own.
	revs, err := env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Env: &FileWrite{Content: "", Revision: Revision([]byte("A=1\n"))}})
	if err != nil || revs.Env != Revision(nil) {
		t.Fatalf("emptying .env = %+v, %v", revs, err)
	}
}

func TestWriteFilesRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	ctx := context.Background()
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/app/compose.yaml", "v1\n")

		t.Fatalf("oversized write = %v", err)

	registerRun(t, env.svc, Operation{ID: "op_dededededededede", HostID: testHostID, Stack: "app", Kind: KindDelete, State: StateRunning})
	_, err := env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Compose: ok})

func TestOnlyOneWriterPassesThePerStackLockAtATime(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, true)
	ctx := context.Background()
	env.fe.putFile("/opt/stacks/app/compose.yaml", "v0\n")
	rev := Revision([]byte("v0\n"))

	// Ten writers start from the same revision: exactly one may win, the others conflict.
	results := make(chan error, 10)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		go func() {
			_, err := env.svc.WriteFiles(ctx, testHostID, "app", FilesInput{Compose: &FileWrite{Content: "winner\n", Revision: rev}})
			results <- err
		}()
	}
	wins, conflicts := 0, 0
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		switch err := <-results; {
		case err == nil:
			wins++
		case CodeOf(err) == CodeRevisionConflict:
			conflicts++
		default:
			t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if wins != 1 || conflicts != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("wins = %d conflicts = %d, want exactly one writer to succeed", wins, conflicts)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `internal/dockerstacks/fileio.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"archive/tar"
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// File access goes through the Engine's archive API on the parked IO container,
// which works on a container that was never started.
var (
	// errIOContainerGone: the IO container does not exist (the host is not prepared any more).
	errIOContainerGone = errors.New("the Docker Manager IO container is missing")
	// errArchivePathMissing: the path inside the IO container does not exist.
	errArchivePathMissing = errors.New("the path does not exist on the Docker host")
)

func archivePath(p string) string {
	return "containers/" + url.PathEscape(IOContainerName) + "/archive?path=" + url.QueryEscape(p)
}

// archivePathMissing tells the Engine's "Could not find the file ... in
// container ..." 404 from "No such container: ...", which is also a 404. The
// Engine gives no other way to tell them apart.
func archivePathMissing(err error) bool {
	return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(err.Error()), "could not find the file")
}

// classifyArchive maps a 404 of the archive API to a sentinel.
func classifyArchive(err error) error {
	if isNotFound(err) {
		if archivePathMissing(err) {
			return errArchivePathMissing
		}
		return errIOContainerGone
	}
	return err
}

// pathExists asks whether a file or folder exists (HEAD, so nothing is
// transferred: a stack's data folder can hold gigabytes).
func (e engine) pathExists(ctx context.Context, p string) (bool, error) {
	resp, err := e.request(ctx, http.MethodHead, archivePath(p), nil, "", false)
	if err == nil {
		_ = resp.Body.Close()
		return true, nil
	}
	if isNotFound(err) {
		return false, nil
	}
	return false, err
}

// readFile reads one regular file of at most MaxFileBytes. A file that does not
// exist is (nil, false, nil); a larger one is CodeFileTooLarge.
func (e engine) readFile(ctx context.Context, p string) ([]byte, bool, error) {
	resp, err := e.request(ctx, http.MethodGet, archivePath(p), nil, "", false)
	if err != nil {
		classified := classifyArchive(err)
		if errors.Is(classified, errArchivePathMissing) {
			return nil, false, nil
		}
		return nil, false, classified
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	tr := tar.NewReader(resp.Body)
	hdr, err := tr.Next()
	if err == io.EOF {
		return nil, false, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", p, err)
	}
	if hdr.Typeflag != tar.TypeReg {
		return nil, false, newError(CodeStacksDirInvalid, "%s is not a regular file (a link or a folder)", p)
	}
	if hdr.Size > MaxFileBytes {
		return nil, false, tooLarge(p)
	}
	data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(tr, MaxFileBytes+1))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", p, err)
	}
	if len(data) > MaxFileBytes {
		return nil, false, tooLarge(p)
	}
	return data, true, nil
}

func tooLarge(what string) *Error {
	return newError(CodeFileTooLarge, "%s is larger than %d KiB", what, MaxFileBytes>>10)
}

// putArchive extracts a tar into a folder of the host (PUT .../archive). The
// folder must exist.
func (e engine) putArchive(ctx context.Context, dir string, archive []byte) error {
	resp, err := e.request(ctx, http.MethodPut, archivePath(dir)+"&noOverwriteDirNonDir=true", bytes.NewReader(archive), "application/x-tar", false)
	if err != nil {
		return classifyArchive(err)
	}
	return resp.Body.Close()
}

// tarEntry is one entry of the archives AuraGo sends: owned by root, named
// relative to the folder the archive is extracted in.
type tarEntry struct {
	name    string
	dir     bool
	mode    int64
	content []byte
}

// buildTar writes a USTAR archive of the entries, all owned by uid 0 and gid 0.
func buildTar(entries []tarEntry, modTime time.Time) ([]byte, error) {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	tw := tar.NewWriter(&buf)
	for _, entry := range entries {
		hdr := &tar.Header{Name: entry.name, Mode: entry.mode, ModTime: modTime, Format: tar.FormatUSTAR}
		if entry.dir {
			hdr.Typeflag = tar.TypeDir
			hdr.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(entry.name, "/") + "/"
		} else {
			hdr.Typeflag = tar.TypeReg
			hdr.Size = int64(len(entry.content))
		}
		if err := tw.WriteHeader(hdr); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if !entry.dir {
			if _, err := tw.Write(entry.content); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
		}
	}
	if err := tw.Close(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

// File modes of what AuraGo writes: the compose file is readable by anyone, the
// .env, which holds secrets, only by root.
const (
	composeFileMode = 0o644
	envFileMode     = 0o600
	stackDirMode    = 0o755
)
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"path"
	"sort"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// ioGone turns "the IO container does not exist" into the error a read on an
// unprepared host gets, with the current helper status.
func (s *Service) ioGone(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host) error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	delete(s.ready, h.ID)
	s.mu.Unlock()
	st, _, err := s.helpers(ctx, e, h)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return notPreparedError(st)
}

// stackMissing is the error for a stack without a compose file. A HEAD request
// cannot tell a missing file from a missing IO container (both are a bodiless
// 404), so the helpers are checked again before the stack is declared gone.
func (s *Service) stackMissing(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, name string) error {
	st, _, err := s.helpers(ctx, e, h)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !st.Prepared {
		s.mu.Lock()
		delete(s.ready, h.ID)
		s.mu.Unlock()
		return notPreparedError(st)
	}
	return newError(CodeStackNotFound, "there is no stack %q on this host", name)
}

// locateCompose finds the compose file of a stack: the first of
// ComposeFileNames that exists in its folder. "" means the folder has none. The
// name the last folder scan found is tried first.
func (s *Service) locateCompose(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, name string) (string, error) {
	dir := stackDir(h, name)
	var hint string
	if c, ok := s.cachedScan(h.ID); ok {
		hint = c.folders[name].composeFile
	}
	if hint != "" {
		found, err := e.pathExists(ctx, path.Join(dir, hint))
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		if found {
			return hint, nil
		}
	}
	for _, candidate := range ComposeFileNames {
		if candidate == hint {
			continue
		}
		found, err := e.pathExists(ctx, path.Join(dir, candidate))
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		if found {
			return candidate, nil
		}
	}
	return "", nil
}

// readStackFile reads a file of a stack as FileContent.
func (s *Service) readStackFile(ctx context.Context, e engine, h dockerhost.Host, name, file string) (FileContent, error) {
	data, exists, err := e.readFile(ctx, path.Join(stackDir(h, name), file))
	if errors.Is(err, errIOContainerGone) {
		return FileContent{}, s.ioGone(ctx, e, h)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return FileContent{}, err
	}
	if !exists {
		return FileContent{Name: file}, nil
	}
	return FileContent{Name: file, Content: string(data), Revision: Revision(data), Exists: true}, nil
}

// composeService is one service of a compose file.
type composeService struct {
	name  string
	image string
}

// parseComposeServices lists the services of a compose file in file order,
// with the image each one names. A file without a services mapping has none; a
// file that is not valid YAML, or whose top level is not a mapping, is an error.
func parseComposeServices(content []byte) ([]composeService, error) {
	var doc yaml.Node
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(content, &doc); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if doc.Kind != yaml.DocumentNode || len(doc.Content) == 0 {
		return nil, nil
	}
	root := doc.Content[0]
	if root.Kind != yaml.MappingNode {
		return nil, errors.New("the compose file is not a YAML mapping")
	}
	var services []composeService
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(root.Content); i += 2 {
		if root.Content[i].Value != "services" || root.Content[i+1].Kind != yaml.MappingNode {
			continue
		}
		list := root.Content[i+1].Content
		for j := 0; j+1 < len(list); j += 2 {
			svc := composeService{name: list[j].Value}
			if body := list[j+1]; body.Kind == yaml.MappingNode {
				for k := 0; k+1 < len(body.Content); k += 2 {
					if body.Content[k].Value == "image" && body.Content[k+1].Kind == yaml.ScalarNode {
						svc.image = body.Content[k+1].Value
					}
				}
			}
			services = append(services, svc)
		}
	}
	return services, nil
}

// serviceDetail describes one service from its containers: the running one
// when there is one, else the first.
func serviceDetail(name, fileImage string, containers []dockerhost.ContainerSummary) ServiceDetail {
	d := ServiceDetail{Name: name, Image: fileImage, State: "missing", Ports: []PortLink{}}
	if len(containers) == 0 {
		return d
	}
	best := containers[0]
	for _, c := range containers {
		if c.State == "running" {
			best = c
			break
		}
	}
	d.State, d.Health, d.ContainerID = best.State, best.Health, best.ID
	if d.Image == "" {
		d.Image = best.Image
	}
	if code, ok := exitCodeOf(best); ok && best.State == "exited" {
		d.ExitCode = &code
	}
	d.Ports = portLinks(containers)
	return d
}

// serviceList builds the services of a stack: the compose file's services in
// file order first, then the containers of the project that match none of them.
func serviceList(services []composeService, members []dockerhost.ContainerSummary) []ServiceDetail {
	byService := map[string][]dockerhost.ContainerSummary{}
	for _, c := range members {
		byService[c.ComposeService] = append(byService[c.ComposeService], c)
	}
	list := make([]ServiceDetail, 0, len(services)+len(byService))
	known := map[string]bool{}
	for _, svc := range services {
		known[svc.name] = true
		list = append(list, serviceDetail(svc.name, svc.image, byService[svc.name]))
	}
	var stray []string
	for name := range byService {
		if !known[name] {
			stray = append(stray, name)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(stray)
	for _, name := range stray {
		label := name
		if label == "" {
			label = byService[name][0].ID
			if names := byService[name][0].Names; len(names) > 0 {
				label = names[0]
			}
		}
		list = append(list, serviceDetail(label, "", byService[name]))
	}
	return list
}

// Get returns a stack with its compose file, its .env, its services and its
// status. The files are read through the IO container, the status from the
// containers labelled with the project name.
func (s *Service) Get(ctx context.Context, hostID, name string) (StackDetail, error) {
	if err := ValidateName(name); err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	h, e, err := s.target(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	if _, err := s.requirePrepared(ctx, e, h); err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	composeName, err := s.locateCompose(ctx, e, h, name)
	if errors.Is(err, errIOContainerGone) {
		return StackDetail{}, s.ioGone(ctx, e, h)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	if composeName == "" {
		return StackDetail{}, s.stackMissing(ctx, e, h, name)
	}
	compose, err := s.readStackFile(ctx, e, h, name, composeName)
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	env, err := s.readStackFile(ctx, e, h, name, EnvFileName)
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	containers, err := dockerhost.ListContainers(ctx, e.c)
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	members := projectGroups(containers)[name]

	status, count := DeriveStatus(members)
	detail := StackDetail{
		StackSummary: StackSummary{
			Name: name, HostID: h.ID, Dir: stackDir(h, name), ComposeFile: composeName, HasEnv: env.Exists,
			Status: status, Services: count, Ports: portLinks(members), ContainerIDs: shortIDs(members),
			Created: oldestCreated(members),
		},
		Compose: compose,
		Env:     env,
	}
	if ref, ok := s.operationRefs(h.ID)[name]; ok {
		detail.Operation = &ref
	}
	services, parseErr := parseComposeServices([]byte(compose.Content))
	if parseErr != nil {
		detail.ParseError = dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(parseErr.Error(), 300)
		services = nil
	}
	detail.ServiceList = serviceList(services, members)
	return detail, nil
}

// checkSize refuses a file above MaxFileBytes.
func checkSize(file, content string) error {
	if len(content) > MaxFileBytes {
		return tooLarge(file)
	}
	return nil
}

// Create writes a new stack: its folder, compose.yaml and, when in.Env is set,
// .env. A folder that already has a compose file is CodeStackExists; a folder
// without one (leftover data) is used as it is. The stack's status is draft
// until it is deployed.
func (s *Service) Create(ctx context.Context, hostID string, in CreateInput) (StackDetail, error) {
	if err := ValidateName(in.Name); err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	if err := checkSize("the compose file", in.Compose); err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	if in.Env != nil {
		if err := checkSize("the .env file", *in.Env); err != nil {
			return StackDetail{}, err
		}
	}
	h, e, err := s.target(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	if _, err := s.requirePrepared(ctx, e, h); err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	if err := s.refuseWhileDeleting(h.ID, in.Name); err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	lock := s.fileLock(h.ID, in.Name)
	lock.Lock()
	defer lock.Unlock()

	dir := stackDir(h, in.Name)
	dirExists, err := e.pathExists(ctx, dir)
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	if dirExists {
		existing, err := s.locateCompose(ctx, e, h, in.Name)
		if errors.Is(err, errIOContainerGone) {
			return StackDetail{}, s.ioGone(ctx, e, h)
		}
		if err != nil {
			return StackDetail{}, err
		}
		if existing != "" {
			exists := newError(CodeStackExists, "the stack %q already exists on this host", in.Name)
			exists.Err = ErrStackExists
			return StackDetail{}, exists
		}
	}

	files := []tarEntry{{name: ComposeFileNames[0], mode: composeFileMode, content: []byte(in.Compose)}}
	if in.Env != nil {
		files = append(files, tarEntry{name: EnvFileName, mode: envFileMode, content: []byte(*in.Env)})
	}
	extractIn := dir
	if !dirExists {
		// A new folder travels in the archive itself; an existing one keeps its owner and mode.
		extractIn = h.StacksDir
		for i := range files {
			files[i].name = in.Name + "/" + files[i].name
		}
		files = append([]tarEntry{{name: in.Name, dir: true, mode: stackDirMode}}, files...)
	}
	archive, err := buildTar(files, s.opts.Now())
	if err != nil {
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	err = e.putArchive(ctx, extractIn, archive)
	s.invalidateScan(h.ID)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, errIOContainerGone):
		return StackDetail{}, s.ioGone(ctx, e, h)
	case errors.Is(err, errArchivePathMissing):
		return StackDetail{}, newError(CodeStacksDirInvalid, "the stacks directory %s does not exist on the Docker host", h.StacksDir)
	case err != nil:
		return StackDetail{}, err
	}
	return s.Get(ctx, hostID, in.Name)
}

// WriteFiles stores the compose file and/or the .env of an existing stack.
// Every file carries the revision it was edited from; if the file on the host
// has another revision (it changed meanwhile), nothing is written and the
// answer is a *ConflictError with what is on the host now. All files are checked
// before any is written. Writes are refused (BusyError) while a delete runs.
func (s *Service) WriteFiles(ctx context.Context, hostID, name string, in FilesInput) (FileRevisions, error) {
	if err := ValidateName(name); err != nil {
		return FileRevisions{}, err
	}
	if in.Compose == nil && in.Env == nil {
		return FileRevisions{}, newError(CodeInvalidOperation, "the request names no file to write")
	}
	if in.Compose != nil {
		if err := checkSize("the compose file", in.Compose.Content); err != nil {
			return FileRevisions{}, err
		}
	}
	if in.Env != nil {
		if err := checkSize("the .env file", in.Env.Content); err != nil {
			return FileRevisions{}, err
		}
	}
	h, e, err := s.target(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		return FileRevisions{}, err
	}
	if _, err := s.requirePrepared(ctx, e, h); err != nil {
		return FileRevisions{}, err
	}
	if err := s.refuseWhileDeleting(h.ID, name); err != nil {
		return FileRevisions{}, err
	}
	lock := s.fileLock(h.ID, name)
	lock.Lock()
	defer lock.Unlock()

	composeName, err := s.locateCompose(ctx, e, h, name)
	if errors.Is(err, errIOContainerGone) {
		return FileRevisions{}, s.ioGone(ctx, e, h)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return FileRevisions{}, err
	}
	if composeName == "" {
		return FileRevisions{}, s.stackMissing(ctx, e, h, name)
	}

	type pending struct {
		label string
		file  string
		mode  int64
		write *FileWrite
	}
	var writes []pending
	if in.Compose != nil {
		writes = append(writes, pending{"compose", composeName, composeFileMode, in.Compose})
	}
	if in.Env != nil {
		writes = append(writes, pending{"env", EnvFileName, envFileMode, in.Env})
	}
	var entries []tarEntry
	for _, w := range writes {
		current, err := s.readStackFile(ctx, e, h, name, w.file)
		if err != nil {
			return FileRevisions{}, err
		}
		if current.Revision != w.write.Revision {
			return FileRevisions{}, &ConflictError{File: w.label, Current: current}
		}
		entries = append(entries, tarEntry{name: w.file, mode: w.mode, content: []byte(w.write.Content)})
	}
	archive, err := buildTar(entries, s.opts.Now())
	if err != nil {
		return FileRevisions{}, err
	}
	err = e.putArchive(ctx, stackDir(h, name), archive)
	s.invalidateScan(h.ID)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, errIOContainerGone):
		return FileRevisions{}, s.ioGone(ctx, e, h)
	case errors.Is(err, errArchivePathMissing):
		return FileRevisions{}, newError(CodeStackNotFound, "the folder of stack %q is gone", name)
	case err != nil:
		return FileRevisions{}, err
	}
	var revisions FileRevisions
	if in.Compose != nil {
		revisions.Compose = Revision([]byte(in.Compose.Content))
	}
	if in.Env != nil {
		revisions.Env = Revision([]byte(in.Env.Content))
	}
	return revisions, nil
}
```
