The contract named `lint.go`, `lint_test.go`, `convert.go`, `convert_test.go`; the extra files keep every file under 600 lines.

**Deviations from `CONTRACT.md`**

1. **File split** as above (the contract lists only four files).
2. **`--expose`** is converted too (to `expose:`), although the contract's flag list lacks it: it is one of the commonest `docker run` flags and a compose key exists.
3. **`env_syntax` diagnostics carry `.env` line numbers.** The contract's `Diagnostic` has no file field; every code except `env_syntax` refers to the compose file. The diagnostic has `params.file = ".env"` so the UI can route it to the `.env` editor (see the notes for part D below).
4. **`Preview.Variables` is aggregated per name**: `line` = first use, `has_default` = every use names a default, `required` = any use is `${X:?m}` / `${X?m}`, `in_env` = defined in `.env`. One `variable_missing` diagnostic per variable, at the first use that has neither default nor value.
5. **`Preview.NamedVolumes`** lists named volumes that a service uses, that the top-level `volumes:` section declares, and that are not `external`, in order of first use (the key as written, not the `<stack>_<key>` engine name).
6. **Lines are clamped.** A `yaml_syntax` line that yaml.v3 reports behind the last line (unclosed quote at the end) is moved onto the last line, so editors never get a line outside the document.
7. Ports or storage entries that use a variable without a value and without a default (`"${PORT}:80"`) are **not judged** (no `invalid_port`, not in the preview); the `variable_missing` diagnostic covers them.
8. `ConvertWarning.Flag` is the long form with dashes (`--publish`, also for `-p`; `-x` for an unknown short flag) and `command` for the container command.

**Notes for the other parts**

Part C (`internal/server`): call `dockerstacks.Lint(in, published)` and `dockerstacks.ConvertDockerRun(command)`; a convert failure is a `*dockerstacks.Error` with `Code == CodeConvertFailed` (400); both functions are pure and need no host. `Lint` skips the ports of project `in.Stack` itself, so `published` may be the unfiltered list or the one from `PublishedPorts(ctx, hostID, excludeProject)`; when the host cannot be read pass `nil` (no conflicts are reported). Part D (UI): the localized text `lint_<code>` may use these params; show `env_syntax` diagnostics in the `.env` editor (their lines are `.env` lines) and every other code in the compose editor.

| Code | Severity | Params | Position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yaml_syntax` | error | `detail` | line of the YAML error |
| `not_a_mapping` | error | `what` = `document` / `services` / `service` | the offending node |
| `no_services` | error | none | line 0, or the empty `services:` key |
| `service_no_image` | error | `service` | service key |
| `invalid_port` | error | `value`, `reason` | the list item |
| `port_duplicate` | error | `port`, `protocol`, `first_line` | the second item |
| `port_conflict` | warning | `port`, `protocol`, `container`, `project` | the list item |
| `variable_missing` | warning | `variable` (`fix` = `env_random` unless required) | first use |
| `env_syntax` | warning | `file` = `.env`, `detail` (English) | line in `.env` |
| `image_latest`, `image_no_tag` | hint | `image` | the image value |
| `privileged`, `network_mode_host` | hint | none | the key |
| `docker_socket` | hint | `source` | the volume item |
| `restart_missing` | hint | none | service key |
| `cap_add` | hint | `caps` (comma separated) | the key |

Every list in the JSON answer is `[]`, never `null` (tested). `Diagnostic.service` is set for per-service findings.

**Files:**

`lint_types.go` holds the contract types of lint (`LintInput`, `Diagnostic`, `Fix`, `LintResult`, `Preview` and its parts) with their JSON tags. `lint_env.go` reads a `.env` file the way Compose does for the cases that matter (comments, blank lines, `export KEY=VALUE`, quotes, inline comments, quoted values over several lines, a UTF-8 BOM, CRLF) and reports every other line as an `env_syntax` warning. It also holds `interpolate`, the single implementation of Compose's variable syntax (`$$`, `$NAME`, `${NAME}`, `:-`, `-`, `:+`, `+`, `:?`, `?`, nested defaults). Lint (B3) uses it to find variables and to expand ports and volumes; the converter (B5) uses it to judge ports.

```go
package dockerstacks

// LintInput is what the editor sends while typing.
type LintInput struct {
	Compose string `json:"compose"`
	Env     string `json:"env"`
	Stack   string `json:"stack,omitempty"` // its own published ports are not conflicts
}

// Diagnostic is one finding. Lines are 1-based, 0 means the whole file. Every code except env_syntax refers to the
// compose file; env_syntax lines refer to the .env file (Params["file"] is ".env").
type Diagnostic struct {
	Line     int               `json:"line"`
	Column   int               `json:"column,omitempty"`
	Severity string            `json:"severity"` // "error" | "warning" | "hint"
	Code     string            `json:"code"`     // the UI localizes lint_<code>
	Message  string            `json:"message"`  // English fallback
	Params   map[string]string `json:"params,omitempty"`
	Service  string            `json:"service,omitempty"`
	Fix      *Fix              `json:"fix,omitempty"`
}

// Fix is a one-click remedy the UI can offer.
type Fix struct {
	Kind     string `json:"kind"` // "env_random": add VARIABLE=<random> to .env
	Variable string `json:"variable"`
}

// LintResult is the answer of Lint.
type LintResult struct {
	Diagnostics []Diagnostic `json:"diagnostics"` // sorted by line, then severity
	Preview     Preview      `json:"preview"`
}

// Preview is what the new-stack screen shows next to the editor.
type Preview struct {
	Services     []ServicePreview  `json:"services"`
	NamedVolumes []string          `json:"named_volumes"` // volumes compose will create
	Variables    []VariablePreview `json:"variables"`
}

type ServicePreview struct {
	Name    string          `json:"name"`
	Line    int             `json:"line"`
	Image   string          `json:"image,omitempty"`
	Build   bool            `json:"build,omitempty"`
	Ports   []PortPreview   `json:"ports"`
	Volumes []VolumePreview `json:"volumes"`
}

type PortPreview struct {
	HostIP    string `json:"host_ip,omitempty"`
	Host      string `json:"host"`      // "8080", "8000-8010" or "" (not published)
	Container string `json:"container"` // "80" or "8000-8010"
	Protocol  string `json:"protocol"`
	Conflict  string `json:"conflict,omitempty"` // container already publishing the host port
}

type VolumePreview struct {
	Kind     string `json:"kind"` // "named" | "bind" | "relative" | "anonymous" | "tmpfs"
	Source   string `json:"source,omitempty"`
	Target   string `json:"target"`
	ReadOnly bool   `json:"read_only,omitempty"`
}

// VariablePreview describes one variable of the compose file. Line is its first use; HasDefault is true when every
// use names a default; Required when any use is ${X:?msg} / ${X?msg}; InEnv when .env defines it.
type VariablePreview struct {
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	Line       int    `json:"line"`
	HasDefault bool   `json:"has_default"`
	Required   bool   `json:"required"`
	InEnv      bool   `json:"in_env"`
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/lint_env.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// problemOpenQuote marks a value whose opening quote is never closed; such a line defines nothing.
const problemOpenQuote = "the quote is never closed"

// envKeyPattern is what a .env key may look like (Compose's reader is a little wider than interpolation itself).
var envKeyPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`)

// parseEnvFile reads a .env file the way Compose does for the cases that matter to lint: comments, blank lines,
// `export KEY=VALUE`, unquoted values (an inline " #" starts a comment), single-quoted values (literal), double-quoted
// values (a few escapes, may span lines). It returns the defined variables and one env_syntax warning per line that
// is not KEY=VALUE. A later definition of a key replaces an earlier one.
func parseEnvFile(src string) (map[string]string, []Diagnostic) {
	env := map[string]string{}
	diags := []Diagnostic{}
	src = strings.TrimPrefix(src, "\xef\xbb\xbf") // UTF-8 byte order mark
	lines := strings.Split(strings.ReplaceAll(src, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n")
	warn := func(line int, detail string) {
		diags = append(diags, Diagnostic{
			Line: line, Severity: "warning", Code: "env_syntax",
			Message: ".env line " + strconv.Itoa(line) + " is not KEY=VALUE, a comment or blank: " + detail,
			Params:  map[string]string{"file": ".env", "detail": detail},
		})
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(lines); i++ {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
		if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "export ") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "export\t") {
			line = strings.TrimLeft(line[len("export"):], " \t")
		}
		eq := strings.IndexByte(line, '=')
		if eq < 0 {
			warn(i+1, "there is no '=' after the name")
			continue
		}
		key := strings.TrimSpace(line[:eq])
		if !envKeyPattern.MatchString(key) {
			warn(i+1, "invalid variable name")
			continue
		}
		value, extra, problem := parseEnvValue(strings.TrimLeft(line[eq+1:], " \t"), lines[i+1:])
		if problem != "" {
			warn(i+1, problem)
		}
		if problem != problemOpenQuote {
			env[key] = value
		}
		i += extra
	}
	return env, diags
}

// parseEnvValue parses the text after "KEY=". following holds the lines after the current one, which a
// double- or single-quoted value may continue into; extra is how many of them were consumed.
func parseEnvValue(rest string, following []string) (value string, extra int, problem string) {
	if rest == "" {
		return "", 0, ""
	}
	q := rest[0]
	if q != '"' && q != '\'' {
		for k := 1; k < len(rest); k++ {
			if rest[k] == '#' && (rest[k-1] == ' ' || rest[k-1] == '\t') {
				rest = rest[:k] // an inline comment starts at a "#" that follows a blank
				break
			}
		}
		return strings.TrimSpace(rest), 0, ""
	}
	body := rest[1:]
	for n := 0; ; n++ {
		if end := closingQuote(body, q); end >= 0 {
			tail := strings.TrimSpace(body[end+1:])
			if tail != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(tail, "#") {
				problem = "unexpected text after the closing quote"
			}
			text := body[:end]
			if q == '"' {
				text = unescapeDoubleQuoted(text)
			}
			return text, n, problem
		}
		if n >= len(following) {
			return "", 0, problemOpenQuote
		}
		body += "\n" + strings.TrimSuffix(following[n], "\r")
	}
}

// closingQuote returns the index of the first unescaped q in s, or -1.
func closingQuote(s string, q byte) int {
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		switch {
		case s[i] == '\\' && q == '"':
			i++
		case s[i] == q:
			return i
		}
	}
	return -1
}

var doubleQuotedEscapes = strings.NewReplacer(`\n`, "\n", `\r`, "\r", `\t`, "\t", `\"`, `"`, `\\`, `\`, `\$`, `$`)

func unescapeDoubleQuoted(s string) string { return doubleQuotedEscapes.Replace(s) }

// varRef is one use of a Compose variable that interpolate saw.
type varRef struct {
	Name     string
	Default  bool // ${X:-d} ${X-d} ${X:+r} ${X+r}: the file says what happens when X is unset
	Required bool // ${X:?msg} ${X?msg}
	Set      bool // X has a value for this operator (non-empty for the ":" forms)
}

func isNameStart(c byte) bool { return c == '_' || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') }
func isNameChar(c byte) bool  { return isNameStart(c) || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') }

// interpolate expands Compose variable syntax in s from env: "$$" is a literal dollar, $NAME and ${NAME} are
// substituted, ${NAME:-d} ${NAME-d} ${NAME:+r} ${NAME+r} ${NAME:?m} ${NAME?m} follow Compose's rules and may nest.
// visit (optional) is told about every variable that is actually evaluated. unresolved reports that a variable
// without a default had no value, so the result is not what Compose would deploy. Text that is not valid
// variable syntax stays as it is.
func interpolate(s string, env map[string]string, visit func(varRef)) (out string, unresolved bool) {
	var b strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < len(s); {
		c := s[i]
		if c != '$' || i+1 >= len(s) {
			b.WriteByte(c)
			i++
			continue
		}
		next := s[i+1]
		switch {
		case next == '$':
			b.WriteByte('$')
			i += 2
		case next == '{':
			end := matchBrace(s, i+1)
			if end < 0 {
				b.WriteString(s[i:])
				return b.String(), unresolved
			}
			text, unres, ok := expandBraced(s[i+2:end], env, visit)
			if !ok {
				text = s[i : end+1]
			}
			b.WriteString(text)
			unresolved = unresolved || unres
			i = end + 1
		case isNameStart(next):
			j := i + 2
			for j < len(s) && isNameChar(s[j]) {
				j++
			}
			val, set := env[s[i+1:j]]
			if visit != nil {
				visit(varRef{Name: s[i+1 : j], Set: set})
			}
			unresolved = unresolved || !set
			b.WriteString(val)
			i = j
		default:
			b.WriteByte(c)
			i++
		}
	}
	return b.String(), unresolved
}

// matchBrace returns the index of the "}" that closes the "{" at s[open], or -1.
func matchBrace(s string, open int) int {
	depth := 0
	for i := open; i < len(s); i++ {
		switch s[i] {
		case '$':
			if i+1 < len(s) && s[i+1] == '$' {
				i++
			}
		case '{':
			depth++
		case '}':
			depth--
			if depth == 0 {
				return i
			}
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// expandBraced expands the inside of ${...}. ok is false when the text is not valid variable syntax.
func expandBraced(body string, env map[string]string, visit func(varRef)) (text string, unresolved, ok bool) {
	if body == "" || !isNameStart(body[0]) {
		return "", false, false
	}
	n := 1
	for n < len(body) && isNameChar(body[n]) {
		n++
	}
	name, op := body[:n], body[n:]
	val, defined := env[name]
	report := func(r varRef) {
		r.Name = name
		if visit != nil {
			visit(r)
		}
	}
	sub := func(arg string) (string, bool) { return interpolate(arg, env, visit) }
	switch {
	case op == "":
		report(varRef{Set: defined})
		return val, !defined, true
	case strings.HasPrefix(op, ":-"), strings.HasPrefix(op, "-"):
		colon := op[0] == ':'
		set := defined && (!colon || val != "")
		report(varRef{Default: true, Set: set})
		if set {
			return val, false, true
		}
		d, unres := sub(op[strings.IndexByte(op, '-')+1:])
		return d, unres, true
	case strings.HasPrefix(op, ":+"), strings.HasPrefix(op, "+"):
		colon := op[0] == ':'
		set := defined && (!colon || val != "")
		report(varRef{Default: true, Set: set})
		if !set {
			return "", false, true
		}
		r, unres := sub(op[strings.IndexByte(op, '+')+1:])
		return r, unres, true
	case strings.HasPrefix(op, ":?"), strings.HasPrefix(op, "?"):
		colon := op[0] == ':'
		set := defined && (!colon || val != "")
		report(varRef{Required: true, Set: set})
		return val, !set, true
	}
	return "", false, false
}
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// portSpec is one published (or only exposed) port binding of a service, after variable expansion.
type portSpec struct {
	HostIP         string
	HostLo, HostHi int // 0 = not published (the engine picks a port)
	CtrLo, CtrHi   int
	Protocol       string // tcp | udp | sctp
}

func (p portSpec) hostText() string      { return rangeText(p.HostLo, p.HostHi) }
func (p portSpec) containerText() string { return rangeText(p.CtrLo, p.CtrHi) }

// fixedHostPorts is true when every host port is chosen by the file (no host range that the engine allocates from).
func (p portSpec) fixedHostPorts() bool {
	return p.HostLo != 0 && (p.HostHi-p.HostLo == p.CtrHi-p.CtrLo)
}

func rangeText(lo, hi int) string {
	switch {
	case lo == 0:
		return ""
	case lo == hi:
		return strconv.Itoa(lo)
	}
	return strconv.Itoa(lo) + "-" + strconv.Itoa(hi)
}

// parsePortRange reads "80" or "8000-8010" (1..65535, low <= high).
func parsePortRange(s string) (lo, hi int, err error) {
	a, b, isRange := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(s), "-")
	if lo, err = parsePortNumber(a); err != nil {
		return 0, 0, err
	}
	if !isRange {
		return lo, lo, nil
	}
	if hi, err = parsePortNumber(b); err != nil {
		return 0, 0, err
	}
	if hi < lo {
		return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("the range %q runs backwards", s)
	}
	return lo, hi, nil
}

func parsePortNumber(s string) (int, error) {
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
	if err != nil || strconv.Itoa(n) != s {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("%q is not a port number", s)
	}
	if n < 1 || n > 65535 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("port %d is outside 1-65535", n)
	}
	return n, nil
}

// newPortSpec assembles and validates a binding from its textual parts (short and long syntax share it).
// published may be empty (not published), container may be a range.
func newPortSpec(hostIP, published, container, protocol string) (portSpec, error) {
	p := portSpec{HostIP: strings.TrimSpace(hostIP), Protocol: strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(protocol))}
	if p.Protocol == "" {
		p.Protocol = "tcp"
	}
	switch p.Protocol {
	case "tcp", "udp", "sctp":
	default:
		return portSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown protocol %q (use tcp, udp or sctp)", protocol)
	}
	if p.HostIP != "" && net.ParseIP(p.HostIP) == nil {
		return portSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("%q is not an IP address", p.HostIP)
	}
	var err error
	if p.CtrLo, p.CtrHi, err = parsePortRange(container); err != nil {
		return portSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("container port: %w", err)
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(published) != "" {
		if p.HostLo, p.HostHi, err = parsePortRange(published); err != nil {
			return portSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("published port: %w", err)
		}
		// A host range may feed a single container port (the engine picks one); otherwise both must match.
		if p.CtrHi != p.CtrLo && p.HostHi-p.HostLo != p.CtrHi-p.CtrLo {
			return portSpec{}, errors.New("the host and container port ranges differ in length")
		}
	}
	return p, nil
}

// parsePortSpec reads the short syntax [[HOST_IP:](HOST_PORT[-RANGE]):]CONTAINER_PORT[-RANGE][/PROTOCOL].
func parsePortSpec(raw string) (portSpec, error) {
	s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
	if s == "" {
		return portSpec{}, errors.New("the port is empty")
	}
	proto := ""
	if i := strings.LastIndexByte(s, '/'); i >= 0 {
		proto, s = s[i+1:], s[:i]
	}
	ip, rest := "", s
	bracketed := strings.HasPrefix(s, "[")
	if bracketed {
		end := strings.IndexByte(s, ']')
		if end < 0 || !strings.HasPrefix(s[end+1:], ":") {
			return portSpec{}, errors.New("an IPv6 address needs the form [::1]:HOST:CONTAINER")
		}
		ip, rest = s[1:end], s[end+2:]
	}
	parts := strings.Split(rest, ":")
	switch {
	case bracketed && len(parts) == 2: // [::1]:8080:80
		return newPortSpec(ip, parts[0], parts[1], proto)
	case bracketed:
		return portSpec{}, errors.New("an IPv6 address needs the form [::1]:HOST:CONTAINER")
	case len(parts) == 1:
		return newPortSpec("", "", parts[0], proto)
	case len(parts) == 2:
		return newPortSpec("", parts[0], parts[1], proto)
	case len(parts) == 3:
		return newPortSpec(parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], proto)
	}
	return portSpec{}, errors.New("too many ':' separated parts")
}

// isWildcardIP is true for the addresses that mean "every interface".
func isWildcardIP(ip string) bool { return ip == "" || ip == "0.0.0.0" || ip == "::" }

// ipsOverlap reports whether two bind addresses can both want the same host port.
func ipsOverlap(a, b string) bool { return isWildcardIP(a) || isWildcardIP(b) || a == b }

// volumeSpec is one storage entry of a service, after variable expansion.
type volumeSpec struct {
	Kind     string // named | bind | relative | anonymous | tmpfs
	Source   string
	Target   string
	ReadOnly bool
}

var volumeNamePattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`)

// volumeKind classifies a volume source the way Compose does: paths start with "/", "~", "." or a drive letter,
// everything else is a named volume.
func volumeKind(source string) (string, error) {
	switch {
	case source == "":
		return "anonymous", nil
	case strings.HasPrefix(source, "."):
		return "relative", nil
	case strings.HasPrefix(source, "/"), strings.HasPrefix(source, "~"), strings.HasPrefix(source, `\\`), isDrivePath(source):
		return "bind", nil
	case volumeNamePattern.MatchString(source):
		return "named", nil
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is neither a path nor a volume name", source)
}

func isDrivePath(s string) bool {
	return len(s) >= 3 && ((s[0] >= 'a' && s[0] <= 'z') || (s[0] >= 'A' && s[0] <= 'Z')) && s[1] == ':' && (s[2] == '\\' || s[2] == '/')
}

// parseVolumeShort reads SOURCE:TARGET[:MODE], a lone TARGET (anonymous volume), including Windows drive paths.
func parseVolumeShort(raw string) (volumeSpec, error) {
	s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
	parts := strings.Split(s, ":")
	if len(parts) > 1 && isDrivePath(parts[0]+":"+parts[1]) {
		parts = append([]string{parts[0] + ":" + parts[1]}, parts[2:]...)
	}
	var v volumeSpec
	switch len(parts) {
	case 1:
		v.Target = parts[0]
	case 2, 3:
		v.Source, v.Target = parts[0], parts[1]
		if len(parts) == 3 {
			for _, m := range strings.Split(parts[2], ",") {
				v.ReadOnly = v.ReadOnly || m == "ro"
			}
		}
		if v.Source == "" {
			return volumeSpec{}, errors.New("the source is empty")
		}
	default:
		return volumeSpec{}, errors.New("too many ':' separated parts")
	}
	if v.Target == "" {
		return volumeSpec{}, errors.New("the target is empty")
	}
	var err error
	v.Kind, err = volumeKind(v.Source)
	return v, err
}

// volumeFromLong builds a volumeSpec from the long syntax fields.
func volumeFromLong(typ, source, target string, readOnly bool) (volumeSpec, error) {
	if target == "" {
		return volumeSpec{}, errors.New("the target is empty")
	}
	v := volumeSpec{Source: source, Target: target, ReadOnly: readOnly}
	switch typ {
	case "tmpfs":
		v.Kind, v.Source = "tmpfs", ""
	case "bind", "npipe":
		kind, err := volumeKind(source)
		if err != nil || kind == "named" || kind == "anonymous" {
			if err == nil {
				err = errors.New("a bind mount needs a path as its source")
			}
			return volumeSpec{}, err
		}
		v.Kind = kind
	default: // "volume", "image", "cluster" or unset
		if source == "" {
			v.Kind = "anonymous"
		} else if volumeNamePattern.MatchString(source) {
			v.Kind = "named"
		} else {
			return volumeSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("%q is not a volume name", source)
		}
	}
	return v, nil
}
```

### Task B3: `Lint`

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/yamlnode.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/lint.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/lint_test.go`

`Lint(in LintInput, published []PublishedPort) LintResult` parses the compose file into `yaml.Node`s, so every diagnostic carries the line (and column) of the node it is about. It never blocks anything:

- A YAML error returns only `yaml_syntax` (with the line from yaml.v3, clamped into the document) plus the `.env` warnings; the structural checks need a tree.
- Structure: `not_a_mapping`, `no_services`, `service_no_image` (neither `image` nor `build`; a service with `extends` is exempt). YAML anchors and `<<` merge keys are followed (bounded, see `TestLintSurvivesAMergeKeyBomb`).
- Ports (short and long syntax): `invalid_port`, `port_duplicate` (same host port, protocol and overlapping bind address twice in the file), `port_conflict` against `published` (ports of project `in.Stack` are skipped). The preview marks the conflicting container.
- Variables: every `${VAR}` in a scalar (comments are not scanned) that has no default and no value in `.env` gives one `variable_missing` warning with the `env_random` fix, except `${VAR:?msg}` (no fix).
- Hints: `image_latest`, `image_no_tag` (not for `build` services, variables or digests), `privileged`, `docker_socket`, `network_mode_host`, `restart_missing` (not with `restart`, `deploy.restart_policy` or `extends`), `cap_add`.
- Sorting: by line, then severity (error, warning, hint), then column.

`yamlnode.go` holds the small node helpers: alias resolution, mapping access that follows `<<`, sequence and scalar accessors, and `walkScalars`.

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// diagKeys lists the diagnostics as "line:code" in result order.
func diagKeys(res LintResult) []string {
	out := []string{}
	for _, d := range res.Diagnostics {
		out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%d:%s", d.Line, d.Code))
	}
	return out
}

func findDiag(t *testing.T, res LintResult, code string, line int) Diagnostic {
	t.Helper()
	for _, d := range res.Diagnostics {
		if d.Code == code && d.Line == line {
			return d
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no %s diagnostic at line %d in %v", code, line, diagKeys(res))
	return Diagnostic{}
}

const cleanCompose = `services:
  web:
    image: nginx:1.27
    restart: unless-stopped
`

		{"root is a list", "- a\n- b\n", "", []string{"1:not_a_mapping"}},
		{"no services key", "name: demo\n", "", []string{"0:no_services"}},

		{"errors sort before hints on one line", "services:\n  web:\n    cpus: 1\n", "", []string{"2:service_no_image", "2:restart_missing"}},

  f:
    image: app:latest
    build: .
    restart: always
`, "", []string{"3:image_no_tag", "12:image_no_tag", "15:variable_missing"}},
		{"invalid ports", `services:
  web:
    image: nginx:1.27
    restart: always

      - target: 80
        published: 8080

`, "", []string{"6:invalid_port", "7:invalid_port", "8:invalid_port", "11:invalid_port"}},
		{"same host port twice", `services:

`, "", []string{"11:port_duplicate"}},
		{"wildcard and address overlap", "services:\n  web:\n    image: nginx:1.27\n    restart: always\n    ports:\n      - \"9090:80\"\n      - \"192.168.1.5:9090:81\"\n",
			"", []string{"7:port_duplicate"}},
		{"variables", `services:

    image: mysql:8
    restart: always

`, "PRESENT=1\nEMPTY=\n", []string{"6:variable_missing", "7:variable_missing", "10:variable_missing", "15:variable_missing"}},
		{"values from .env count as set", "services:\n  db:\n    image: mysql:8\n    restart: always\n    environment:\n      P: ${DB_ROOT}\n",

		{"anchors and merge keys", `x-base: &base

	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {

func TestLintVariableFixes(t *testing.T) {
	compose := "services:\n  db:\n    image: mysql:8\n    restart: always\n    environment:\n      A: ${DB_ROOT}\n      B: ${API_KEY:?set it}\n      C: ${EMPTY:?x}\n"
	res := Lint(LintInput{Compose: compose, Env: "EMPTY=\n"}, nil)
	if d := findDiag(t, res, "variable_missing", 6); d.Severity != "warning" || d.Fix == nil || d.Fix.Kind != "env_random" || d.Fix.Variable != "DB_ROOT" || d.Params["variable"] != "DB_ROOT" {
		t.Fatalf("DB_ROOT diagnostic = %+v, want a warning with the env_random fix", d)
	}
	if d := findDiag(t, res, "variable_missing", 7); d.Fix != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a required variable must not offer a random value, got %+v", d.Fix)
	}
	if d := findDiag(t, res, "variable_missing", 8); d.Fix != nil {
		t.Fatalf("an empty required variable must not offer a random value, got %+v", d.Fix)
	}
	want := []VariablePreview{
		{Name: "DB_ROOT", Line: 6},
		{Name: "API_KEY", Line: 7, Required: true},
		{Name: "EMPTY", Line: 8, Required: true, InEnv: true},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(res.Preview.Variables, want) {
		t.Fatalf("variables = %+v, want %+v", res.Preview.Variables, want)
	}
}

func TestLintPortConflicts(t *testing.T) {
	published := []PublishedPort{
		{HostIP: "0.0.0.0", Port: 8080, Protocol: "tcp", Container: "grafana", Project: "mon"},
		{HostIP: "127.0.0.1", Port: 9090, Protocol: "tcp", Container: "prom", Project: "mon"},
		{Port: 5353, Protocol: "udp", Container: "dns"},
	}
	compose := `services:
  web:
    image: nginx:1.27
    restart: always
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
      - "9090:80"
      - "5353:53/udp"
      - "5353:53"
      - "192.168.1.5:9091:80"
`
	conflicts := func(res LintResult) []string {
		var out []string
		for _, p := range res.Preview.Services[0].Ports {
			out = append(out, p.Host+"="+p.Conflict)
		}
		return out
	}
	res := Lint(LintInput{Compose: compose}, published)
	if got, want := diagKeys(res), []string{"6:port_conflict", "7:port_conflict", "8:port_conflict"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("diagnostics = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := conflicts(res), []string{"8080=grafana", "9090=prom", "5353=dns", "5353=", "9091="}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("conflicts = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	d := findDiag(t, res, "port_conflict", 6)
	if d.Severity != "warning" || d.Service != "web" || d.Params["container"] != "grafana" || d.Params["project"] != "mon" || d.Params["port"] != "8080" {
		t.Fatalf("conflict diagnostic = %+v", d)
	}

	own := Lint(LintInput{Compose: compose, Stack: "mon"}, published)
	if got, want := diagKeys(own), []string{"8:port_conflict"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("with Stack=mon the ports of project mon are not conflicts: diagnostics = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
}

	compose := `services:

`

	want := Preview{

					{Kind: "relative", Source: "./init", Target: "/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d", ReadOnly: true},

	if !reflect.DeepEqual(res.Preview, want) {
		got, _ := json.MarshalIndent(res.Preview, "", " ")
		exp, _ := json.MarshalIndent(want, "", " ")
		t.Fatalf("preview =\n%s\nwant\n%s", got, exp)
	}
}

func TestLintJSONHasNoNullLists(t *testing.T) {
	raw, err := json.Marshal(Lint(LintInput{Compose: "services:\n  web:\n    image: nginx:1.27\n    restart: always\n"}, nil))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	text := string(raw)
	for _, want := range []string{`"diagnostics":[]`, `"named_volumes":[]`, `"variables":[]`, `"ports":[]`, `"volumes":[]`} {
		if !strings.Contains(text, want) {
			t.Fatalf("lint JSON %s lacks %s", text, want)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(text, "null") {
		t.Fatalf("lint JSON must not contain null lists: %s", text)
	}
	empty, _ := json.Marshal(Lint(LintInput{}, nil))
	if strings.Contains(string(empty), "null") {
		t.Fatalf("lint JSON of an empty file must not contain null lists: %s", empty)
	}
}

func TestLintSurvivesAMergeKeyBomb(t *testing.T) {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("x0: &x0 {image: nginx:1.27}\n")
	for i := 1; i <= 12; i++ {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "x%d: &x%d {<<: [%s]}\n", i, i, strings.TrimSuffix(strings.Repeat(fmt.Sprintf("*x%d, ", i-1), 10), ", "))
	}
	b.WriteString("services:\n  web:\n    <<: *x12\n")
	start := time.Now()
	res := Lint(LintInput{Compose: b.String()}, nil)
	if elapsed := time.Since(start); elapsed > 5*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("lint took %v on a merge-key bomb", elapsed)
	}
	if len(res.Preview.Services) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("services = %+v, want the one service", res.Preview.Services)
	}
}
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import "gopkg.in/yaml.v3"

// maxAliasDepth and maxMergedPairs bound alias and merge-key chains so a hostile file ("billion laughs" built from
// <<: [*a, *a, ...]) cannot make the walkers loop or explode.
const (
	maxAliasDepth  = 8
	maxMergedPairs = 10000
)

// yamlPair is one key/value pair of a mapping node.
type yamlPair struct{ Key, Value *yaml.Node }

// resolveAlias follows alias nodes to the node they point at.
func resolveAlias(n *yaml.Node) *yaml.Node {
	for i := 0; n != nil && n.Kind == yaml.AliasNode && i < maxAliasDepth; i++ {
		n = n.Alias
	}
	return n
}

// mapPairs returns the pairs of a mapping node: its own keys first, then the keys that "<<" merges in (an own key
// wins over a merged one). Aliases are resolved. A node that is not a mapping yields nil.
func mapPairs(n *yaml.Node) []yamlPair {
	budget := maxMergedPairs
	return collectPairs(n, 0, &budget)
}

func collectPairs(n *yaml.Node, depth int, budget *int) []yamlPair {
	n = resolveAlias(n)
	if n == nil || n.Kind != yaml.MappingNode || depth > maxAliasDepth || *budget <= 0 {
		return nil
	}
	*budget -= len(n.Content) / 2
	var own []yamlPair
	var merges []*yaml.Node
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(n.Content); i += 2 {
		k, v := n.Content[i], n.Content[i+1]
		if k.Kind == yaml.ScalarNode && (k.Tag == "!!merge" || (k.Value == "<<" && k.Style == 0)) {
			merges = append(merges, v)
			continue
		}
		own = append(own, yamlPair{k, resolveAlias(v)})
		seen[k.Value] = true
	}
	for _, m := range merges {
		sources := []*yaml.Node{m}
		if r := resolveAlias(m); r != nil && r.Kind == yaml.SequenceNode {
			sources = r.Content
		}
		for _, src := range sources {
			for _, p := range collectPairs(src, depth+1, budget) {
				if !seen[p.Key.Value] {
					seen[p.Key.Value] = true
					own = append(own, p)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return own
}

// mapGet returns the key and (alias-resolved) value node of key in a mapping.
func mapGet(n *yaml.Node, key string) (k, v *yaml.Node) {
	for _, p := range mapPairs(n) {
		if p.Key.Kind == yaml.ScalarNode && p.Key.Value == key {
			return p.Key, p.Value
		}
	}
	return nil, nil
}

// mapValue is mapGet without the key node.
func mapValue(n *yaml.Node, key string) *yaml.Node {
	_, v := mapGet(n, key)
	return v
}

// seqItems returns the alias-resolved items of a sequence node, nil for anything else.
func seqItems(n *yaml.Node) []*yaml.Node {
	n = resolveAlias(n)
	if n == nil || n.Kind != yaml.SequenceNode {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]*yaml.Node, 0, len(n.Content))
	for _, c := range n.Content {
		if r := resolveAlias(c); r != nil {
			out = append(out, r)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// scalarText returns the text of a scalar node and whether n is a non-null scalar.
func scalarText(n *yaml.Node) (string, bool) {
	n = resolveAlias(n)
	if n == nil || n.Kind != yaml.ScalarNode || n.Tag == "!!null" {
		return "", false
	}
	return n.Value, true
}

// scalarBool reports whether n is the boolean true: a YAML bool that decodes to true or the quoted string "true".
// Other spellings ("yes", "on") are not guessed.
func scalarBool(n *yaml.Node) bool {
	n = resolveAlias(n)
	if n == nil || n.Kind != yaml.ScalarNode {
		return false
	}
	var b bool
	if n.Tag == "!!bool" {
		return n.Decode(&b) == nil && b
	}
	return n.Value == "true"
}

// walkScalars calls fn for every scalar node below n in document order (keys and values). Alias nodes are not
// followed, so an anchored value is visited once, where it is defined.
func walkScalars(n *yaml.Node, fn func(*yaml.Node)) {
	if n == nil {
		return
	}
	switch n.Kind {
	case yaml.ScalarNode:
		fn(n)
	case yaml.DocumentNode, yaml.MappingNode, yaml.SequenceNode:
		for _, c := range n.Content {
			walkScalars(c, fn)
		}
	}
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/lint.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

const (
	sevError   = "error"
	sevWarning = "warning"
	sevHint    = "hint"

	maxLintedPortRange = 4096 // host ports checked per binding; a range wider than this is only checked at its start
)

type portKey struct {
	port  int
	proto string
}

type portUse struct {
	ip   string
	line int
}

type varUse struct {
	preview     VariablePreview
	allDefault  bool
	missing     bool // some use has no default and no value
	missingReq  bool // ... and one of those uses is required
	missingLine int
	missingCol  int
}

type linter struct {
	env       map[string]string
	stack     string
	published []PublishedPort
	diags     []Diagnostic
	preview   Preview

	vars      map[string]*varUse
	varOrder  []string
	ports     map[portKey][]portUse
	usedNamed []string
	declared  map[string]bool // top-level volumes: name -> created by compose (not external)
}

// Lint checks a compose file and its .env without touching an engine. It never blocks anything: a YAML error stops
// the structural checks but still returns the syntax diagnostic with its line. published are the ports other
// containers publish on the host; the ports of project in.Stack are not conflicts.
func Lint(in LintInput, published []PublishedPort) LintResult {
	env, diags := parseEnvFile(in.Env)
	l := &linter{
		env: env, stack: in.Stack, published: published, diags: diags,
		preview:  Preview{Services: []ServicePreview{}, NamedVolumes: []string{}, Variables: []VariablePreview{}},
		vars:     map[string]*varUse{},
		ports:    map[portKey][]portUse{},
		declared: map[string]bool{},
	}
	var doc yaml.Node
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(in.Compose), &doc); err != nil {
		line, detail := yamlErrorDetails(err)
		if last := strings.Count(in.Compose, "\n") + 1; line > last {
			line = last // an error at the end of the stream may name the line after the last one
		}
		l.diags = append(l.diags, Diagnostic{
			Line: line, Severity: sevError, Code: "yaml_syntax",
			Message: "YAML syntax error: " + detail, Params: map[string]string{"detail": detail},
		})
	} else {
		l.checkDocument(&doc)
	}
	sort.SliceStable(l.diags, func(i, j int) bool {
		a, b := l.diags[i], l.diags[j]
		if a.Line != b.Line {
			return a.Line < b.Line
		}
		if ra, rb := severityRank(a.Severity), severityRank(b.Severity); ra != rb {
			return ra < rb
		}
		return a.Column < b.Column
	})
	return LintResult{Diagnostics: l.diags, Preview: l.preview}
}

func severityRank(s string) int {
	switch s {
	case sevError:
		return 0
	case sevWarning:
		return 1
	}
	return 2
}

var yamlErrorLine = regexp.MustCompile(`^line (\d+):\s*(.*)$`)

// yamlErrorDetails splits a yaml.v3 error ("yaml: line 3: did not find expected key") into line and text.
func yamlErrorDetails(err error) (line int, detail string) {
	msg := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(err.Error(), "yaml: "), "unmarshal errors:"))
	msg, _, _ = strings.Cut(msg, "\n")
	if m := yamlErrorLine.FindStringSubmatch(strings.TrimSpace(msg)); m != nil {
		line, _ = strconv.Atoi(m[1])
		return line, m[2]
	}
	return 0, msg
}

// add records a diagnostic positioned at node n (nil = whole file).
func (l *linter) add(n *yaml.Node, svc, severity, code, message string, params map[string]string) {
	d := Diagnostic{Severity: severity, Code: code, Message: message, Params: params, Service: svc}
	if n != nil {
		d.Line, d.Column = n.Line, n.Column
	}
	l.diags = append(l.diags, d)
}

func nonNull(n *yaml.Node) bool { return n != nil && !(n.Kind == yaml.ScalarNode && n.Tag == "!!null") }

func (l *linter) checkDocument(doc *yaml.Node) {
	var top *yaml.Node // an empty file or one with only comments decodes to a zero node
	if doc.Kind == yaml.DocumentNode && len(doc.Content) > 0 {
		top = resolveAlias(doc.Content[0])
	}
	if !nonNull(top) {
		l.add(nil, "", sevError, "no_services", "The compose file has no services.", nil)
		return
	}
	if top.Kind != yaml.MappingNode {
		l.add(top, "", sevError, "not_a_mapping", "The compose file must be a mapping with a services key.",
			map[string]string{"what": "document"})
		return
	}
	l.collectVariables(top)
	l.collectDeclaredVolumes(top)
	sk, sv := mapGet(top, "services")
	switch {
	case sk == nil:
		l.add(nil, "", sevError, "no_services", "The compose file has no services.", nil)
	case !nonNull(sv) || (sv.Kind == yaml.MappingNode && len(sv.Content) == 0):
		l.add(sk, "", sevError, "no_services", "The services section is empty.", nil)
	case sv.Kind != yaml.MappingNode:
		l.add(sv, "", sevError, "not_a_mapping", "services must be a mapping of service names.",
			map[string]string{"what": "services"})
	default:
		for _, p := range mapPairs(sv) {
			l.checkService(p.Key, p.Value)
		}
	}
	l.finishPreview()
}

func (l *linter) collectDeclaredVolumes(top *yaml.Node) {
	_, vols := mapGet(top, "volumes")
	for _, p := range mapPairs(vols) {
		_, ext := mapGet(p.Value, "external")
		l.declared[p.Key.Value] = !nonNull(ext) || !(ext.Kind == yaml.MappingNode || scalarBool(ext))
	}
}

// collectVariables finds every ${VAR} use in the document's scalars (comments are not nodes, so they are skipped).
func (l *linter) collectVariables(top *yaml.Node) {
	walkScalars(top, func(n *yaml.Node) {
		if !strings.Contains(n.Value, "$") {
			return
		}
		if n.Style&(yaml.LiteralStyle|yaml.FoldedStyle) != 0 {
			for i, text := range strings.Split(n.Value, "\n") { // a block scalar's text starts on the line after the header
				interpolate(text, l.env, l.recordVar(n.Line+1+i, 0))
			}
			return
		}
		interpolate(n.Value, l.env, l.recordVar(n.Line, n.Column))
	})
}

func (l *linter) recordVar(line, col int) func(varRef) {
	return func(r varRef) {
		u := l.vars[r.Name]
		if u == nil {
			_, inEnv := l.env[r.Name]
			u = &varUse{preview: VariablePreview{Name: r.Name, Line: line, InEnv: inEnv}, allDefault: true}
			l.vars[r.Name] = u
			l.varOrder = append(l.varOrder, r.Name)
		}
		u.allDefault = u.allDefault && r.Default
		u.preview.Required = u.preview.Required || r.Required
		if r.Default || r.Set {
			return
		}
		if !u.missing {
			u.missing, u.missingLine, u.missingCol = true, line, col
		}
		u.missingReq = u.missingReq || r.Required
	}
}

// finishPreview turns the collected variables and named volumes into the preview and the variable diagnostics.
func (l *linter) finishPreview() {
	for _, name := range l.varOrder {
		u := l.vars[name]
		u.preview.HasDefault = u.allDefault
		l.preview.Variables = append(l.preview.Variables, u.preview)
		if !u.missing {
			continue
		}
		d := Diagnostic{
			Line: u.missingLine, Column: u.missingCol, Severity: sevWarning, Code: "variable_missing",
			Message: fmt.Sprintf("Variable %s is not set in .env and has no default.", name),
			Params:  map[string]string{"variable": name},
		}
		if !u.missingReq {
			d.Fix = &Fix{Kind: "env_random", Variable: name}
		}
		l.diags = append(l.diags, d)
	}
	for _, name := range l.usedNamed {
		if l.declared[name] {
			l.preview.NamedVolumes = append(l.preview.NamedVolumes, name)
		}
	}
}

func (l *linter) checkService(k, v *yaml.Node) {
	name := k.Value
	sp := ServicePreview{Name: name, Line: k.Line, Ports: []PortPreview{}, Volumes: []VolumePreview{}}
	defer func() { l.preview.Services = append(l.preview.Services, sp) }()
	if v == nil || v.Kind != yaml.MappingNode {
		l.add(k, name, sevError, "not_a_mapping", fmt.Sprintf("Service %s must be a mapping.", name),
			map[string]string{"what": "service"})
		return
	}
	_, imgNode := mapGet(v, "image")
	image, _ := scalarText(imgNode)
	image = strings.TrimSpace(image)
	_, buildNode := mapGet(v, "build")
	_, extends := mapGet(v, "extends")
	sp.Image, sp.Build = image, nonNull(buildNode)
	switch {
	case image == "" && !sp.Build && !nonNull(extends):
		l.add(k, name, sevError, "service_no_image",
			fmt.Sprintf("Service %s has neither an image nor a build section.", name), map[string]string{"service": name})
	case image != "" && !sp.Build:
		l.checkImage(name, imgNode, image)
	}
	if pk, pv := mapGet(v, "privileged"); pk != nil && scalarBool(pv) {
		l.add(pk, name, sevHint, "privileged", "A privileged container has full access to the host.", nil)
	}
	if nk, nv := mapGet(v, "network_mode"); nk != nil {
		if mode, _ := scalarText(nv); mode == "host" {
			l.add(nk, name, sevHint, "network_mode_host", "network_mode host shares the host's network stack.", nil)
		}
	}
	if ck, cv := mapGet(v, "cap_add"); ck != nil {
		if caps := scalarList(cv); len(caps) > 0 {
			l.add(ck, name, sevHint, "cap_add", "Extra Linux capabilities: "+strings.Join(caps, ", "),
				map[string]string{"caps": strings.Join(caps, ", ")})
		}
	}
	if rk, _ := mapGet(v, "restart"); rk == nil && !nonNull(extends) {
		_, deploy := mapGet(v, "deploy")
		if dk, _ := mapGet(deploy, "restart_policy"); dk == nil {
			l.add(k, name, sevHint, "restart_missing",
				fmt.Sprintf("Service %s has no restart policy, so it stays down after a reboot.", name), nil)
		}
	}
	_, ports := mapGet(v, "ports")
	for _, item := range seqItems(ports) {
		l.checkPort(name, item, &sp)
	}
	_, vols := mapGet(v, "volumes")
	for _, item := range seqItems(vols) {
		l.checkVolume(name, item, &sp)
	}
	_, tmpfs := mapGet(v, "tmpfs")
	for _, target := range scalarList(tmpfs) {
		if expanded, unresolved := interpolate(target, l.env, nil); !unresolved {
			path, _, _ := strings.Cut(expanded, ":")
			sp.Volumes = append(sp.Volumes, VolumePreview{Kind: "tmpfs", Target: path})
		}
	}
}

// scalarList returns the non-empty scalar texts of a scalar or a sequence of scalars.
func scalarList(n *yaml.Node) []string {
	var out []string
	if s, ok := scalarText(n); ok {
		return nonEmpty(out, s)
	}
	for _, item := range seqItems(n) {
		if s, ok := scalarText(item); ok {
			out = nonEmpty(out, s)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func nonEmpty(list []string, s string) []string {
	if s = strings.TrimSpace(s); s != "" {
		list = append(list, s)
	}
	return list
}

func (l *linter) checkImage(svc string, n *yaml.Node, image string) {
	if strings.Contains(image, "$") || strings.Contains(image, "@") {
		return // a variable decides the tag, or a digest pins it
	}
	last := image[strings.LastIndexByte(image, '/')+1:]
	tag := ""
	if i := strings.LastIndexByte(last, ':'); i >= 0 {
		tag = last[i+1:]
	}
	params := map[string]string{"image": image}
	switch tag {
	case "latest":
		l.add(n, svc, sevHint, "image_latest", fmt.Sprintf("%s follows the latest tag, so it changes without notice.", image), params)
	case "":
		l.add(n, svc, sevHint, "image_no_tag", fmt.Sprintf("%s has no tag, so Docker uses latest.", image), params)
	}
}

func (l *linter) findConflict(port int, proto, ip string) *PublishedPort {
	for i := range l.published {
		p := &l.published[i]
		pp := strings.ToLower(p.Protocol)
		if pp == "" {
			pp = "tcp"
		}
		if (l.stack != "" && p.Project == l.stack) || p.Port != port || pp != proto || !ipsOverlap(p.HostIP, ip) {
			continue
		}
		return p
	}
	return nil
}

// portSpecOf reads one entry of a service's ports list (short or long syntax). ok is false when the entry cannot
// be judged because a variable in it has no value; err is the reason an entry is invalid.
func (l *linter) portSpecOf(item *yaml.Node) (spec portSpec, raw string, ok bool, err error) {
	expand := func(s string) (string, bool) { return interpolate(s, l.env, nil) }
	switch item.Kind {
	case yaml.ScalarNode:
		raw = item.Value
		text, unresolved := expand(raw)
		if unresolved {
			return portSpec{}, raw, false, nil
		}
		spec, err = parsePortSpec(text)
		return spec, raw, true, err
	case yaml.MappingNode:
		field := func(key string) (string, bool) {
			text, _ := scalarText(mapValue(item, key))
			return expand(text)
		}
		target, u1 := field("target")
		published, u2 := field("published")
		hostIP, u3 := field("host_ip")
		proto, u4 := field("protocol")
		raw = "target: " + target + ", published: " + published
		if u1 || u2 || u3 || u4 {
			return portSpec{}, raw, false, nil
		}
		if target == "" {
			return portSpec{}, raw, true, fmt.Errorf("the target port is missing")
		}
		spec, err = newPortSpec(hostIP, published, target, proto)
		return spec, raw, true, err
	}
	return portSpec{}, "", true, fmt.Errorf("a port must be a string, a number or a mapping")
}

func (l *linter) checkPort(svc string, item *yaml.Node, sp *ServicePreview) {
	spec, raw, ok, err := l.portSpecOf(item)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	if err != nil {
		l.add(item, svc, sevError, "invalid_port", fmt.Sprintf("Invalid port %q: %v", raw, err),
			map[string]string{"value": raw, "reason": err.Error()})
		return
	}
	pv := PortPreview{HostIP: spec.HostIP, Host: spec.hostText(), Container: spec.containerText(), Protocol: spec.Protocol}
	if spec.fixedHostPorts() {
		l.checkHostPorts(svc, item, spec, &pv)
	}
	sp.Ports = append(sp.Ports, pv)
}

// checkHostPorts looks for the same host port twice in the file and for ports other containers already publish.
func (l *linter) checkHostPorts(svc string, item *yaml.Node, spec portSpec, pv *PortPreview) {
	dupReported := false
	width := spec.HostHi - spec.HostLo + 1
	if width > maxLintedPortRange {
		width = maxLintedPortRange
	}
	for port := spec.HostLo; port < spec.HostLo+width; port++ {
		key := portKey{port, spec.Protocol}
		if !dupReported {
			for _, prev := range l.ports[key] {
				if !ipsOverlap(prev.ip, spec.HostIP) {
					continue
				}
				dupReported = true
				l.add(item, svc, sevError, "port_duplicate",
					fmt.Sprintf("Host port %d/%s is published twice (first at line %d).", port, spec.Protocol, prev.line),
					map[string]string{"port": fmt.Sprint(port), "protocol": spec.Protocol, "first_line": fmt.Sprint(prev.line)})
				break
			}
		}
		l.ports[key] = append(l.ports[key], portUse{ip: spec.HostIP, line: item.Line})
		if pv.Conflict != "" {
			continue
		}
		if c := l.findConflict(port, spec.Protocol, spec.HostIP); c != nil {
			pv.Conflict = c.Container
			l.add(item, svc, sevWarning, "port_conflict",
				fmt.Sprintf("Host port %d/%s is already published by container %s.", port, spec.Protocol, c.Container),
				map[string]string{"port": fmt.Sprint(port), "protocol": spec.Protocol, "container": c.Container, "project": c.Project})
		}
	}
}

func (l *linter) checkVolume(svc string, item *yaml.Node, sp *ServicePreview) {
	var spec volumeSpec
	var err error
	switch item.Kind {
	case yaml.ScalarNode:
		text, unresolved := interpolate(item.Value, l.env, nil)
		if unresolved {
			return
		}
		spec, err = parseVolumeShort(text)
	case yaml.MappingNode:
		field := func(key string) (string, bool) {
			text, _ := scalarText(mapValue(item, key))
			return interpolate(text, l.env, nil)
		}
		typ, u1 := field("type")
		source, u2 := field("source")
		target, u3 := field("target")
		if u1 || u2 || u3 {
			return
		}
		spec, err = volumeFromLong(typ, source, target, scalarBool(mapValue(item, "read_only")))
	default:
		return
	}
	if err != nil {
		return // Compose reports malformed storage entries when the stack is deployed
	}
	sp.Volumes = append(sp.Volumes, VolumePreview{Kind: spec.Kind, Source: spec.Source, Target: spec.Target, ReadOnly: spec.ReadOnly})
	switch {
	case spec.Kind == "named":
		if !stringIn(l.usedNamed, spec.Source) {
			l.usedNamed = append(l.usedNamed, spec.Source)
		}
	case strings.Contains(spec.Source, "docker.sock") || strings.Contains(spec.Source, "docker_engine"):
		l.add(item, svc, sevHint, "docker_socket", "Mounting the Docker socket gives the container control of the host.",
			map[string]string{"source": spec.Source})
	}
}

func stringIn(list []string, s string) bool {
	for _, e := range list {
		if e == s {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

### Task B4: Shell word splitter

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/convert_shell.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/convert_shell_test.go`

`splitCommand` splits a pasted command line into words without running anything: blanks and newlines separate words; a backslash (POSIX) or a backtick (PowerShell) before a line break joins the lines (trailing blanks and CRLF are tolerated); single quotes are literal; double quotes allow an escaped quote, backslash, dollar sign and backtick; a backslash before any other character stays, so `C:\data` survives; `$(...)` stays in one piece; a word that starts with `#` begins a comment. Because the result goes into a compose file, where a lone `$` starts a variable, a dollar sign the shell would have kept literally (single quotes, `\$`) is returned as `$$`. Unbalanced quotes are an error.

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"errors"
	"strings"
)

// splitCommand splits a pasted command line into words the way a shell would, without running anything:
//
//   - blanks and newlines separate words; a backslash (POSIX) or backtick (PowerShell) before a line break joins the
//     lines, trailing blanks after it are tolerated;
//   - single quotes keep their content literally, double quotes allow an escaped quote, backslash, dollar sign or
//     backtick (the PowerShell escape character is the backtick), a backslash before any other character stays (so
//     C:\data survives);
//   - $(...) is kept as one piece, a word that starts with # begins a comment.
//
// The result is meant for a compose file, where a lone "$" starts a variable: a dollar sign the shell would have kept
// literally (single quotes, \$) is returned as "$$", so Compose reads the same text back. An unbalanced quote is an
// error.
func splitCommand(s string) ([]string, error) {
	var words []string
	var cur strings.Builder
	inWord := false
	flush := func() {
		if inWord {
			words = append(words, cur.String())
			cur.Reset()
			inWord = false
		}
	}
	literal := func(c byte) { // a character that must reach the compose file unchanged
		if c == '$' {
			cur.WriteString("$$")
		} else {
			cur.WriteByte(c)
		}
		inWord = true
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		c := s[i]
		switch {
		case c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\r' || c == '\n':
			flush()
		case c == '\\' || c == '`':
			if end, ok := lineContinuation(s, i+1); ok {
				i = end
				continue
			}
			if i+1 < len(s) && escapable(s[i+1], c) {
				i++
				literal(s[i])
				continue
			}
			cur.WriteByte(c) // a backslash in C:\data or a backtick pair around `pwd`
			inWord = true
		case c == '\'':
			end := strings.IndexByte(s[i+1:], '\'')
			if end < 0 {
				return nil, errors.New("unbalanced single quote")
			}
			for _, q := range []byte(s[i+1 : i+1+end]) {
				literal(q)
			}
			inWord = true
			i += end + 1
		case c == '"':
			next, err := doubleQuoted(s, i+1, &cur)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			inWord = true
			i = next
		case c == '$' && i+1 < len(s) && s[i+1] == '(':
			end := closingParen(s, i+1)
			cur.WriteString(s[i:end])
			inWord = true
			i = end - 1
		case c == '#' && !inWord:
			for i < len(s) && s[i] != '\n' {
				i++
			}
		default:
			cur.WriteByte(c)
			inWord = true
		}
	}
	flush()
	return words, nil
}

// lineContinuation reports whether s[from:] is optional blanks followed by a line break and returns the index of the
// last character of that break.
func lineContinuation(s string, from int) (end int, ok bool) {
	j := from
	for j < len(s) && (s[j] == ' ' || s[j] == '\t' || s[j] == '\r') {
		j++
	}
	if j < len(s) && s[j] == '\n' {
		return j, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// escapable tells whether the character after an escape character is taken literally. esc is '\\' or '`'.
func escapable(next, esc byte) bool {
	if esc == '`' {
		return next == '`' || next == '"' || next == '\'' || next == '$'
	}
	return strings.IndexByte(" \t\"'\\$`#()&;|<>*?[]{}!~", next) >= 0
}

// doubleQuoted appends the content of a double-quoted section that starts at s[from] to cur and returns the index of
// its closing quote.
func doubleQuoted(s string, from int, cur *strings.Builder) (int, error) {
	for i := from; i < len(s); i++ {
		c := s[i]
		switch {
		case c == '"':
			return i, nil
		case (c == '\\' || c == '`') && i+1 < len(s):
			if end, ok := lineContinuation(s, i+1); ok && c == '\\' {
				i = end
				continue
			}
			if n := s[i+1]; n == '"' || n == '\\' || n == '`' || n == '$' {
				i++
				if n == '$' {
					cur.WriteString("$$")
				} else {
					cur.WriteByte(n)
				}
				continue
			}
			cur.WriteByte(c)
		default:
			cur.WriteByte(c)
		}
	}
	return 0, errors.New("unbalanced double quote")
}

// closingParen returns the index just after the ")" that closes the "(" at s[open]; an unclosed one ends at the end.
func closingParen(s string, open int) int {
	depth := 0
	for i := open; i < len(s); i++ {
		switch s[i] {
		case '(':
			depth++
		case ')':
			depth--
			if depth == 0 {
				return i + 1
			}
		}
	}
	return len(s)
}
```

### Task B5: `ConvertDockerRun`

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/convert.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/convert_nodes.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/convert_build.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerstacks/convert_runtime.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerstacks/convert_test.go`

The converter turns one `docker run` command (also `docker container run`, optionally behind `sudo` or a copied `$ ` prompt) into compose YAML:

- `convert.go`: the public types, the flag tables (supported flags, flags that are recognised so that their value is skipped, repeatable flags), and the command parser: `--flag=value`, `--flag value`, repeated flags, combined short flags (`-it`, `-dp 80:80`) and attached values (`-p80:80`, `-e=A=1`); everything after the image is the container command. A bool flag with `=false` is switched off. Errors (`*Error`, `CodeConvertFailed`): empty command, not a `docker run`, no image, unbalanced quotes.
- `convert_nodes.go`: `yaml.Node` helpers. The file is built from nodes so the key order is fixed and reads like a compose file: `image`, `container_name`, `command`, `entrypoint`, `restart`, `ports`, `expose`, `volumes`, `tmpfs`, `environment`, `env_file`, `labels`, networks, host and user settings, capabilities, devices, limits, `healthcheck`, `logging`, `deploy` (GPUs), `platform`, `pull_policy`, `pid`, `ipc`, `tty`, `stdin_open`. Strings that YAML would read as another type (`"1"`, `"true"`, `"no"`) are quoted; ports are always quoted; the encoder uses a 2-space indent.
- `convert_build.go`: the build sequence and the mappings of the plain flags: storage (`-v` is kept as typed, named volumes are declared under a top-level `volumes:`; `--mount` becomes the long syntax with `bind`/`volume`/`tmpfs` options), environment (`-e KEY` without a value is passed through), labels, limits, ulimits, `--sysctl`. `$(pwd)`, `${PWD}`, `$PWD` and `pwd` in backticks inside a `-v`/`--mount` value become `.` (the stack folder); other `$(...)` substitutions are kept and reported.
- `convert_runtime.go`: networks (`host`/`none`/`bridge`/`container:x` become `network_mode`, other names become `networks:` plus a top-level `external` entry, `--network-alias` becomes `aliases`), health check, logging, `--gpus` (`all`, a count or `device=0,1`).

Flags the converter knows but cannot convert are reported as `flag_unsupported` and their value is skipped (the full `docker run` flag list is in the tables, so `--cpuset-cpus 0-1 nginx` still finds the image). Unknown flags are reported too. `--rm` is `flag_ignored`; invalid values (`--restart sometimes`, `--cpus abc`, a malformed port) are `flag_value_invalid` and the value is left out, except ports and volumes, which are kept as typed so lint can point at them.

```go
			}
			if res.Service != tc.service {
				t.Errorf("service = %q, want %q", res.Service, tc.service)
			}
			if res.Compose != tc.compose {
				t.Errorf("compose =\n%s\nwant\n%s", res.Compose, tc.compose)
			}
			got := []string{}
			for _, w := range res.Warnings {
				if w.Message == "" {
					t.Errorf("warning %+v has no message", w)
				}
				got = append(got, w.Code+" "+w.Flag)
			}
			want := tc.warnings
			if want == nil {
				want = []string{}
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
				t.Errorf("warnings = %q, want %q", got, want)
			}
			// the output must be a compose file the linter can read, unless the command itself was wrong
			if !strings.Contains(strings.Join(got, ","), warnValueInvalid) {
				for _, d := range Lint(LintInput{Compose: res.Compose}, nil).Diagnostics {
					if d.Severity == "error" {
						t.Errorf("lint reports %+v for the converted file", d)
					}
				}
			}
			if match := regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$`); !match.MatchString(res.Service) {
				t.Errorf("service name %q breaks the stack name rules", res.Service)
			}
		})
	}

func TestConvertDockerRunErrors(t *testing.T) {
	for name, command := range map[string]string{
		"empty":             "   ",
		"another command":   "docker ps -a",
		"not docker":        "podman run nginx",
		"docker container":  "docker container ls",
		"no image":          "docker run -d --name web",
		"flags only":        "docker run -it --rm",
		"unbalanced quote":  `docker run -e "A=1 nginx`,
		"unbalanced single": `docker run -e 'A=1 nginx`,
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			res, err := ConvertDockerRun(command)
			var coded *Error
			if !errors.As(err, &coded) || coded.Code != CodeConvertFailed || coded.Message == "" {
				t.Fatalf("ConvertDockerRun(%q) = %+v, %v; want an *Error with code %s", command, res, err, CodeConvertFailed)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestConvertResultJSON(t *testing.T) {
	res, err := ConvertDockerRun("docker run nginx")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(res)
	if !strings.Contains(string(raw), `"warnings":[]`) {
		t.Fatalf("result JSON %s must carry an empty warnings list, not null", raw)
	}
}
```

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"strings"
)

// ConvertResult is the compose file for one `docker run` command.
type ConvertResult struct {
	Compose  string           `json:"compose"` // "services:\n  <name>:\n    image: ..." (2-space indent)
	Service  string           `json:"service"`
	Warnings []ConvertWarning `json:"warnings"`
}

// ConvertWarning names a flag the converter could not carry over completely.
type ConvertWarning struct {
	Code    string `json:"code"` // "flag_unsupported" | "flag_ignored" | "flag_value_invalid"
	Flag    string `json:"flag"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
}

const (
	warnUnsupported  = "flag_unsupported"
	warnIgnored      = "flag_ignored"
	warnValueInvalid = "flag_value_invalid"
)

// flag kinds of `docker run`
const (
	kindUnknown = iota
	kindBool
	kindValue
)

// shortFlags maps the one-letter flags of `docker run` to their long names.
var shortFlags = map[byte]string{
	'a': "attach", 'c': "cpu-shares", 'd': "detach", 'e': "env", 'h': "hostname", 'i': "interactive", 'l': "label",
	'm': "memory", 'p': "publish", 'P': "publish-all", 'q': "quiet", 't': "tty", 'u': "user", 'v': "volume", 'w': "workdir",
}

var flagAliases = map[string]string{"net": "network"}

// Flags the converter understands.
var (
	supportedBoolFlags  = flagSet("detach", "rm", "privileged", "init", "read-only", "interactive", "tty", "no-healthcheck")
	supportedValueFlags = flagSet("name", "publish", "expose", "volume", "mount", "env", "env-file", "restart", "network",
		"network-alias", "hostname", "workdir", "user", "label", "cap-add", "cap-drop", "device", "entrypoint", "memory",
		"cpus", "shm-size", "ulimit", "security-opt", "tmpfs", "sysctl", "add-host", "dns", "log-driver", "log-opt",
		"platform", "pull", "stop-signal", "stop-timeout", "health-cmd", "health-interval", "health-timeout",
		"health-retries", "health-start-period", "gpus", "pid", "ipc", "group-add")
	// Flags of `docker run` that are recognised, so that their value is skipped, but have no conversion.
	otherBoolFlags  = flagSet("publish-all", "oom-kill-disable", "quiet", "sig-proxy", "disable-content-trust", "use-api-socket")
	otherValueFlags = flagSet("annotation", "attach", "blkio-weight", "blkio-weight-device", "cgroup-parent", "cgroupns", "cidfile",
		"cpu-count", "cpu-percent", "cpu-period", "cpu-quota", "cpu-rt-period", "cpu-rt-runtime", "cpu-shares", "cpuset-cpus",
		"cpuset-mems", "detach-keys", "device-cgroup-rule", "device-read-bps", "device-read-iops", "device-write-bps",
		"device-write-iops", "dns-option", "dns-search", "domainname", "health-start-interval", "io-maxbandwidth",
		"io-maxiops", "ip", "ip6", "isolation", "kernel-memory", "label-file", "link", "link-local-ip", "mac-address",
		"memory-reservation", "memory-swap", "memory-swappiness", "oom-score-adj", "pids-limit", "runtime", "storage-opt",
		"userns", "uts", "volume-driver", "volumes-from")
	// Flags that may be given more than once; every other flag keeps its last value.
	repeatableFlags = flagSet("publish", "expose", "volume", "mount", "env", "env-file", "network", "network-alias", "label",
		"cap-add", "cap-drop", "device", "ulimit", "security-opt", "tmpfs", "sysctl", "add-host", "dns", "log-opt", "group-add")
)

func flagSet(names ...string) map[string]bool {
	m := make(map[string]bool, len(names))
	for _, n := range names {
		m[n] = true
	}
	return m
}

func flagKind(name string) int {
	switch {
	case supportedBoolFlags[name], otherBoolFlags[name]:
		return kindBool
	case supportedValueFlags[name], otherValueFlags[name]:
		return kindValue
	}
	return kindUnknown
}

// runCommand is the parsed `docker run` command line.
type runCommand struct {
	image    string
	args     []string            // everything after the image
	values   map[string][]string // flag -> values in command order (one entry for non-repeatable flags)
	bools    map[string]bool
	warnings []ConvertWarning
}

func (r *runCommand) warn(code, flag, message string) {
	r.warnings = append(r.warnings, ConvertWarning{Code: code, Flag: flag, Message: message})
}

func convertFailed(message string) error { return &Error{Code: CodeConvertFailed, Message: message} }

// ConvertDockerRun turns one `docker run ...` command (also `docker container run`, with line continuations and
// quotes) into compose YAML. Errors carry CodeConvertFailed: not a docker run command, no image, unbalanced quotes.
// Flags that have no Compose equivalent produce warnings instead of failing.
func ConvertDockerRun(command string) (ConvertResult, error) {
	words, err := splitCommand(command)
	if err != nil {
		return ConvertResult{}, convertFailed("The command has an " + err.Error() + ".")
	}
	for len(words) > 0 && (words[0] == "$" || words[0] == "sudo") { // a copied prompt, or sudo
		words = words[1:]
	}
	if len(words) == 0 {
		return ConvertResult{}, convertFailed("The command is empty.")
	}
	i := 1
	if words[0] == "docker" && i < len(words) && words[i] == "container" {
		i++
	}
	if words[0] != "docker" || i >= len(words) || words[i] != "run" {
		return ConvertResult{}, convertFailed("This is not a docker run command.")
	}
	run := &runCommand{values: map[string][]string{}, bools: map[string]bool{}}
	run.parse(words[i+1:])
	if run.image == "" {
		return ConvertResult{}, convertFailed("The command names no image.")
	}
	return run.build()
}

// parse reads flags up to the image; everything after the image belongs to the container's command.
func (r *runCommand) parse(words []string) {
	for i := 0; i < len(words); i++ {
		w := words[i]
		switch {
		case w == "--":
			if i+1 < len(words) {
				r.image, r.args = words[i+1], words[i+2:]
			}
			return
		case strings.HasPrefix(w, "--"):
			name, value, hasValue := strings.Cut(w[2:], "=")
			if alias, ok := flagAliases[name]; ok {
				name = alias
			}
			switch flagKind(name) {
			case kindBool:
				r.setBool(name, !hasValue || value != "false")
			case kindValue:
				if !hasValue {
					if i+1 >= len(words) {
						r.warn(warnValueInvalid, "--"+name, "--"+name+" needs a value.")
						continue
					}
					i++
					value = words[i]
				}
				r.setValue(name, value)
			default:
				r.warn(warnUnsupported, "--"+name, "--"+name+" is not a docker run flag the converter knows; it was left out.")
			}
		case strings.HasPrefix(w, "-") && len(w) > 1:
			i = r.parseShort(words, i)
		default:
			r.image, r.args = w, words[i+1:]
			return
		}
	}
}

// parseShort handles a cluster of one-letter flags such as -it, -dp 80:80 or -p80:80 and returns the index of the
// last word it consumed.
func (r *runCommand) parseShort(words []string, i int) int {
	w := words[i]
	for j := 1; j < len(w); j++ {
		name, ok := shortFlags[w[j]]
		if !ok {
			r.warn(warnUnsupported, "-"+string(w[j]), "-"+string(w[j])+" is not a docker run flag the converter knows; it was left out.")
			return i
		}
		if flagKind(name) == kindBool {
			r.setBool(name, true)
			continue
		}
		value := strings.TrimPrefix(w[j+1:], "=")
		if value == "" {
			if i+1 >= len(words) {
				r.warn(warnValueInvalid, "--"+name, "--"+name+" needs a value.")
				return i
			}
			i++
			value = words[i]
		}
		r.setValue(name, value)
		return i
	}
	return i
}

func (r *runCommand) setBool(name string, on bool) {
	switch {
	case !on:
		delete(r.bools, name)
	case supportedBoolFlags[name]:
		r.bools[name] = true
	default:
		r.warn(warnUnsupported, "--"+name, "--"+name+" has no Compose equivalent; it was left out.")
	}
}

func (r *runCommand) setValue(name, value string) {
	switch {
	case supportedValueFlags[name] && repeatableFlags[name]:
		r.values[name] = append(r.values[name], value)
	case supportedValueFlags[name]:
		r.values[name] = []string{value}
	default:
		r.warn(warnUnsupported, "--"+name, "--"+name+" is not converted yet; add the matching Compose key by hand.")
	}
}

func (r *runCommand) last(name string) (string, bool) {
	v := r.values[name]
	if len(v) == 0 {
		return "", false
	}
	return v[len(v)-1], true
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/convert_nodes.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

var (
	restartPattern  = regexp.MustCompile(`^(no|always|unless-stopped|on-failure(:\d+)?)$`)
	bytesPattern    = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d+(\.\d+)?[bkmgBKMG]?$`)
	durationPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^(0|(\d+(\.\d+)?(ns|us|ms|s|m|h))+)$`)
	pwdPattern      = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\$(?:\(pwd\)|\{pwd\}|pwd\b)` + "|`pwd`")
	userIDPattern   = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d+:\d+$`)
)

// ---- YAML node helpers: nodes (not maps) keep the key order of a compose file readable ----

func strNode(v string) *yaml.Node {
	n := &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Tag: "!!str", Value: v}
	switch strings.ToLower(v) {
	case "y", "n", "yes", "no", "on", "off": // YAML 1.1 tools read these as booleans
		n.Style = yaml.DoubleQuotedStyle
	}
	return n
}

func quotedNode(v string) *yaml.Node {
	return &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Tag: "!!str", Value: v, Style: yaml.DoubleQuotedStyle}
}

func quotedNodes(values []string) []*yaml.Node {
	out := make([]*yaml.Node, 0, len(values))
	for _, v := range values {
		out = append(out, quotedNode(v))
	}
	return out
}

func boolNode(b bool) *yaml.Node {
	return &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Tag: "!!bool", Value: strconv.FormatBool(b)}
}

func nullNode() *yaml.Node { return &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Tag: "!!null"} }

// numberNode writes digits (and a decimal point) as a YAML number and anything else as a string.
func numberNode(v string) *yaml.Node {
	if _, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil {
		return &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Tag: "!!int", Value: v}
	}
	if _, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64); err == nil && !strings.ContainsAny(v, "eEnN+") {
		return &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Tag: "!!float", Value: v}
	}
	return strNode(v)
}

func seqNode(items ...*yaml.Node) *yaml.Node {
	return &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.SequenceNode, Tag: "!!seq", Content: items}
}

func flowSeqNode(items ...*yaml.Node) *yaml.Node {
	n := seqNode(items...)
	n.Style = yaml.FlowStyle
	return n
}

func strSeq(values []string, quote bool) *yaml.Node {
	n := seqNode()
	for _, v := range values {
		if quote {
			n.Content = append(n.Content, quotedNode(v))
		} else {
			n.Content = append(n.Content, strNode(v))
		}
	}
	return n
}

// mapping is a YAML mapping node that is filled in the order the keys are added.
type mapping struct{ n *yaml.Node }

func newMapping() *mapping { return &mapping{&yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.MappingNode, Tag: "!!map"}} }

func (m *mapping) add(key string, val *yaml.Node) { m.set(key, val) }

// set adds key, or replaces its value when the key is already there (the key keeps its place).
func (m *mapping) set(key string, val *yaml.Node) {
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(m.n.Content); i += 2 {
		if m.n.Content[i].Value == key {
			m.n.Content[i+1] = val
			return
		}
	}
	m.n.Content = append(m.n.Content, strNode(key), val)
}

func (m *mapping) empty() bool { return len(m.n.Content) == 0 }

// ---- names ----

// sanitizeServiceName makes s fit the stack name rules ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ ("app" when nothing is left).
func sanitizeServiceName(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, c := range strings.ToLower(s) {
		switch {
		case (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_' || c == '-':
			b.WriteRune(c)
		default:
			b.WriteByte('-')
		}
	}
	out := strings.TrimLeft(b.String(), "_-")
	if len(out) > 63 {
		out = out[:63]
	}
	if out == "" {
		return "app"
	}
	return out
}

// serviceNameFromImage is the last path segment of an image reference without its tag or digest.
func serviceNameFromImage(image string) string {
	if i := strings.IndexByte(image, '@'); i >= 0 {
		image = image[:i]
	}
	last := image[strings.LastIndexByte(image, '/')+1:]
	if i := strings.IndexByte(last, ':'); i >= 0 {
		last = last[:i]
	}
	return sanitizeServiceName(last)
}
```
