Create `internal/dockerstacks/convert_build.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/csv"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// ---- building the compose file ----

type converter struct {
	run      *runCommand
	svc      *mapping
	named    []string // named volumes the service uses
	networks []string // user-defined networks the service joins
}

func (c *converter) warn(code, flag, message string) { c.run.warn(code, flag, message) }

func (c *converter) addNamed(name string) {
	if !stringIn(c.named, name) {
		c.named = append(c.named, name)
	}
}

// build writes the service in a fixed key order: what runs, how it starts, how it is exposed, what it stores, then
// the tuning options.
func (r *runCommand) build() (ConvertResult, error) {
	r.normalizeValues()
	c := &converter{run: r, svc: newMapping()}
	name, hasName := r.last("name")
	service := serviceNameFromImage(r.image)
	if hasName {
		service = sanitizeServiceName(name)
	}
	c.svc.add("image", strNode(r.image))
	if hasName {
		c.svc.add("container_name", strNode(name))
	}
	if len(r.args) > 0 {
		c.svc.add("command", strSeq(r.args, false))
	}
	c.entrypoint()
	c.restart()
	c.ports()
	c.list("expose", "expose", true)
	c.volumes()
	c.list("tmpfs", "tmpfs", false)
	c.environment()
	c.list("env-file", "env_file", false)
	c.labels()
	c.network()
	c.text("hostname", "hostname")
	c.list("add-host", "extra_hosts", false)
	c.list("dns", "dns", false)
	c.text("workdir", "working_dir")
	c.user()
	c.list("group-add", "group_add", false)
	c.flag("privileged", "privileged")
	c.list("cap-add", "cap_add", false)
	c.list("cap-drop", "cap_drop", false)
	c.list("device", "devices", false)
	c.list("security-opt", "security_opt", false)
	c.keyValues("sysctl", "sysctls")
	c.ulimits()
	c.flag("read-only", "read_only")
	c.size("shm-size", "shm_size")
	c.size("memory", "mem_limit")
	c.cpus()
	c.flag("init", "init")
	c.text("stop-signal", "stop_signal")
	c.stopTimeout()
	c.healthcheck()
	c.logging()
	c.gpus()
	c.text("platform", "platform")
	c.pullPolicy()
	c.text("pid", "pid")
	c.text("ipc", "ipc")
	c.flag("tty", "tty")
	c.flag("interactive", "stdin_open")
	if r.bools["rm"] {
		c.warn(warnIgnored, "--rm", "Compose keeps stopped containers; --rm has no equivalent here.")
	}

	services := newMapping()
	services.add(service, c.svc.n)
	doc := newMapping()
	doc.add("services", services.n)
	if len(c.named) > 0 {
		volumes := newMapping()
		for _, v := range c.named {
			volumes.add(v, &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.MappingNode, Tag: "!!map", Style: yaml.FlowStyle})
		}
		doc.add("volumes", volumes.n)
	}
	if len(c.networks) > 0 {
		networks := newMapping()
		for _, n := range c.networks {
			ext := newMapping()
			ext.add("external", boolNode(true))
			networks.add(n, ext.n)
		}
		doc.add("networks", networks.n)
	}
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	enc := yaml.NewEncoder(&buf)
	enc.SetIndent(2)
	if err := enc.Encode(doc.n); err != nil {
		return ConvertResult{}, convertFailed("The compose file could not be written: " + err.Error())
	}
	if err := enc.Close(); err != nil {
		return ConvertResult{}, convertFailed("The compose file could not be written: " + err.Error())
	}
	warnings := r.warnings
	if warnings == nil {
		warnings = []ConvertWarning{}
	}
	return ConvertResult{Compose: buf.String(), Service: service, Warnings: warnings}, nil
}

// normalizeValues replaces $(pwd) in storage flags by "." (the stack folder) and warns about other command
// substitutions, which Compose cannot run.
func (r *runCommand) normalizeValues() {
	for _, flag := range []string{"volume", "mount"} {
		for i, v := range r.values[flag] {
			r.values[flag][i] = pwdPattern.ReplaceAllString(v, ".")
		}
	}
	flags := make([]string, 0, len(r.values))
	for f := range r.values {
		flags = append(flags, f)
	}
	sort.Strings(flags)
	for _, f := range flags {
		for _, v := range r.values[f] {
			if strings.Contains(v, "$(") {
				r.warn(warnValueInvalid, "--"+f, "--"+f+" contains a shell command substitution; Compose cannot run it, replace it by its value.")
				break
			}
		}
	}
	for _, a := range r.args {
		if strings.Contains(a, "$(") {
			r.warn(warnValueInvalid, "command", "The container command contains a shell command substitution; Compose cannot run it, replace it by its value.")
			break
		}
	}
}

// ---- generic mappings from one flag to one key ----

func (c *converter) text(flag, key string) {
	if v, ok := c.run.last(flag); ok && v != "" {
		c.svc.add(key, strNode(v))
	}
}

func (c *converter) list(flag, key string, quote bool) {
	if v := c.run.values[flag]; len(v) > 0 {
		c.svc.add(key, strSeq(v, quote))
	}
}

func (c *converter) flag(flag, key string) {
	if c.run.bools[flag] {
		c.svc.add(key, boolNode(true))
	}
}

func (c *converter) invalid(flag, value, why string) {
	c.warn(warnValueInvalid, "--"+flag, fmt.Sprintf("--%s %q was left out: %s.", flag, value, why))
}

// size handles --memory and --shm-size.
func (c *converter) size(flag, key string) {
	v, ok := c.run.last(flag)
	switch {
	case !ok || v == "":
	case !bytesPattern.MatchString(v):
		c.invalid(flag, v, "expected a number with an optional b, k, m or g")
	default:
		c.svc.add(key, numberNode(v))
	}
}

func (c *converter) cpus() {
	v, ok := c.run.last("cpus")
	if !ok || v == "" {
		return
	}
	if f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64); err != nil || f <= 0 || strings.ContainsAny(v, "eEnNiI+") {
		c.invalid("cpus", v, "expected a number above zero")
		return
	}
	c.svc.add("cpus", numberNode(v))
}

func (c *converter) stopTimeout() {
	v, ok := c.run.last("stop-timeout")
	if !ok || v == "" {
		return
	}
	if n, err := strconv.Atoi(v); err != nil || n < 0 {
		c.invalid("stop-timeout", v, "expected a number of seconds")
		return
	}
	c.svc.add("stop_grace_period", strNode(v+"s"))
}

func (c *converter) pullPolicy() {
	v, ok := c.run.last("pull")
	switch {
	case !ok || v == "":
	case v == "always" || v == "missing" || v == "never":
		c.svc.add("pull_policy", strNode(v))
	default:
		c.invalid("pull", v, "expected always, missing or never")
	}
}

func (c *converter) user() {
	v, ok := c.run.last("user")
	switch {
	case !ok || v == "":
	case userIDPattern.MatchString(v):
		c.svc.add("user", quotedNode(v)) // 1000:1000 would be read as a base-60 number by YAML 1.1 tools
	default:
		c.svc.add("user", strNode(v))
	}
}

func (c *converter) entrypoint() {
	v, ok := c.run.last("entrypoint")
	switch {
	case !ok:
	case v == "":
		c.svc.add("entrypoint", flowSeqNode())
	case strings.ContainsAny(v, " \t"):
		c.svc.add("entrypoint", flowSeqNode(quotedNode(v))) // docker run takes the whole value as the program
	default:
		c.svc.add("entrypoint", strNode(v))
	}
}

func (c *converter) restart() {
	v, ok := c.run.last("restart")
	switch {
	case !ok || v == "":
	case !restartPattern.MatchString(v):
		c.invalid("restart", v, "expected no, always, unless-stopped or on-failure[:max]")
	default:
		c.svc.add("restart", strNode(v))
	}
}

func (c *converter) ports() {
	items := c.run.values["publish"]
	if len(items) == 0 {
		return
	}
	for _, p := range items {
		if text, unresolved := interpolate(p, nil, nil); !unresolved {
			if _, err := parsePortSpec(text); err != nil {
				c.warn(warnValueInvalid, "--publish", fmt.Sprintf("Port %q looks wrong: %v. It was kept as typed.", p, err))
			}
		}
	}
	c.svc.add("ports", strSeq(items, true))
}

// ---- storage ----

func (c *converter) volumes() {
	seq := seqNode()
	for _, v := range c.run.values["volume"] {
		if text, unresolved := interpolate(v, nil, nil); !unresolved {
			spec, err := parseVolumeShort(text)
			switch {
			case err != nil:
				c.warn(warnValueInvalid, "--volume", fmt.Sprintf("Volume %q looks wrong: %v. It was kept as typed.", v, err))
			case spec.Kind == "named":
				c.addNamed(spec.Source)
			}
		}
		seq.Content = append(seq.Content, strNode(v))
	}
	for _, m := range c.run.values["mount"] {
		if node := c.mount(m); node != nil {
			seq.Content = append(seq.Content, node)
		}
	}
	if len(seq.Content) > 0 {
		c.svc.add("volumes", seq)
	}
}

// csvFields splits "a=b,c=d" the way docker does for --mount and --gpus: quotes protect commas.
func csvFields(s string) ([]string, error) {
	r := csv.NewReader(strings.NewReader(s))
	r.LazyQuotes = true
	return r.Read()
}

// mount converts one --mount value to a long-syntax volume entry (nil when it cannot be converted).
func (c *converter) mount(spec string) *yaml.Node {
	fields, err := csvFields(spec)
	if err != nil {
		c.invalid("mount", spec, "the value cannot be read")
		return nil
	}
	typ, source, target, readOnly := "volume", "", "", false
	nocopy, subpath, propagation, tmpfsSize := false, "", "", ""
	for _, f := range fields {
		key, val, hasVal := strings.Cut(f, "=")
		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(key)) {
		case "type":
			typ = val
		case "source", "src":
			source = val
		case "target", "destination", "dst":
			target = val
		case "readonly", "ro", "read_only":
			readOnly = !hasVal || (val != "false" && val != "0")
		case "bind-propagation":
			propagation = val
		case "volume-nocopy":
			nocopy = !hasVal || (val != "false" && val != "0")
		case "volume-subpath":
			subpath = val
		case "tmpfs-size":
			tmpfsSize = val
		case "consistency":
		default:
			c.warn(warnUnsupported, "--mount", fmt.Sprintf("--mount option %q is not converted; add it by hand.", key))
		}
	}
	if typ != "bind" && typ != "volume" && typ != "tmpfs" {
		c.invalid("mount", spec, "the type must be bind, volume or tmpfs")
		return nil
	}
	if target == "" {
		c.invalid("mount", spec, "the target is missing")
		return nil
	}
	m := newMapping()
	m.add("type", strNode(typ))
	if source != "" && typ != "tmpfs" {
		m.add("source", strNode(source))
		if typ == "volume" {
			c.addNamed(source)
		}
	}
	m.add("target", strNode(target))
	if readOnly {
		m.add("read_only", boolNode(true))
	}
	sub := newMapping()
	switch typ {
	case "bind":
		if propagation != "" {
			sub.add("propagation", strNode(propagation))
		}
	case "volume":
		if nocopy {
			sub.add("nocopy", boolNode(true))
		}
		if subpath != "" {
			sub.add("subpath", strNode(subpath))
		}
	case "tmpfs":
		if tmpfsSize != "" {
			sub.add("size", numberNode(tmpfsSize))
		}
	}
	if !sub.empty() {
		m.add(typ, sub.n)
	}
	return m.n
}

// ---- environment, labels, key=value flags ----

func (c *converter) environment() {
	env := newMapping()
	for _, e := range c.run.values["env"] {
		key, val, hasVal := strings.Cut(e, "=")
		key = strings.TrimSpace(key)
		switch {
		case key == "":
		case hasVal:
			env.set(key, strNode(val))
		default:
			env.set(key, nullNode()) // passed through from the environment Compose runs in
		}
	}
	if !env.empty() {
		c.svc.add("environment", env.n)
	}
}

func (c *converter) labels() {
	labels := newMapping()
	for _, l := range c.run.values["label"] {
		key, val, _ := strings.Cut(l, "=")
		if key = strings.TrimSpace(key); key != "" {
			labels.set(key, strNode(val))
		}
	}
	if !labels.empty() {
		c.svc.add("labels", labels.n)
	}
}

// keyValues handles --sysctl: KEY=VALUE pairs become a mapping.
func (c *converter) keyValues(flag, key string) {
	m := newMapping()
	for _, kv := range c.run.values[flag] {
		k, v, ok := strings.Cut(kv, "=")
		if k = strings.TrimSpace(k); !ok || k == "" {
			c.invalid(flag, kv, "expected KEY=VALUE")
			continue
		}
		m.set(k, strNode(v))
	}
	if !m.empty() {
		c.svc.add(key, m.n)
	}
}

func (c *converter) ulimits() {
	m := newMapping()
	for _, u := range c.run.values["ulimit"] {
		name, limits, ok := strings.Cut(u, "=")
		soft, hard, split := strings.Cut(limits, ":")
		_, errSoft := strconv.ParseInt(soft, 10, 64)
		_, errHard := strconv.ParseInt(hard, 10, 64)
		if !ok || name == "" || errSoft != nil || (split && errHard != nil) {
			c.invalid("ulimit", u, "expected NAME=SOFT[:HARD] with numbers")
			continue
		}
		if !split {
			m.set(name, numberNode(soft))
			continue
		}
		both := newMapping()
		both.add("soft", numberNode(soft))
		both.add("hard", numberNode(hard))
		m.set(name, both.n)
	}
	if !m.empty() {
		c.svc.add("ulimits", m.n)
	}
}
```

Create `internal/dockerstacks/convert_runtime.go`:

```go
package dockerstacks

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// ---- networks ----

func (c *converter) network() {
	var user []string
	mode := ""
	for _, n := range c.run.values["network"] {
		switch {
		case n == "host" || n == "none" || n == "bridge" || strings.HasPrefix(n, "container:"):
			if mode == "" {
				mode = n
			}
		case n == "" || n == "default":
		default:
			user = append(user, n)
		}
	}
	aliases := c.run.values["network-alias"]
	switch {
	case mode != "":
		c.svc.add("network_mode", strNode(mode))
		if len(user) > 0 {
			c.warn(warnValueInvalid, "--network", "network_mode cannot be combined with other networks; "+strings.Join(user, ", ")+" was left out.")
		}
		if len(aliases) > 0 {
			c.warn(warnIgnored, "--network-alias", "Network aliases only apply to user-defined networks.")
		}
	case len(user) == 0:
		if len(aliases) > 0 {
			c.warn(warnIgnored, "--network-alias", "Network aliases only apply to user-defined networks.")
		}
	case len(aliases) == 0:
		c.svc.add("networks", strSeq(user, false))
	default:
		m := newMapping()
		for _, n := range user {
			entry := newMapping()
			entry.add("aliases", strSeq(aliases, false))
			m.add(n, entry.n)
		}
		c.svc.add("networks", m.n)
	}
	for _, n := range user {
		if mode == "" && !stringIn(c.networks, n) {
			c.networks = append(c.networks, n)
		}
	}
}

// ---- health, logging, GPUs ----

func (c *converter) healthcheck() {
	if c.run.bools["no-healthcheck"] {
		hc := newMapping()
		hc.add("disable", boolNode(true))
		c.svc.add("healthcheck", hc.n)
		return
	}
	hc := newMapping()
	if cmd, ok := c.run.last("health-cmd"); ok && cmd != "" {
		if strings.EqualFold(cmd, "none") {
			hc.add("disable", boolNode(true))
		} else {
			hc.add("test", flowSeqNode(quotedNode("CMD-SHELL"), quotedNode(cmd)))
		}
	}
	for _, d := range [][2]string{{"health-interval", "interval"}, {"health-timeout", "timeout"}, {"health-start-period", "start_period"}} {
		v, ok := c.run.last(d[0])
		switch {
		case !ok || v == "":
		case !durationPattern.MatchString(v):
			c.invalid(d[0], v, "expected a duration such as 30s or 1m30s")
		default:
			hc.add(d[1], strNode(v))
		}
	}
	if v, ok := c.run.last("health-retries"); ok && v != "" {
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(v); err != nil || n < 0 {
			c.invalid("health-retries", v, "expected a number")
		} else {
			hc.add("retries", numberNode(v))
		}
	}
	if !hc.empty() {
		c.svc.add("healthcheck", hc.n)
	}
}

func (c *converter) logging() {
	driver, hasDriver := c.run.last("log-driver")
	opts := newMapping()
	for _, o := range c.run.values["log-opt"] {
		k, v, ok := strings.Cut(o, "=")
		if k = strings.TrimSpace(k); !ok || k == "" {
			c.invalid("log-opt", o, "expected KEY=VALUE")
			continue
		}
		opts.set(k, strNode(v))
	}
	logging := newMapping()
	if hasDriver && driver != "" {
		logging.add("driver", strNode(driver))
	}
	if !opts.empty() {
		logging.add("options", opts.n)
	}
	if !logging.empty() {
		c.svc.add("logging", logging.n)
	}
}

// gpus converts --gpus (all, a count, or a device list) to a device reservation.
func (c *converter) gpus() {
	v, ok := c.run.last("gpus")
	if !ok || v == "" {
		return
	}
	fields, err := csvFields(v)
	if err != nil {
		c.invalid("gpus", v, "the value cannot be read")
		return
	}
	count, driver, current := "", "nvidia", ""
	var ids, caps []string
	for _, f := range fields {
		key, val, hasVal := strings.Cut(f, "=")
		if !hasVal {
			switch current { // a bare item continues the previous list: device=0,1
			case "device":
				ids = append(ids, f)
			case "capabilities":
				caps = append(caps, f)
			default:
				count = f
			}
			continue
		}
		current = ""
		switch strings.ToLower(key) {
		case "count":
			count = val
		case "driver":
			driver = val
		case "device":
			ids, current = strings.Split(val, ","), "device"
		case "capabilities":
			caps, current = strings.Split(val, ","), "capabilities"
		default:
			c.warn(warnUnsupported, "--gpus", fmt.Sprintf("--gpus option %q is not converted; add it by hand.", key))
		}
	}
	if len(ids) == 0 && (count == "" || count == "-1") {
		count = "all"
	}
	if n, err := strconv.Atoi(count); count != "" && count != "all" && (err != nil || n < 1) {
		c.invalid("gpus", v, "expected all, a number of GPUs or device=...")
		return
	}
	if !stringIn(caps, "gpu") {
		caps = append([]string{"gpu"}, caps...)
	}
	dev := newMapping()
	dev.add("driver", strNode(driver))
	if len(ids) > 0 {
		dev.add("device_ids", flowSeqNode(quotedNodes(ids)...))
	} else {
		dev.add("count", numberNode(count))
	}
	capNodes := make([]*yaml.Node, 0, len(caps))
	for _, cp := range caps {
		capNodes = append(capNodes, strNode(cp))
	}
	dev.add("capabilities", flowSeqNode(capNodes...))
	reservations := newMapping()
	reservations.add("devices", seqNode(dev.n))
	resources := newMapping()
	resources.add("reservations", reservations.n)
	deploy := newMapping()
	deploy.add("resources", resources.n)
	c.svc.add("deploy", deploy.n)
}
```

Append these two bullets at the end of the `## Local contracts` list:

```markdown
- **Lint** (`Lint`, files `lint*.go`, `yamlnode.go`) is pure: no Engine access, no host. The compose file is parsed into `yaml.v3` nodes, so every diagnostic has a line and column; a YAML error returns only `yaml_syntax` plus the `.env` warnings. It never blocks anything. The codes and their `params` are the contract with the UI strings `lint_<code>`: `yaml_syntax`, `not_a_mapping`, `no_services`, `service_no_image`, `invalid_port`, `port_duplicate`, `port_conflict`, `variable_missing` (fix `env_random`, none for `${X:?m}`), `image_latest`, `image_no_tag`, `privileged`, `docker_socket`, `network_mode_host`, `restart_missing`, `cap_add`, `env_syntax`. **`env_syntax` lines belong to `.env`, every other code to the compose file.** `published` are the ports other containers publish on the host; those of project `LintInput.Stack` are not conflicts. `interpolate` is the one implementation of Compose variable syntax (`$$`, `$NAME`, `${X:-d}`, `${X:?m}`, nested defaults); a port or volume that uses a variable without value and default is not judged (the variable warning covers it). Every list in the answer is non-nil. Adding a code means adding its `lint_<code>` strings to all 16 desktop locales and the test table in `lint_test.go`.
- **`docker run` converter** (`ConvertDockerRun`, files `convert*.go`) builds the compose file from `yaml.Node`s so the key order is fixed (`image`, `container_name`, `command`, ...). `splitCommand` is a shell word splitter that runs nothing: quotes, `\` and PowerShell backtick continuations, `C:\path` survives, `$(pwd)` in storage flags becomes `.`; a dollar sign the shell kept literally is emitted as `$$`. The flag tables in `convert.go` list every `docker run` flag: supported ones are converted, known ones without a conversion are reported as `flag_unsupported` and their value is skipped (so the image is still found). Errors carry `CodeConvertFailed`; everything else is a warning (`flag_unsupported`, `flag_ignored`, `flag_value_invalid`) with the long flag name.
```

## Part C: stacks HTTP API (`internal/server`)

Part C puts the stacks service of Part A behind `/api/docker-manager/`: the service is opened and closed with the host registry, and the routes for helpers, prepare, stacks, files, operations (with the SSE stream), lint, the `docker run` converter and external compose projects join the phase 1 router. The tasks therefore carry a `git grep` caller check; every caller of an edited symbol is in `internal/server/docker_manager_*.go`, `server.go` or a test.

**Deviations from the contract** (names and JSON shapes of the contract are kept; each deviation is forced by the codebase or protects something):

1. **Service seam.** The handlers use the narrow interface `dmStackService` and a `stacks` field on `dmRequest`, set from `Server.DockerStacks` (`*dockerstacks.Service`, as the contract says) when it is not nil. Handler tests build a `dmRequest` with a fake; one wiring test uses the real service.
2. **`deploy_error`.** `POST /hosts/{h}/stacks` with `deploy: true` answers 201 `{stack, operation}`. When the files were written but the up operation could not be started (rare: journal error, service closing) the answer is still 201 `{stack, deploy_error: {code, message}}`, so a client does not repeat a create that succeeded. Additive; not in the contract.
3. **Body limit.** Requests that carry compose or `.env` text (create, files, lint) may be 8 MiB; larger bodies answer 413 `file_too_large`. The phase 1 limit of 1 MiB could not carry two 1 MiB files; the file size limit itself stays in the service.
4. **Convert timeout.** The contract names 5 s. `ConvertDockerRun` is a pure function without a context, so the route bounds its work by input size instead (command at most 64 KiB, else 400 `convert_failed`).
5. **Lint and convert need no stacks service.** Without it (503 elsewhere) lint runs without the port check and answers `ports_unchecked: true`; convert needs no service at all. Lint also answers `ports_unchecked: true` when the host's ports cannot be read; an unknown host id is 404 `host_not_found`.
6. **Project actions.** An unknown action word answers 400 `invalid_action` (like the container actions); the route timeout is 60 s (`dmActionTimeout`), the contract lists none.
7. **Helper containers** are also reported with `protected_owner: "docker_manager"` (not only `aurago_helper`), so the list and the 409 of the removal agree and the existing lock logic of the app works. `docker_manager` is **not** added to `containerProtectedOwners`: that list is shared with `/api/containers` and the agent docker tool (which would need the 16 manuals updated), and the helpers carry no `aurago.managed` label, so `dmHelperRole` recognizes them by `aurago.docker-manager.role`.
8. **Operations.** `POST …/ops` with `kind: "delete"` answers 400 `invalid_operation` before the service is called. List answers carry `output: ""` (the handler blanks it). The stream sends `Content-Type: text/event-stream` exactly, and no `id:` lines: a reconnect is always a new snapshot, so `Last-Event-ID` has no meaning. When the service closes the channel without a `done` event, Part A's hand-off says to send nothing more; the handler looks the operation up once and sends `done` if it has finished in the meantime (it saves the client a reconnect), and otherwise sends nothing.
9. **Host test.** `helpers` is added only when the connection test says `ok`; a helper status that cannot be read is left out (no error member).

**Facts about Parts A and B that this part relies on**

- `Start` and `Prepare` only record the operation and return it queued; everything that needs the Engine happens inside the operation. Their errors are `*Error` (`invalid_operation`, `stack_name_invalid`), `*BusyError`, `dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound`, or an internal one (journal, closed service). That is why they answer through `operationFailure`, which never reports `host_unreachable`.
- `List`, `Get`, `Create`, `WriteFiles`, `Helpers`, `ProjectVolumes`, `ProjectAction` and `PublishedPorts` do reach the Engine: their other errors are `dockerhost.StatusError` or transport errors, classified by the phase 1 `engineFailure`.
- `host_not_prepared` carries `Fields["helpers"]` (`HelperStatus`), `api_too_old` `Fields["api_version"]`, `runner_image_missing` `Fields["command"]`; `Error.Message` is one line without secrets.
- `Subscribe` returns the snapshot and a channel that is closed after the done event, on cancel, when the subscriber falls 256 events behind, or when the service closes; a finished operation gets an already closed channel. `Operation(id)` after a closed channel gives the final row. `Operations` returns rows without output.
- `Lint` skips the ports of project `in.Stack` itself; `PublishedPorts(ctx, host, excludeProject)` leaves out helper containers. `ConvertDockerRun` fails with `*Error` code `convert_failed`.
- The built-in host `local` resolves without the store (the shutdown test relies on it).

**Hand-off to part D (UI): what the routes answer**

| Route | Success | Failures the UI switches on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /hosts/{h}/helpers` | `{helpers}` | `api_too_old` is not an error here: `helpers.api_supported` is false |
| `POST /hosts/{h}/prepare` | 202 `{operation}` | 409 `operation_in_progress` (`operation_id`, `kind`), 403 `read_only` |
| `GET /hosts/{h}/stacks[?refresh=1]` | `{host_id, stacks_dir, stacks, external, ignored, scanned_at, cached}` | 409 `host_not_prepared` (`helpers`), 409 `api_too_old` (`api_version`), 409 `stacks_dir_unavailable`, 502 `host_unreachable` (`reason`) |
| `POST /hosts/{h}/stacks` | 201 `{stack, operation?, deploy_error?}` | 400 `stack_name_invalid`, 409 `stack_exists`, 413 `file_too_large`, plus the read failures |
| `GET /hosts/{h}/stacks/{name}` | `{stack}` | 404 `stack_not_found` |
| `PUT …/files` | `{revisions}` | 409 `revision_conflict` (`file`, `current`), 409 `operation_in_progress` while a delete runs |
| `GET …/volumes` | `{volumes}` | |
| `POST …/ops`, `DELETE …/stacks/{name}[?volumes=1]` | 202 `{operation}` | 409 `operation_in_progress` (`operation_id`, `kind`) |
| `POST /hosts/{h}/lint` | `{diagnostics, preview, ports_unchecked?}` | 404 `host_not_found` |
| `POST /hosts/{h}/projects/{p}/{start,stop,restart}` | `{}` | 404 `stack_not_found`, 409 `operation_in_progress` |
| `GET /operations[?host=&stack=&active=1&limit=]` | `{operations}` without output | |
| `GET /operations/{id}` | `{operation}` with the output tail | 404 `operation_not_found` |
| `GET /operations/{id}/stream` | SSE `snapshot`, `output`/`progress`/`state`, `done` | 404 `operation_not_found` as JSON before the stream starts |
| `POST /convert/docker-run` | `{compose, service, warnings}` | 400 `convert_failed` |

Every answer is the phase 1 envelope. `host_not_found` (404), `stacks_unavailable` (503) and `docker_disabled` (503) can come from any of them, `read_only` (403) from every mutating one. The stream ends after `done`; the UI closes its EventSource on it. A stream that ends without `done` means "reconnect" (a new snapshot replaces the entry). Every operation also appears in `GET /operations?active=1` while it runs, which is how the drawer reattaches after a page reload.

```go
package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
)

func TestDockerManagerStackFailureMapping(t *testing.T) {
	engine := func(status int) error {
		return &dockerhost.StatusError{Status: status, Err: fmt.Errorf("Docker API returned %d: engine said no", status)}
	}
	coded := func(code string, fields map[string]any) error {
		return fmt.Errorf("list stacks: %w", &dockerstacks.Error{Code: code, Message: "message of " + code, Fields: fields})
	}
	helpers := dockerstacks.HelperStatus{APIVersion: "1.45", APISupported: true, RunnerImage: dockerstacks.RunnerImageTag, IOContainer: "missing"}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		err    error
		status int
		code   string
		field  string // a member the answer must carry
	}{
		{"name invalid", coded(dockerstacks.CodeStackNameInvalid, nil), http.StatusBadRequest, "stack_name_invalid", ""},
		{"stack missing", coded(dockerstacks.CodeStackNotFound, nil), http.StatusNotFound, "stack_not_found", ""},
		{"stack exists", coded(dockerstacks.CodeStackExists, nil), http.StatusConflict, "stack_exists", ""},
		{"operation missing", coded(dockerstacks.CodeOperationNotFound, nil), http.StatusNotFound, "operation_not_found", ""},
		{"invalid operation", coded(dockerstacks.CodeInvalidOperation, nil), http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_operation", ""},
		{"file too large", coded(dockerstacks.CodeFileTooLarge, nil), http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "file_too_large", ""},
		{"host not prepared", coded(dockerstacks.CodeHostNotPrepared, map[string]any{"helpers": helpers}), http.StatusConflict, "host_not_prepared", "helpers"},
		{"runner image missing", coded(dockerstacks.CodeRunnerImageMissing, map[string]any{"command": "docker pull " + dockerstacks.RunnerImageTag}), http.StatusConflict, "runner_image_missing", "command"},
		{"api too old", coded(dockerstacks.CodeAPITooOld, map[string]any{"api_version": "1.40"}), http.StatusConflict, "api_too_old", "api_version"},
		{"stacks dir", coded(dockerstacks.CodeStacksDirInvalid, nil), http.StatusConflict, "stacks_dir_unavailable", ""},
		{"convert failed", coded(dockerstacks.CodeConvertFailed, nil), http.StatusBadRequest, "convert_failed", ""},
		{"revision conflict", fmt.Errorf("write: %w", &dockerstacks.ConflictError{File: "compose", Current: dockerstacks.FileContent{Name: "compose.yaml", Content: "services: {}", Revision: "abc", Exists: true}}), http.StatusConflict, "revision_conflict", "current"},
		{"busy", &dockerstacks.BusyError{OperationID: "op_0123456789abcdef", Kind: "up"}, http.StatusConflict, "operation_in_progress", "operation_id"},
		{"unknown host", dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound, http.StatusNotFound, "host_not_found", ""},
		{"engine refused", fmt.Errorf("list: %w", engine(500)), http.StatusBadGateway, "docker_error", ""},
		{"nothing answered", errors.New("dial tcp 10.0.0.5:2375: connect: connection refused"), http.StatusBadGateway, "host_unreachable", "reason"},
		{"unknown code", coded("brand_new_code", nil), http.StatusInternalServerError, "brand_new_code", ""},
	} {
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		(&dmRequest{s: &Server{}, w: rec}).stackFailure(tc.err)
		var body map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &body); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: answer %q is not JSON: %v", tc.name, rec.Body.String(), err)
		}
		if rec.Code != tc.status || body["status"] != "error" || body["code"] != tc.code {
			t.Errorf("%s: answer = %d %s, want %d error %q", tc.name, rec.Code, rec.Body.String(), tc.status, tc.code)
		}
		if tc.field != "" && body[tc.field] == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: answer %s lacks %q", tc.name, rec.Body.String(), tc.field)
		}
	}
}

func TestDockerManagerStackFailureFieldsKeepTheEnvelope(t *testing.T) {
	err := &dockerstacks.Error{Code: dockerstacks.CodeHostNotPrepared, Message: "not prepared", Fields: map[string]any{
		"status": "ok", "code": "other", "message": "other", "helpers": dockerstacks.HelperStatus{},
	}}
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	(&dmRequest{s: &Server{}, w: rec}).stackFailure(err)
	var body map[string]any
	if json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &body) != nil || body["status"] != "error" || body["code"] != "host_not_prepared" || body["message"] != "not prepared" {
		t.Fatalf("answer = %s, want the envelope members of the error, not its fields", rec.Body.String())
	}
}

func TestDockerManagerRevisionConflictCarriesTheHostFile(t *testing.T) {
	conflict := &dockerstacks.ConflictError{File: "env", Current: dockerstacks.FileContent{Name: ".env", Content: "A=1\n", Revision: "r1", Exists: true}}
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	(&dmRequest{s: &Server{}, w: rec}).stackFailure(conflict)
	var body struct {
		File    string                   `json:"file"`
		Current dockerstacks.FileContent `json:"current"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &body); err != nil || body.File != "env" || body.Current != conflict.Current {
		t.Fatalf("answer = %s (%v), want file env and the current .env content", rec.Body.String(), err)
	}
}

func TestDockerManagerOperationFailureIsNeverAnUnreachableHost(t *testing.T) {
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	(&dmRequest{s: &Server{}, w: rec}).operationFailure(errors.New("database is locked"))
	if rec.Code != http.StatusInternalServerError || !strings.Contains(rec.Body.String(), `"internal_error"`) {
		t.Fatalf("answer = %d %s, want 500 internal_error", rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
	}
}
```

```go
func TestInitDockerHostsOpensAndClosesTheStacksServiceWithTheRegistry(t *testing.T) {
	s := testContainerServer(true, false)
	dir := t.TempDir()
	s.Cfg.Directories.DataDir = dir

	s.initDockerHosts()
	t.Cleanup(s.closeDockerHosts)
	if s.DockerHosts == nil || s.DockerStacks == nil {
		t.Fatalf("registry open = %v, stacks service open = %v; want both", s.DockerHosts != nil, s.DockerStacks != nil)
	}
	// The operation journal is a table of the registry's own database file.
	ops, err := s.DockerStacks.Operations(context.Background(), dockerstacks.OperationFilter{})
	if err != nil || len(ops) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("operations = %v, %v; want an empty journal", ops, err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "docker_manager.db")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("docker_manager.db is not in the data directory: %v", err)
	}

	s.closeDockerHosts()
	// The built-in host resolves without the store, so this refusal comes from the service itself.
	if _, err := s.DockerStacks.Prepare(context.Background(), dockerhost.LocalHostID); err == nil || err.Error() != "the stacks service is closed" {
		t.Fatalf("Prepare after closeDockerHosts = %v, want the closed-service refusal", err)
	}
}

func TestInitDockerHostsKeepsTheRegistryWhenTheStacksServiceCannotOpen(t *testing.T) {
	s := testContainerServer(true, false)
	dir := t.TempDir()
	s.Cfg.Directories.DataDir = dir
	// A journal table with a foreign schema makes the service's schema step fail (its index needs the columns).
	store, err := dockerhost.OpenStore(filepath.Join(dir, "docker_manager.db"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := store.DB().Exec(`CREATE TABLE docker_operations (id TEXT)`); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := store.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	s.initDockerHosts()
	t.Cleanup(s.closeDockerHosts)
	if s.DockerHosts == nil {
		t.Fatal("a failing stacks service took the host registry down")
	}
	if s.DockerStacks != nil {
		t.Fatal("DockerStacks is set although its journal could not be created")
	}
}
```

```go
package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// ── Docker Manager stacks API: shared pieces ────────────────────────────────
// The stack, operation, lint and convert routes (docker_manager_stacks.go,
// docker_manager_operations.go, docker_manager_lint.go) call the stacks
// service through the narrow interface below and answer its failures through
// the mapping in this file.

// Timeouts of the stack routes. The routes that only start an operation answer
// as soon as it is queued; the others may run a lister or read files on the host.
const (
	dmStackReadTimeout   = 45 * time.Second // helpers, list, get, volumes, lint
	dmStackFileTimeout   = 30 * time.Second // file writes
	dmStackCreateTimeout = 45 * time.Second
	dmStackStartTimeout  = 15 * time.Second // prepare, ops, delete
	// dmStackBodyLimit bounds a request that carries compose and .env text: two
	// files of dockerstacks.MaxFileBytes, JSON-escaped.
	dmStackBodyLimit = 8 << 20
)

// dmCodeStacksUnavailable answers a stack route while the stacks service is not
// open (Server.DockerStacks is nil).
const dmCodeStacksUnavailable = "stacks_unavailable"

// dmStackService is what the stack handlers use of *dockerstacks.Service, so the
// handler tests can substitute a small fake.
type dmStackService interface {
	Helpers(ctx context.Context, hostID string) (dockerstacks.HelperStatus, error)
	Prepare(ctx context.Context, hostID string) (dockerstacks.Operation, error)
	List(ctx context.Context, hostID string, refresh bool) (dockerstacks.Listing, error)
	Get(ctx context.Context, hostID, name string) (dockerstacks.StackDetail, error)
	Create(ctx context.Context, hostID string, in dockerstacks.CreateInput) (dockerstacks.StackDetail, error)
	WriteFiles(ctx context.Context, hostID, name string, in dockerstacks.FilesInput) (dockerstacks.FileRevisions, error)
	Start(ctx context.Context, hostID, name, kind string, opts dockerstacks.OpOptions) (dockerstacks.Operation, error)
	Operation(ctx context.Context, id string) (dockerstacks.Operation, error)
	Operations(ctx context.Context, f dockerstacks.OperationFilter) ([]dockerstacks.Operation, error)
	Subscribe(id string) (dockerstacks.Operation, <-chan dockerstacks.Event, func(), error)
	ProjectAction(ctx context.Context, hostID, project, action string) error
	ProjectVolumes(ctx context.Context, hostID, name string) ([]dockerstacks.ProjectVolume, error)
	PublishedPorts(ctx context.Context, hostID, excludeProject string) ([]dockerstacks.PublishedPort, error)
}

var _ dmStackService = (*dockerstacks.Service)(nil)

// stackService returns the stacks service, or answers 503 stacks_unavailable.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackService() (dmStackService, bool) {
	if dm.stacks == nil {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, dmCodeStacksUnavailable, "The Docker stacks service is not available", nil)
		return nil, false
	}
	return dm.stacks, true
}

// dmStackStatus is the HTTP status of every code of internal/dockerstacks.
var dmStackStatus = map[string]int{
	dockerstacks.CodeStackNameInvalid:   http.StatusBadRequest,
	dockerstacks.CodeStackNotFound:      http.StatusNotFound,
	dockerstacks.CodeStackExists:        http.StatusConflict,
	dockerstacks.CodeRevisionConflict:   http.StatusConflict,
	dockerstacks.CodeOperationBusy:      http.StatusConflict,
	dockerstacks.CodeOperationNotFound:  http.StatusNotFound,
	dockerstacks.CodeInvalidOperation:   http.StatusBadRequest,
	dockerstacks.CodeFileTooLarge:       http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge,
	dockerstacks.CodeHostNotPrepared:    http.StatusConflict,
	dockerstacks.CodeRunnerImageMissing: http.StatusConflict,
	dockerstacks.CodeAPITooOld:          http.StatusConflict,
	dockerstacks.CodeStacksDirInvalid:   http.StatusConflict,
	dockerstacks.CodeConvertFailed:      http.StatusBadRequest,
}

// dmFailure is an error answer that is ready to be written.
type dmFailure struct {
	status  int
	code    string
	message string
	extra   dmFields
}

// stackFailureOf classifies the failures that internal/dockerstacks produces
// itself: *ConflictError (409 revision_conflict with the file and what is on the
// host), *BusyError (409 operation_in_progress with the running operation) and
// *Error (the status table above; its Fields join the envelope, but never replace
// status, code or message). ok is false for anything else: Engine, transport and
// registry errors.
func stackFailureOf(err error) (dmFailure, bool) {
	var conflict *dockerstacks.ConflictError
	var busy *dockerstacks.BusyError
	var coded *dockerstacks.Error
	switch {
	case errors.As(err, &conflict):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusConflict, dockerstacks.CodeRevisionConflict, conflict.Error(),
			dmFields{"file": conflict.File, "current": conflict.Current}}, true
	case errors.As(err, &busy):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusConflict, dockerstacks.CodeOperationBusy, busy.Error(),
			dmFields{"operation_id": busy.OperationID, "kind": busy.Kind}}, true
	case errors.As(err, &coded):
		status, known := dmStackStatus[coded.Code]
		if !known {
			status = http.StatusInternalServerError
		}
		extra := dmFields{}
		for key, value := range coded.Fields {
			if key != "status" && key != "code" && key != "message" {
				extra[key] = value
			}
		}
		return dmFailure{status, coded.Code, dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(coded.Error(), 512), extra}, true
	}
	return dmFailure{}, false
}

func (dm *dmRequest) writeFailure(f dmFailure) {
	dmWriteError(dm.w, f.status, f.code, f.message, f.extra)
}

// stackFailure answers an error of a call that touched the host's Engine: the
// coded failures above, an unknown host as 404 host_not_found, and anything else
// through engineFailure (docker_error, or host_unreachable with the reason).
func (dm *dmRequest) stackFailure(err error) {
	if f, ok := stackFailureOf(err); ok {
		dm.writeFailure(f)
		return
	}
	if errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound) {
		dm.hostFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dm.engineFailure(err, "")
}

// operationFailure answers an error of a call that never reaches an Engine:
// starting an operation (it only records one), reading the journal, the pure
// converter. An unknown host is 404; anything else is a logged 500 and must not
// be reported as an unreachable host.
func (dm *dmRequest) operationFailure(err error) {
	if f, ok := stackFailureOf(err); ok {
		dm.writeFailure(f)
		return
	}
	dm.hostFailure(err)
}

// decodeSized reads a JSON body of at most limit bytes. A body over the limit
// answers 413 file_too_large; anything else that is not JSON answers 400.
func (dm *dmRequest) decodeSized(dst any, limit int64) bool {
	body := http.MaxBytesReader(dm.w, dm.r.Body, limit)
	if err := json.NewDecoder(body).Decode(dst); err != nil {
		var tooLarge *http.MaxBytesError
		if errors.As(err, &tooLarge) {
			dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, dockerstacks.CodeFileTooLarge, "the request body is too large", nil)
			return false
		}
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeBadRequest, "the request body is not valid JSON", nil)
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// dmSlice turns a nil slice into an empty one, so a list always encodes as [].
func dmSlice[T any](items []T) []T {
	if items == nil {
		return []T{}
	}
	return items
}
```

`stackFailure` is for calls that reach an Engine (`engineFailure` classifies everything that is not a coded failure); `operationFailure` is for calls that only record an operation, read the journal or convert (an unknown host is a 404, anything else a logged 500, never `host_unreachable`).

```go
// dmFakeStacks stands in for *dockerstacks.Service in the handler tests. Every
// call is recorded as "Method arg arg"; errs[method] makes that method fail.
type dmFakeStacks struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	calls []string
	errs  map[string]error

	helpers   dockerstacks.HelperStatus
	listing   dockerstacks.Listing
	detail    dockerstacks.StackDetail
	revisions dockerstacks.FileRevisions
	operation dockerstacks.Operation
	history   []dockerstacks.Operation
	volumes   []dockerstacks.ProjectVolume
	ports     []dockerstacks.PublishedPort

	// Subscribe answers with snapshot and events (nil events = an already closed channel).
	snapshot dockerstacks.Operation
	events   chan dockerstacks.Event

	// What the last call received.
	create dockerstacks.CreateInput
	files  dockerstacks.FilesInput
	opts   dockerstacks.OpOptions
	filter dockerstacks.OperationFilter
	kind   string
}

func newDMFakeStacks() *dmFakeStacks { return &dmFakeStacks{errs: map[string]error{}} }

// record notes a call and returns the error configured for its method.
func (f *dmFakeStacks) record(call string) error {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.calls = append(f.calls, call)
	method, _, _ := strings.Cut(call, " ")
	return f.errs[method]
}

func (f *dmFakeStacks) called(call string) bool {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	for _, got := range f.calls {
		if got == call {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return len(f.calls)
}

	rec := f.serve(method, path, body)
	var decoded map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &decoded); err != nil {
		f.t.Fatalf("%s %s: answer %q is not JSON: %v", method, path, f.lastRaw, err)
	}
	return rec.Code, decoded
}

func (f *dmStackFixture) expectError(code int, body map[string]any, wantStatus int, wantCode string) {
	f.t.Helper()
	if code != wantStatus || body["status"] != "error" || body["code"] != wantCode {
		f.t.Fatalf("answer = %d %s, want %d error %q", code, f.lastRaw, wantStatus, wantCode)
	}
}
```

Create `internal/server/docker_manager_stacks.go`:

```go
package server

import (
	"net/http"

	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// ── Docker Manager stacks API: helpers, stacks, files, operations, projects ──
// Everything below /api/docker-manager/hosts/{id}/ that belongs to the stacks
// service. docker.readonly refuses prepare, create, file writes, operations,
// delete and project actions with 403 read_only; the reads, lint and convert
// change nothing and stay available.

// dmProjectActions are the actions of POST /hosts/{id}/projects/{project}/{action}.
var dmProjectActions = map[string]bool{"start": true, "stop": true, "restart": true}

// stackRoute serves the stack, operation, lint and convert routes. It returns
// false when the path matches none of them.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackRoute(segs []string) bool {
	switch {
	case len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] == "hosts" && segs[2] == "helpers":
		dm.helperStatus(segs[1])
	case len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] == "hosts" && segs[2] == "prepare":
		dm.prepareHost(segs[1])
	case len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] == "hosts" && segs[2] == "stacks":
		dm.stackCollection(segs[1])
	case len(segs) == 4 && segs[0] == "hosts" && segs[2] == "stacks":
		dm.stackItem(segs[1], segs[3])
	case len(segs) == 5 && segs[0] == "hosts" && segs[2] == "stacks":
		dm.stackSub(segs[1], segs[3], segs[4])
	case len(segs) == 5 && segs[0] == "hosts" && segs[2] == "projects":
		dm.projectAction(segs[1], segs[3], segs[4])
	default:
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// helperStatus serves GET /hosts/{id}/helpers: what the host has of the runner
// image and the IO container. It only reads.
func (dm *dmRequest) helperStatus(hostID string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackReadTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	helpers, err := svc.Helpers(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"helpers": helpers})
}

// prepareHost serves POST /hosts/{id}/prepare: it starts the prepare operation
// (runner image and IO container) and answers 202 with it.
func (dm *dmRequest) prepareHost(hostID string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodPost) {
		return
	}
	if dm.readOnly {
		dm.readOnlyRefusal()
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackStartTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	op, err := svc.Prepare(ctx, hostID)
	if err != nil {
		dm.operationFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusAccepted, dmFields{"operation": op})
}

// stackCollection serves GET and POST /hosts/{id}/stacks.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackCollection(hostID string) {
	switch dm.r.Method {
	case http.MethodGet:
		dm.stackList(hostID)
	case http.MethodPost:
		dm.stackCreate(hostID)
	default:
		dm.allow(http.MethodGet, http.MethodPost)
	}
}

// stackList serves GET /hosts/{id}/stacks[?refresh=1]. The listing's members sit
// at the top level of the answer.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackList(hostID string) {
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackReadTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	listing, err := svc.List(ctx, hostID, dmTruthy(dm.r.URL.Query().Get("refresh")))
	if err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{
		"host_id":    listing.HostID,
		"stacks_dir": listing.StacksDir,
		"stacks":     dmSlice(listing.Stacks),
		"external":   dmSlice(listing.External),
		"ignored":    dmSlice(listing.Ignored),
		"scanned_at": listing.ScannedAt,
		"cached":     listing.Cached,
	})
}

// dmStackCreate is the body of POST /hosts/{id}/stacks.
type dmStackCreate struct {
	dockerstacks.CreateInput
	Deploy bool `json:"deploy"`
}

// stackCreate serves POST /hosts/{id}/stacks: it writes the stack's files and,
// with deploy, starts the up operation. When the files were written but the
// operation could not be started, the answer is still 201 with the stack and a
// deploy_error member, so the client does not retry a create that succeeded.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackCreate(hostID string) {
	if dm.readOnly {
		dm.readOnlyRefusal()
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	var in dmStackCreate
	if !dm.decodeSized(&in, dmStackBodyLimit) {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackCreateTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	detail, err := svc.Create(ctx, hostID, in.CreateInput)
	if err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	fields := dmFields{"stack": detail}
	if in.Deploy {
		op, err := svc.Start(ctx, hostID, in.Name, dockerstacks.KindUp, dockerstacks.OpOptions{})
		if err != nil {
			failure, coded := stackFailureOf(err)
			if !coded {
				dm.s.logDockerManager("Docker stack deploy could not be started", err)
				failure = dmFailure{code: dmCodeInternal, message: "The deployment could not be started"}
			}
			fields["deploy_error"] = dmFields{"code": failure.code, "message": failure.message}
		} else {
			fields["operation"] = op
		}
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusCreated, fields)
}

// stackItem serves GET and DELETE /hosts/{id}/stacks/{name}.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackItem(hostID, name string) {
	switch dm.r.Method {
	case http.MethodGet:
		dm.stackGet(hostID, name)
	case http.MethodDelete:
		dm.stackDelete(hostID, name)
	default:
		dm.allow(http.MethodGet, http.MethodDelete)
	}
}

func (dm *dmRequest) stackGet(hostID, name string) {
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackReadTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	detail, err := svc.Get(ctx, hostID, name)
	if err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"stack": detail})
}

// stackDelete serves DELETE /hosts/{id}/stacks/{name}[?volumes=1]: it starts the
// delete operation (down, then the stack folder is removed) and answers 202.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackDelete(hostID, name string) {
	if dm.readOnly {
		dm.readOnlyRefusal()
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackStartTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	opts := dockerstacks.OpOptions{Volumes: dmTruthy(dm.r.URL.Query().Get("volumes"))}
	op, err := svc.Start(ctx, hostID, name, dockerstacks.KindDelete, opts)
	if err != nil {
		dm.operationFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusAccepted, dmFields{"operation": op})
}

// stackSub serves /hosts/{id}/stacks/{name}/{files|volumes|ops}.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackSub(hostID, name, sub string) {
	switch sub {
	case "files":
		dm.stackFiles(hostID, name)
	case "volumes":
		dm.stackVolumes(hostID, name)
	case "ops":
		dm.stackOperation(hostID, name)
	default:
		dm.notFound()
	}
}

// stackFiles serves PUT .../files: the compose file and/or the .env, each with
// the revision it was edited from. A file that changed on the host meanwhile is
// a 409 revision_conflict that carries what is on the host now.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackFiles(hostID, name string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodPut) {
		return
	}
	if dm.readOnly {
		dm.readOnlyRefusal()
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	var in dockerstacks.FilesInput
	if !dm.decodeSized(&in, dmStackBodyLimit) {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackFileTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	revisions, err := svc.WriteFiles(ctx, hostID, name, in)
	if err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"revisions": revisions})
}

// stackVolumes serves GET .../volumes: the volumes `down --volumes` would remove.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackVolumes(hostID, name string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackReadTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	volumes, err := svc.ProjectVolumes(ctx, hostID, name)
	if err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"volumes": dmSlice(volumes)})
}

// dmOperationRequest is the body of POST .../ops.
type dmOperationRequest struct {
	Kind    string `json:"kind"`
	Volumes bool   `json:"volumes"`
}

// stackOperation serves POST .../ops: it starts config, up, down, stop, restart,
// pull or update and answers 202 with the queued operation. Delete has its own
// route (DELETE on the stack), so that removing a stack is never one typo away.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackOperation(hostID, name string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodPost) {
		return
	}
	if dm.readOnly {
		dm.readOnlyRefusal()
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	var in dmOperationRequest
	if !dm.decode(&in) {
		return
	}
	if in.Kind == dockerstacks.KindDelete {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dockerstacks.CodeInvalidOperation, "delete is started with DELETE on the stack, not through ops", nil)
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackStartTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	op, err := svc.Start(ctx, hostID, name, in.Kind, dockerstacks.OpOptions{Volumes: in.Volumes})
	if err != nil {
		dm.operationFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusAccepted, dmFields{"operation": op})
}

// projectAction serves POST /hosts/{id}/projects/{project}/{start|stop|restart}:
// the action on every container of an external compose project, through the
// Engine's container API.
func (dm *dmRequest) projectAction(hostID, project, action string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodPost) {
		return
	}
	if !dmProjectActions[action] {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeInvalidAction, "unknown project action: "+dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(action, 32), nil)
		return
	}
	if dm.readOnly {
		dm.readOnlyRefusal()
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmActionTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	if err := svc.ProjectAction(ctx, hostID, project, action); err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, nil)
}
```

```go
package server

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
)

// dmSSEFrame is one block of an event stream: an event with its data, or a comment.
type dmSSEFrame struct {
	event, data, comment string
}

// dmParseSSE splits a finished stream into frames.
func dmParseSSE(t *testing.T, stream string) []dmSSEFrame {
	t.Helper()
	var frames []dmSSEFrame
	reader := bufio.NewReader(strings.NewReader(stream))
	for {
		frame, err := dmReadSSEFrame(reader)
		if err != nil {
			return frames
		}
		frames = append(frames, frame)
	}
}

// dmReadSSEFrame reads lines up to the blank line that ends a frame.
func dmReadSSEFrame(r *bufio.Reader) (dmSSEFrame, error) {
	var frame dmSSEFrame
	seen := false
	for {
		line, err := r.ReadString('\n')
		if err != nil {
			return frame, err
		}
		line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r\n")
		switch {
		case line == "":
			if seen {
				return frame, nil
			}
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, ": "):
			frame.comment, seen = strings.TrimPrefix(line, ": "), true
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "event: "):
			frame.event, seen = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "event: "), true
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "data: "):
			frame.data, seen = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "data: "), true
		}
	}
}

func dmOp(state, output string) dockerstacks.Operation {
	return dockerstacks.Operation{ID: "op_0123456789abcdef", HostID: "local", Stack: "web", Kind: dockerstacks.KindUp, State: state, Output: output}
}

func TestDockerManagerOperationListAndGet(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMStackFixture(t)

	// No operations: an empty array, never null.
	code, body := f.do(http.MethodGet, "/operations", nil)
	if code != http.StatusOK || len(dmArray(t, body, "operations")) != 0 || strings.Contains(f.lastRaw, "null") {
		t.Fatalf("empty list = %d %s, want an empty operations array", code, f.lastRaw)
	}

	// The filter reaches the service, and the list carries no output.
	f.fake.history = []dockerstacks.Operation{dmOp(dockerstacks.StateRunning, "secret output tail")}
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodGet, "/operations?host=local&stack=web&active=1&limit=5", nil)
	want := dockerstacks.OperationFilter{HostID: "local", Stack: "web", Active: true, Limit: 5}
	if got := dmArray(t, body, "operations"); code != http.StatusOK || len(got) != 1 || got[0]["output"] != "" || f.fake.filter != want {
		t.Fatalf("filtered list = %d %s (filter %+v), want one operation without output and filter %+v", code, f.lastRaw, f.fake.filter, want)
	}
	f.do(http.MethodGet, "/operations?limit=abc", nil)
	if f.fake.filter.Limit != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("filter = %+v, want no limit for a malformed ?limit", f.fake.filter)
	}

	// One operation carries its output; an unknown id is a 404.
	f.fake.operation = dmOp(dockerstacks.StateSucceeded, "all done")
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodGet, "/operations/op_0123456789abcdef", nil)
	if op := dmObject(t, body, "operation"); code != http.StatusOK || op["output"] != "all done" || op["state"] != "succeeded" {
		t.Fatalf("get = %d %s, want the operation with its output", code, f.lastRaw)
	}
	f.fake.errs["Operation"] = &dockerstacks.Error{Code: dockerstacks.CodeOperationNotFound, Message: "no such operation"}
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodGet, "/operations/op_ffffffffffffffff", nil)
	f.expectError(code, body, http.StatusNotFound, "operation_not_found")
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/operations", nil)
	f.expectError(code, body, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "method_not_allowed")
}

func TestDockerManagerOperationStreamOfAFinishedOperation(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMStackFixture(t)
	f.fake.snapshot = dmOp(dockerstacks.StateSucceeded, "all done")

	rec := f.serve(http.MethodGet, "/operations/op_0123456789abcdef/stream", nil)
	if ct := rec.Header().Get("Content-Type"); ct != "text/event-stream" || rec.Header().Get("Cache-Control") != "no-cache" || rec.Header().Get("X-Accel-Buffering") != "no" {
		t.Fatalf("headers = %v, want the event stream headers", rec.Header())
	}
	frames := dmParseSSE(t, rec.Body.String())
	if len(frames) != 2 || frames[0].event != "snapshot" || frames[1].event != "done" {
		t.Fatalf("frames = %+v, want snapshot then done", frames)
	}
	var snapshot dockerstacks.Operation
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(frames[0].data), &snapshot); err != nil || snapshot.Output != "all done" {
		t.Fatalf("snapshot data = %q (%v), want the operation with its output", frames[0].data, err)
	}
	if !f.fake.called("Unsubscribe op_0123456789abcdef") {
		t.Fatal("the subscription was not cancelled")
	}

	f.fake.errs["Subscribe"] = &dockerstacks.Error{Code: dockerstacks.CodeOperationNotFound, Message: "no such operation"}
	code, body := f.do(http.MethodGet, "/operations/op_ffffffffffffffff/stream", nil)
	f.expectError(code, body, http.StatusNotFound, "operation_not_found")
}

func TestDockerManagerOperationStreamEndsWhenTheChannelClosesWithoutDone(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMStackFixture(t)
	f.fake.snapshot = dmOp(dockerstacks.StateRunning, "pulling")
	f.fake.operation = dmOp(dockerstacks.StateRunning, "pulling") // what Operation answers afterwards

	// The subscriber was dropped (or AuraGo is closing) and the operation goes on: the stream just ends.
	rec := f.serve(http.MethodGet, "/operations/op_0123456789abcdef/stream", nil)
	frames := dmParseSSE(t, rec.Body.String())
	if len(frames) != 1 || frames[0].event != "snapshot" {
		t.Fatalf("frames = %+v, want only the snapshot so that the client reconnects", frames)
	}

	// The operation finished while the subscriber was away: the client still gets done.
	f.fake.operation = dmOp(dockerstacks.StateFailed, "boom")
	rec = f.serve(http.MethodGet, "/operations/op_0123456789abcdef/stream", nil)
	frames = dmParseSSE(t, rec.Body.String())
	if len(frames) != 2 || frames[1].event != "done" || !strings.Contains(frames[1].data, `"state":"failed"`) {
		t.Fatalf("frames = %+v, want snapshot then done with the final state", frames)
	}
}

func TestDockerManagerOperationStreamFollowsALiveOperation(t *testing.T) {
	old := dmSSEHeartbeat
	dmSSEHeartbeat = 20 * time.Millisecond
	t.Cleanup(func() { dmSSEHeartbeat = old })

	f := newDMStackFixture(t)
	f.fake.snapshot = dmOp(dockerstacks.StateRunning, "pulling")
	f.fake.events = make(chan dockerstacks.Event, 8)
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		dm := &dmRequest{s: f.s, w: w, r: r, stacks: f.fake}
		dm.route(dockerManagerSegments(r.URL.Path))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, srv.URL+"/api/docker-manager/operations/op_0123456789abcdef/stream", nil)
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	reader := bufio.NewReader(resp.Body)
	next := func() dmSSEFrame {
		t.Helper()
		frame, err := dmReadSSEFrame(reader)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("stream ended early: %v", err)
		}
		return frame
	}

	if frame := next(); frame.event != "snapshot" {
		t.Fatalf("first frame = %+v, want the snapshot", frame)
	}
	// A quiet stream writes comments.
	if frame := next(); frame.comment != "heartbeat" {
		t.Fatalf("second frame = %+v, want a heartbeat comment", frame)
	}

	progress := &dockerstacks.Progress{ID: "nginx", Status: "Downloading", Current: 5, Total: 10, Percent: 50}
	running := dmOp(dockerstacks.StateHealthWait, "")
	finished := dmOp(dockerstacks.StateSucceeded, "all done")
	f.fake.events <- dockerstacks.Event{Type: dockerstacks.EventOutput, Seq: 1, Text: "Container web Started\n"}
	f.fake.events <- dockerstacks.Event{Type: dockerstacks.EventProgress, Seq: 2, Progress: progress}
	f.fake.events <- dockerstacks.Event{Type: dockerstacks.EventState, Seq: 3, Operation: &running}
	f.fake.events <- dockerstacks.Event{Type: dockerstacks.EventDone, Seq: 4, Operation: &finished}

	var order []string
	for {
		frame, err := dmReadSSEFrame(reader)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("stream ended before done: %v (frames so far %v)", err, order)
		}
		if frame.event == "" {
			continue // heartbeats may interleave
		}
		order = append(order, frame.event)
		if frame.event == "output" && !strings.Contains(frame.data, "Container web Started") {
			t.Fatalf("output frame = %q, want the chunk", frame.data)
		}
		if frame.event == "progress" && !strings.Contains(frame.data, `"percent":50`) {
			t.Fatalf("progress frame = %q, want the parsed progress", frame.data)
		}
		if frame.event == "done" {
			if !strings.Contains(frame.data, `"output":"all done"`) {
				t.Fatalf("done frame = %q, want the full final operation", frame.data)
			}
			break
		}
	}
	if strings.Join(order, ",") != "output,progress,state,done" {
		t.Fatalf("events = %v, want output, progress, state, done in order", order)
	}
	// After done the handler returns: the connection reaches EOF and the subscription is cancelled.
	if _, err := io.ReadAll(reader); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("reading to the end of the stream: %v", err)
	}
	dmWaitFor(t, "the subscription to be cancelled", func() bool { return f.fake.called("Unsubscribe op_0123456789abcdef") })
}

func TestDockerManagerOperationStreamEndsWhenTheClientGoesAway(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMStackFixture(t)
	f.fake.snapshot = dmOp(dockerstacks.StateRunning, "")
	f.fake.events = make(chan dockerstacks.Event) // never delivers
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		dm := &dmRequest{s: f.s, w: w, r: r, stacks: f.fake}
		dm.route(dockerManagerSegments(r.URL.Path))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, srv.URL+"/api/docker-manager/operations/op_0123456789abcdef/stream", nil)
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if frame, err := dmReadSSEFrame(bufio.NewReader(resp.Body)); err != nil || frame.event != "snapshot" {
		t.Fatalf("first frame = %+v, %v, want the snapshot", frame, err)
	}
	cancel()
	dmWaitFor(t, "the handler to cancel its subscription after the client left", func() bool { return f.fake.called("Unsubscribe op_0123456789abcdef") })
}

// dmWaitFor polls cond for up to five seconds.
func dmWaitFor(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}
```

```go
package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
)

// ── Docker Manager operations API ───────────────────────────────────────────
// /api/docker-manager/operations: the journal of stack operations and the live
// stream of one. Reading is allowed in docker.readonly mode.

const (
	// dmSSEWriteTimeout bounds each write of an event stream, so a client that
	// stops reading ends the stream instead of pinning the handler; heartbeats
	// re-arm it. The API listeners' httpstream wrapper renews its own budget per
	// write too. The deadline is never cleared (a stuck client must time out).
	dmSSEWriteTimeout = 30 * time.Second
)

// dmSSEHeartbeat is how long an idle operation stream stays silent before it
// writes a comment line. A variable so that a test can shorten it.
var dmSSEHeartbeat = 15 * time.Second

// operationRoute serves the operation routes. It returns false when the path is
// none of them.
func (dm *dmRequest) operationRoute(segs []string) bool {
	switch {
	case len(segs) == 1 && segs[0] == "operations":
		dm.operationList()
	case len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] == "operations":
		dm.operationGet(segs[1])
	case len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] == "operations" && segs[2] == "stream":
		dm.operationStream(segs[1])
	default:
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// operationList serves GET /operations[?host=&stack=&active=1&limit=]: newest
// first, without their output (the operation itself has it).
func (dm *dmRequest) operationList() {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	query := dm.r.URL.Query()
	filter := dockerstacks.OperationFilter{
		HostID: query.Get("host"),
		Stack:  query.Get("stack"),
		Active: dmTruthy(query.Get("active")),
	}
	if limit, err := strconv.Atoi(query.Get("limit")); err == nil && limit > 0 {
		filter.Limit = limit // the service clamps it to 100
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmRegistryTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	ops, err := svc.Operations(ctx, filter)
	if err != nil {
		dm.operationFailure(err)
		return
	}
	for i := range ops {
		ops[i].Output = ""
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"operations": dmSlice(ops)})
}

// operationGet serves GET /operations/{id}: the operation with its output tail.
func (dm *dmRequest) operationGet(id string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmRegistryTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	op, err := svc.Operation(ctx, id)
	if err != nil {
		dm.operationFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"operation": op})
}

// dmEventStream writes server-sent events, one write deadline per write.
type dmEventStream struct {
	w       http.ResponseWriter
	flusher http.Flusher
	rc      *http.ResponseController
}

// arm sets the write deadline for the next frame. Writers without deadline
// support (httptest recorders) own their transport.
func (st *dmEventStream) arm() error {
	if err := st.rc.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(dmSSEWriteTimeout)); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrNotSupported) {
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

// send writes one event whose data is the compact JSON of data (one "data:"
// line) and flushes it.
func (st *dmEventStream) send(event string, data any) error {
	raw, err := json.Marshal(data)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := st.arm(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(st.w, "event: %s\ndata: %s\n\n", event, raw); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	st.flusher.Flush()
	return nil
}

// comment writes an SSE comment line, which keeps proxies and the write
// deadline alive on a quiet stream.
func (st *dmEventStream) comment(text string) error {
	if err := st.arm(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(st.w, ": %s\n\n", text); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	st.flusher.Flush()
	return nil
}

// operationStream serves GET /operations/{id}/stream as text/event-stream:
//
//   - "event: snapshot": the Operation with the output so far;
//   - "event: output", "progress", "state": the service's Event as JSON;
//   - "event: done": the finished Operation, after which the handler returns;
//   - ": heartbeat" comments while nothing happens.
//
// A finished operation answers snapshot and done at once. When the service
// closes the channel without a done event (the subscriber fell 256 events
// behind, or AuraGo is shutting down) the handler looks the operation up once
// more: a finished one still gets its done event, any other stream just ends and
// the client reconnects for a fresh snapshot. The handler starts no goroutine and
// returns when the client goes away; the subscription is always cancelled.
func (dm *dmRequest) operationStream(id string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	flusher, ok := dm.w.(http.Flusher)
	if !ok {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusInternalServerError, dmCodeInternal, "streaming is not supported", nil)
		return
	}
	snapshot, events, cancel, err := svc.Subscribe(id)
	if err != nil {
		dm.operationFailure(err)
		return
	}
	defer cancel()

	header := dm.w.Header()
	header.Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
	header.Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
	header.Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
	dm.w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
	stream := &dmEventStream{w: dm.w, flusher: flusher, rc: http.NewResponseController(dm.w)}

	if stream.send("snapshot", snapshot) != nil {
		return
	}
	if snapshot.Done() {
		_ = stream.send(dockerstacks.EventDone, snapshot)
		return
	}
	beat := time.NewTicker(dmSSEHeartbeat)
	defer beat.Stop()
	ctx := dm.r.Context()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		case <-beat.C:
			if stream.comment("heartbeat") != nil {
				return
			}
		case ev, open := <-events:
			switch {
			case !open:
				dm.finishClosedStream(ctx, svc, stream, id)
				return
			case ev.Type == dockerstacks.EventDone:
				if ev.Operation != nil {
					_ = stream.send(dockerstacks.EventDone, *ev.Operation)
				} else {
					dm.finishClosedStream(ctx, svc, stream, id)
				}
				return
			default:
				if stream.send(ev.Type, ev) != nil {
					return
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// finishClosedStream handles a channel that closed without a done event: if the
// operation has finished in the meantime the client gets its done event now;
// otherwise nothing more is sent and the client reconnects.
func (dm *dmRequest) finishClosedStream(ctx context.Context, svc dmStackService, stream *dmEventStream, id string) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, dmRegistryTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	if op, err := svc.Operation(ctx, id); err == nil && op.Done() {
		_ = stream.send(dockerstacks.EventDone, op)
	}
}
```

```go
const dmLintCompose = "services:\n  web:\n    image: nginx:1.27\n    restart: always\n    ports:\n      - \"8080:80\"\n"

// dmDiagnosticCodes lists the codes of a lint answer.
func dmDiagnosticCodes(t *testing.T, body map[string]any) []string {
	t.Helper()
	var codes []string
	for _, d := range dmArray(t, body, "diagnostics") {
		codes = append(codes, d["code"].(string))
	}
	return codes
}

func TestDockerManagerLintReadsThePortsOfTheHost(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMStackFixture(t)
	f.fake.ports = []dockerstacks.PublishedPort{{Port: 8080, Protocol: "tcp", Container: "other", Project: "shop"}}

	code, body := f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/local/lint", map[string]any{"compose": dmLintCompose, "env": "", "stack": "web"})
	if code != http.StatusOK || !f.fake.called("PublishedPorts local web") || body["ports_unchecked"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("lint = %d %s, want 200 with the ports of the host read for stack web", code, f.lastRaw)
	}
	if codes := dmDiagnosticCodes(t, body); len(codes) != 1 || codes[0] != "port_conflict" {
		t.Fatalf("diagnostics = %v, want only port_conflict", codes)
	}
	services := dmArray(t, dmObject(t, body, "preview"), "services")
	if ports, _ := services[0]["ports"].([]any); len(ports) != 1 || ports[0].(map[string]any)["conflict"] != "other" {
		t.Fatalf("preview = %s, want the conflicting container named on the port", f.lastRaw)
	}

	// A host that cannot be read: lint without port conflicts, and say so.
	f.fake.errs["PublishedPorts"] = errors.New("dial tcp 10.0.0.5:2375: connect: connection refused")
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/local/lint", map[string]any{"compose": dmLintCompose})
	if code != http.StatusOK || body["ports_unchecked"] != true || len(dmDiagnosticCodes(t, body)) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("lint on an unreachable host = %d %s, want 200, no diagnostics and ports_unchecked", code, f.lastRaw)
	}
	// So does a server whose stacks service is not open.
	f.noStacks = true
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/local/lint", map[string]any{"compose": dmLintCompose})
	if code != http.StatusOK || body["ports_unchecked"] != true {
		t.Fatalf("lint without the stacks service = %d %s, want 200 with ports_unchecked", code, f.lastRaw)
	}
	f.noStacks = false

	// A wrong host id is the caller's mistake, not a missing ports check.
	f.fake.errs["PublishedPorts"] = dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/h_000000000000/lint", map[string]any{"compose": dmLintCompose})
	f.expectError(code, body, http.StatusNotFound, "host_not_found")
	delete(f.fake.errs, "PublishedPorts")

	// Syntax errors come back as diagnostics with their line, not as an HTTP error; lint changes nothing, so
	// read-only mode does not block it.
	f.readOnly = true
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/local/lint", map[string]any{"compose": "a: [\n"})
	diagnostics := dmArray(t, body, "diagnostics")
	if code != http.StatusOK || len(diagnostics) != 1 || diagnostics[0]["code"] != "yaml_syntax" || diagnostics[0]["line"] != float64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("lint of broken YAML = %d %s, want one yaml_syntax diagnostic on line 1", code, f.lastRaw)
	}
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodGet, "/hosts/local/lint", nil)
	f.expectError(code, body, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "method_not_allowed")
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/local/lint", strings.Repeat("{", 3))
	f.expectError(code, body, http.StatusBadRequest, "bad_request")
}
```

```go
package server

import (
	"errors"
	"net/http"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
)

// ── Docker Manager lint and docker run converter ────────────────────────────
// Both are pure functions of the request (dockerstacks.Lint and
// dockerstacks.ConvertDockerRun): they change nothing on any host, so they stay
// available in docker.readonly mode.

// dmConvertMaxBytes bounds the command of a convert request. The converter
// takes no context, so its work is bounded by its input instead of a timeout.
const dmConvertMaxBytes = 64 << 10

// lintRoute serves the lint and convert routes. It returns false when the path
// is neither.
func (dm *dmRequest) lintRoute(segs []string) bool {
	switch {
	case len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] == "hosts" && segs[2] == "lint":
		dm.lintStack(segs[1])
	case len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] == "convert" && segs[1] == "docker-run":
		dm.convertDockerRun()
	default:
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// lintStack serves POST /hosts/{id}/lint: diagnostics and a preview for a
// compose file and its .env. The ports other containers publish on the host are
// read for the conflict check; when the host cannot be read (or the stacks
// service is not open) the lint runs without them and the answer says
// ports_unchecked. An unknown host id is a 404.
func (dm *dmRequest) lintStack(hostID string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodPost) {
		return
	}
	var in dockerstacks.LintInput
	if !dm.decodeSized(&in, dmStackBodyLimit) {
		return
	}
	var published []dockerstacks.PublishedPort
	unchecked := true
	if dm.stacks != nil {
		ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackReadTimeout)
		defer cancel()
		ports, err := dm.stacks.PublishedPorts(ctx, hostID, in.Stack)
		switch {
		case err == nil:
			published, unchecked = ports, false
		case errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound):
			dm.hostFailure(err)
			return
		}
	}
	result := dockerstacks.Lint(in, published)
	fields := dmFields{"diagnostics": dmSlice(result.Diagnostics), "preview": result.Preview}
	if unchecked {
		fields["ports_unchecked"] = true
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, fields)
}

// dmConvertRequest is the body of POST /convert/docker-run.
type dmConvertRequest struct {
	Command string `json:"command"`
}

// convertDockerRun serves POST /convert/docker-run: one `docker run` command in,
// compose YAML and the warnings for flags that could not be converted out.
func (dm *dmRequest) convertDockerRun() {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodPost) {
		return
	}
	var in dmConvertRequest
	if !dm.decode(&in) {
		return
	}
	if len(in.Command) > dmConvertMaxBytes {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dockerstacks.CodeConvertFailed, "The command is longer than 64 KiB.", nil)
		return
	}
	result, err := dockerstacks.ConvertDockerRun(in.Command)
	if err != nil {
		dm.operationFailure(err)
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{
		"compose":  result.Compose,
		"service":  result.Service,
		"warnings": dmSlice(result.Warnings),
	})
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing tests**

The container list (remote and local host) marks the three helper roles with `aurago_helper` and the owner `docker_manager` and leaves ordinary containers alone. Removing a helper by name or ID prefix is a 409 `container_protected_confirmation_required` with owner `docker_manager` on a remote and on the local host, nothing reaches the Engine, `confirm=protected` goes through, an ordinary container is unaffected, and readonly still refuses first. The host test carries the helper status of the (fake) Engine; an unreachable host and a server without the stacks service answer without it.

Create `internal/server/docker_manager_helpers_test.go`:

```go
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
)

// setContainers replaces the container list the fake engine answers with.
func (e *dmFakeEngine) setContainers(raw string) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.containers = raw
}

// dmHelperContainers is a list with the three helper roles next to an ordinary container.
func dmHelperContainers(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	return dmContainersJSON(t,
		dmContainerJSON('1', "aurago-dm-op-op_0123456789abcdef", "sha256:img1", "exited", "none",
			map[string]string{dockerstacks.LabelRole: dockerstacks.RoleRunner, dockerstacks.LabelOperation: "op_0123456789abcdef"}, nil),
		dmContainerJSON('2', dockerstacks.IOContainerName, "sha256:img1", "created", "none",
			map[string]string{dockerstacks.LabelRole: dockerstacks.RoleIO, dockerstacks.LabelStacksDir: "/opt/stacks"}, nil),
		dmContainerJSON('3', "aurago-dm-ls-0a1b2c3d", "sha256:img1", "exited", "none",
			map[string]string{dockerstacks.LabelRole: dockerstacks.RoleLister}, nil),
		dmContainerJSON('4', "blog", "sha256:img2", "running", "bridge", nil, nil),
	)
}

func TestDockerManagerContainerListFlagsHelpers(t *testing.T) {

			dockerstacks.IOContainerName:       dockerstacks.RoleIO,
			"aurago-dm-ls-0a1b2c3d":            dockerstacks.RoleLister,
		} {

			if helper["aurago_helper"] != role || helper["protected_owner"] != "docker_manager" {
				t.Errorf("%s: %s = %v, want aurago_helper %q and protected_owner docker_manager", host, name, helper, role)
			}

			t.Errorf("%s: blog = %v, want no helper flag and no owner", host, blog)
```
