```go
}

func TestDockerManagerRemovingAHelperAsksForConfirmation(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMFixture(t)
	id := f.addRemote("NAS")
	f.remote.setContainers(dmHelperContainers(t))
	f.local.setContainers(dmHelperContainers(t))
	defer replaceContainerProtection(containerProtection{})() // the local classification itself is not under test here
	base := "/hosts/" + id + "/containers/"

	// By name and by ID prefix, the helper is protected; nothing reaches the engine unconfirmed.
	for _, ref := range []string{dockerstacks.IOContainerName, strings.Repeat("1", 12)} {
		code, body := f.do(http.MethodDelete, base+ref, nil)
		dmExpectError(t, f, code, body, http.StatusConflict, containerCodeConfirmationRequired)
		if body["owner"] != "docker_manager" || !strings.Contains(body["message"].(string), "confirm=protected") {
			t.Fatalf("unconfirmed remove of %s = %s, want owner docker_manager and the repeat hint", ref, f.lastRaw)
		}
	}
	if f.remote.called("DELETE /containers/"+dockerstacks.IOContainerName) || f.remote.called("DELETE /containers/"+strings.Repeat("1", 12)) {
		t.Fatalf("an unconfirmed remove reached the engine: %v", f.remote.calls)
	}
	code, _ := f.do(http.MethodDelete, base+dockerstacks.IOContainerName+"?confirm=protected", nil)
	if code != http.StatusOK || !f.remote.called("DELETE /containers/"+dockerstacks.IOContainerName) {

		t.Fatalf("local unconfirmed remove = %s, calls %v", f.lastRaw, f.local.calls)

func TestDockerManagerHostTestCarriesTheHelperStatus(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMFixture(t)
	id := f.addRemote("NAS")

	// The fake engine has no runner image and an IO container without the Docker Manager's labels.
	code, body := f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/"+id+"/test", nil)
	helpers := dmObject(t, body, "helpers")
	if code != http.StatusOK || helpers["api_version"] != "1.45" || helpers["api_supported"] != true || helpers["runner_image"] != dockerstacks.RunnerImageTag ||
		helpers["runner_image_present"] != false || helpers["io_container"] != "mismatch" || helpers["prepared"] != false {
		t.Fatalf("test = %d %s, want the helper status of an unprepared host", code, f.lastRaw)
	}

	// An unreachable host answers without helpers, and a server without the stacks service never adds them.
	f.remote.srv.Close()
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/"+id+"/test", nil)
	if code != http.StatusOK || body["helpers"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("unreachable test = %d %s, want no helpers member", code, f.lastRaw)
	}
	stacks := f.s.DockerStacks
	f.s.DockerStacks = nil
	t.Cleanup(stacks.Close)
	code, body = f.do(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/local/test", nil)
	if code != http.StatusOK || body["helpers"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("test without the stacks service = %d %s, want no helpers member", code, f.lastRaw)
	}
}
```

```go
// containers (runner, lister and IO container): removing one needs the same

	switch role := labels[dockerstacks.LabelRole]; role {
	case dockerstacks.RoleRunner, dockerstacks.RoleIO, dockerstacks.RoleLister:

	}
	return ""
```

```go
// network, owner). Any other remote host has its own Engine and its own
// containers: the owner from names and labels, plus the self check on the
// container's full ID (an Engine reached by another route, such as an SSH or
// tcp host on AuraGo's own machine, can still hold the container AuraGo runs
// in). The Docker Manager's helper containers are checked first, on every
// host. It writes the 409 and returns false when the request stops.
func (dm *dmRequest) removeAllowed(ctx context.Context, host dockerhost.Host, client *dockerutil.Client, ref string) bool {
```

```go
// remoteContainerProtection finds the container by name, full ID or ID prefix
```

new_string:

```go
// helperRemoveAllowed asks for the protected confirmation before one of the
// Docker Manager's helper containers is removed. The helpers carry no
// aurago.managed label (the stacks service owns their labels), so the owner
// rules of the other hosts cannot see them; the container is found in the host's
// list by name, full ID or ID prefix. A request that already carries
// confirm=protected makes no extra request. A failing list stops the removal:
// whether the target is a helper is not known then. It writes the answer and
// returns false when the request stops.
func (dm *dmRequest) helperRemoveAllowed(ctx context.Context, client *dockerutil.Client, ref string) bool {
	if dm.r.URL.Query().Get(containerConfirmParam) == containerConfirmProtected {
		return true
	}
	list, err := dockerhost.ListContainers(ctx, client)
	if err != nil {
		dm.engineFailure(err, "")
		return false
	}
	needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
	for _, container := range list {
		if dmContainerMatches(container, needle) && dmHelperRole(container.Labels) != "" {
			p := containerProtection{Owner: dmHelperOwner}
			dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusConflict, containerCodeConfirmationRequired, p.confirmationMessage(), dmFields{"owner": p.label()})
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// remoteContainerProtection finds the container by name, full ID or ID prefix
```

- [ ] **Step 4: DOX: record the contracts in the server guide**

`internal/server/AGENTS.md` owns the server's HTTP contracts and had no Docker Manager section (phase 1 only added the package guide `internal/dockerhost/AGENTS.md`). Re-read the guide chain first (root `AGENTS.md`, then this guide), then add the section in front of `### Code Studio`:

In `internal/server/AGENTS.md`:

old_string:

```markdown
### Code Studio
```

new_string:

```markdown
### Docker Manager API

- `/api/docker-manager/` (`docker_manager_api.go`: one router for hosts, containers, resources and stacks) uses the generic `/api/` auth like `/api/containers`: a browser session or a Bearer token with the `admin` scope, no auth code of its own, never 401. Envelope `{"status":"ok",…}` or `{"status":"error","code","message",…}`. Docker disabled is 503 `docker_disabled`, a missing registry 503 `docker_hosts_unavailable`, a missing stacks service 503 `stacks_unavailable`. `docker.readonly` (read per request) refuses container actions and removal, host prepare, stack create, file writes, operations, stack delete and project actions with 403 `read_only`; reads, lint, convert, host management and the operation stream stay open.
- Wiring: `initDockerHosts` (`docker_manager_service.go`) opens `docker_manager.db`, the host registry and then `dockerstacks.Open(store.DB(), registry, …)`; `closeDockerHosts` stops the stacks service before the registry and the store. A store failure leaves `DockerHosts` nil; a stacks failure leaves only `DockerStacks` nil (hosts and containers keep working, lint answers `ports_unchecked`, convert needs no service). `Open` reattaches operations that were running when AuraGo stopped.
- The stack handlers (`docker_manager_stacks.go`, `docker_manager_operations.go`, `docker_manager_lint.go`) call the service through the narrow `dmStackService` interface (`*dockerstacks.Service` satisfies it; handler tests use `dmFakeStacks`). `stackFailureOf` is the only mapping of `dockerstacks` failures: `*Error` by `Code` through `dmStackStatus` with its `Fields` merged into the envelope (never over status, code or message), `*ConflictError` → 409 `revision_conflict` with `file` and `current`, `*BusyError` → 409 `operation_in_progress` with `operation_id` and `kind`. Calls that reach an Engine answer every other error through `engineFailure` (`stackFailure`); calls that only record an operation, read the journal or convert answer it as an unknown host or a logged 500 (`operationFailure`) and never as `host_unreachable`. A body with compose or `.env` text may be 8 MiB (413 `file_too_large` above that); the file limit itself belongs to the service.
- `POST …/stacks` with `deploy` starts the up operation after the files exist; when only the start fails the answer stays 201 with `deploy_error {code,message}`, so a client never repeats a create that succeeded. `POST …/ops` refuses `delete` (400 `invalid_operation`; `DELETE …/stacks/{name}` is the only way to delete a stack). `POST /hosts/{id}/test` adds `helpers` when the Engine answered and the status could be read.
- `GET /operations/{id}/stream` is `text/event-stream`: `snapshot` (the operation with its output), `output`, `progress` and `state` (the service's `Event`), `done` (the final operation), then the handler returns. An idle stream writes a comment every `dmSSEHeartbeat` (15 s), and a write deadline (30 s) is armed before every write (`dmEventStream`). A channel that closes without `done` (the subscriber fell 256 events behind, or AuraGo is closing) ends the stream after one more look at the operation: finished → `done`, otherwise nothing, and the client reconnects for a fresh snapshot. The handler starts no goroutine and always cancels its subscription. Operation lists never carry output.
- The Docker Manager's helper containers (label `aurago.docker-manager.role` = `runner`, `io` or `lister`, created by `internal/dockerstacks`) carry no `aurago.managed` label, so `dmHelperRole` recognizes them by that label alone. The container list reports `aurago_helper` and `protected_owner: docker_manager`; removal on every host asks for `confirm=protected` first (409 `container_protected_confirmation_required`, owner `docker_manager`; `helperRemoveAllowed` makes one extra list request, none when the request already confirms, and a failing list stops the removal) before the host's own classification runs. Other container actions never ask, as for every owner. `/api/containers` does not know the helpers.
- Verify `go test ./internal/server -run '(?i)(TestDockerManager|TestInitDockerHosts)'` and `go test ./internal/audit -run Manifest` (the `/api/docker-manager/` contract lists `text/event-stream`). Stack behaviour is in `../dockerstacks/AGENTS.md`, hosts and Engine reads in `../dockerhost/AGENTS.md`.

### Code Studio
```

### Open questions for the owner of Part A and the integrator

1. **Reads in docker.readonly mode are not free of Engine writes.** `Service.target` starts the one-time helper sweep (removes exited runners and old listers of finished operations) on first contact with a host, and `List` runs a lister container. Contract decision 10 gates only prepare, create, file writes, operations, delete and project actions, so Part C follows it; if the user wants readonly to mean "no Engine writes at all", the service needs an `Options.ReadOnly func() bool` consulted by the sweep and the lister (then `List` would answer from the container list alone).
2. **A closing service** (`errServiceClosed`, unexported) comes out of `Start`/`Prepare` as a logged 500 `internal_error`. It can only happen during shutdown; an exported sentinel would let the server answer 503.
3. **The legacy Containers page and the agent docker tool** do not know the helpers: `/api/containers` shows them as ordinary containers and the agent tool may remove them (they are re-created by the next prepare). Adding `docker_manager` to `containerProtectedOwners` and the agent list needs `aurago.managed=docker_manager` labels from Part A plus the 16 manuals; left out on purpose (deviation 7).
4. **No per-client limit on open operation streams** (the flows stream has one). The route is admin-only and each stream is one goroutine and a 256-event buffer.

## Part D: the desktop app (`ui/`)

Part D is the UI of Docker Manager phase 2 (Stacks): the CodeMirror bundle with YAML and the lint pieces, six new modules (`stack-model`, `stacks`, `editor`, `ops`, `palette`, `newstack`), extended `model`, `store`, `views`, `dialogs` and composition root, the stylesheet, the strings in all 16 locales, the Node and browser tests, and the DOX guide. The last task applies the UI follow-ups of the phase 1 review (Part E of the contract).

**Prerequisites.** Phase 1 is merged (`13de9d026`). Parts A to C are **not** needed to build or test this part: the UI codes against the contract's routes and JSON, the Node tests use a fake API and a fake `EventSource`, and the browser smoke serves its own fake `/api/docker-manager/` (including an SSE stream). `node_modules` must exist (it holds `@codemirror/lang-yaml` 6.1.3 and `rollup`); **never run `npm install` or `npm ci`** for this part. Headless Chrome is needed for the browser tests (`AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1`); on this Windows box run them with the PowerShell tool and the sandbox off (`reference_chrome_launch_from_agent`). Commands below are PowerShell from the repository root.

**How the code was verified.** Everything below was applied, task by task, to a scratch checkout of `13de9d026` and run there: after every task the Node test (`node scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`), the Go guards (`TestDockerManager*`, `TestDesktopDynamicI18nPrefixKeysExistInAllLanguages`, `TestCodeMirrorBundleExportsYAMLAndLint`, `TestFrontend_StaticI18nKeysExistInEnglishBundle`, which only fails for two `help.chromecast.*` keys that `main` is missing), and from Task D12 on the two browser tests in headless Chrome against the rebuilt bundle; `npm run check:ui` and the whole `./ui` package at the end. While the stylesheet was written the app was also driven in headless Chrome and screenshotted (dark theme and Fruity light: stack list, stack pane, compose editor with lint, conflict and delete dialogs, palette, new-stack view); that review changed the layout of the new-stack view (fixed header and footer), the height of the progress drawer, and removed a duplicate card for an unreachable host. The code in the plan is that verified code: new files are given in full, edits as exact old/new pairs generated from the verified states (each old text matches exactly once), the two files that change in most places (`docker-manager.js`, the browser test) are given whole. The line numbers of an edit are the lines of the file as the previous task left it (`13de9d026` for the first edit of a file).

**Conventions.** Files in a Windows working tree have CRLF line endings; the Edit tool matches the old texts regardless. None of the code contains a backslash followed by `u`, so the Write and Edit tools do not alter it. Helper scripts go to `disposable\` (never staged); every commit adds exact paths. The strings come in one rows file per task (`[key, en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pt, pl, sv, da, no, cs, el, hi, ja, zh]`) merged by a script that checks the text count and the `{{placeholders}}` of every row. All 16 locales get real translations; Greek, Hindi, Japanese and Chinese were written without a native reviewer, like the phase 1 strings (see the phase 1 notes: have a native speaker look at `el`, `hi`, `ja`, `zh` before a release).

**Order and what runs when.** D1 to D10 add code without changing what the app does: from D5 on `views.rail(snap)` needs fields that only the new root provides, so **the app is not runnable between D5 and D12**; the Node tests are the check in between, and each task states exactly what they print. D11 wires the loader and the stylesheet, D12 swaps the root and brings the browser smoke, D13 is the follow-up task.

### Deviations from the contract

1. **The workbench lives in `docker-manager-editor.js`.** The contract names the editor module "CodeMirror YAML wrapper, lint gutter, fallback textarea". The per-stack drafts, the save with a revision and the conflict flow need a home and the contract's module list is exact, so `createWorkbench` is a second factory of the editor module (Task D6). The progress drawer's commands (`run`, `prepare`, `remove`, `done`) are likewise part of `docker-manager-ops.js`.
2. **Lint diagnostics are routed to their file by code.** `Diagnostic` has no file field. The UI treats `env_syntax` as a `.env` diagnostic and every other code as a compose diagnostic (`stackModel.diagnosticFile`). Part B also sets `params.file` to `.env` for `env_syntax`; the UI does not need it. If another code ever needs a different file, change that one function.
3. **Placeholders of the localized lint texts.** Part B's final `Params` are: `yaml_syntax` {detail}; `not_a_mapping` {what}; `service_no_image` (the service comes from `Diagnostic.Service`); `invalid_port` {value, reason}; `port_duplicate` {port, protocol, first_line}; `port_conflict` {port, protocol, container, project}; `variable_missing` {variable}; `env_syntax` {file, detail}; `image_latest` and `image_no_tag` {image}; `docker_socket` {source}; `cap_add` {caps}. The texts use `{{service}}` (taken from `Diagnostic.Service`), and from `Params`: `detail` (`yaml_syntax`), `value` (`invalid_port`), `port` (`port_duplicate`, `port_conflict`), `container` (`port_conflict`), `variable` (`variable_missing`); the other params reach the text function but no current text shows them. A text whose placeholder stays open and any code the UI does not know show the server's English `message` instead (`stackModel.diagnosticText`).
4. **`views.js` gets `gate` and `diffHtml`, `stack-model` gets a few helpers the contract does not list** (`formatBytes`, `age`, `clock`, `portLinks`, `linkAddress`, the stream reducer). They are pure and tested.
5. **Error bodies the UI reads** (`normalizeError(...).data` is the whole body): `host_not_prepared` with `helpers` (`runner_image`, `runner_image_present`, `io_container`), `api_too_old` with `api_version`, `runner_image_missing` with `command`, `revision_conflict` with `file` and `current` (a `FileContent`), `operation_in_progress` with `operation_id`. All are in the contract's error table; the answers must carry the fields as listed there. A create with `deploy: true` that wrote the files but could not start the deployment is no HTTP error: it answers 201 with `deploy_error` (`{code, message}`) and no `operation`. The list `GET /operations` carries `output: ""` on every operation; the UI never lets that replace the output it holds.
6. **The palette button key is `palette_button`.** `palette_<action>` is the key family of the commands, so the toolbar label cannot be `palette_open`.
7. **Only some actions ask the server to rescan (`?refresh=1`):** the Refresh button, the end of an operation, a create, a project action and a host retry. Polls and section switches use the server's 30 s listing cache.
8. **One defect of phase 1 fixed in the follow-up task** (D13): the row menu button of the Containers table opened the desktop context menu and the same click closed it again.
9. **`menus-and-routing.js` is not changed.** The Docker Manager `ctx` keeps `esc, t, api, setWindowMenus, clearWindowMenus, showContextMenu, wireContextMenuBoundary, readonly`; the app has its own `<dialog>` and toasts, so the missing `notify` and `modalDialog` are not needed and no bundle is regenerated.
10. **No user-facing documentation page.** Phase 1 documented the app only in the DOX guide `ui/js/desktop/apps/AGENTS.md`; Task D12 extends that section.

### What the UI expects from the backend (Parts A to C)

| Call | Fields the UI uses |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /hosts/{h}/stacks[?refresh=1]` | `stacks[]` (`name`, `dir`, `compose_file`, `has_env`, `status`, `services.{total,running}`, `ports[]`, `created`, `operation`), `external[]` (`name`, `working_dir`, `status`, `services`, `ports`), `ignored[]` (`name`); 409 `host_not_prepared` / `api_too_old` / `stacks_dir_unavailable`, 503 `stacks_unavailable` |
| `GET /hosts/{h}/stacks/{name}` | `stack` = summary + `service_list[]` (`name`, `image`, `state`, `health`, `exit_code`, `container_id` (12 characters, matched against the container list's `id`), `ports[]`), `compose`, `env` (`name`, `content`, `revision`, `exists`), `parse_error` |
| `PUT .../files` | body `{compose?: {content, revision}, env?: {...}}`; answer `revisions`; 409 `revision_conflict` with `file`, `current` |
| `POST /hosts/{h}/stacks` | body `{name, compose, env?, deploy?}`; 201 `{stack, operation?, deploy_error?}` (`deploy_error` is `{code, message}`: the files were written but the deployment could not start, there is no `operation`) |
| `POST .../ops`, `DELETE .../stacks/{name}[?volumes=1]`, `POST /hosts/{h}/prepare` | 202 `{operation}`; 409 `operation_in_progress` with `operation_id` |
| `GET /operations?active=1`, `GET /operations/{id}`, SSE `/operations/{id}/stream` | `Operation` fields (`id`, `host_id`, `stack`, `kind`, `state`, `output`, `error`, `error_line`, `warning`, `ports`, `created_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at`); SSE events `snapshot` (an `Operation`), `output`, `progress`, `state` (an `Event`), `done` (an `Operation`) |
| `POST /hosts/{h}/lint` | `diagnostics[]` (`line`, `column`, `severity`, `code`, `message`, `params`, `service`, `fix`), `preview` (`services[]`, `named_volumes`, `variables[]`), `ports_unchecked` |
| `POST /convert/docker-run` | `compose`, `service`, `warnings[]` (`code`, `flag`, `message`) |
| `GET .../volumes`, `POST /hosts/{h}/projects/{p}/{start\|stop\|restart}` | `volumes[]` (`name`, `driver`, `size`) / `{}` |
| `GET /hosts/{h}/containers` | `aurago_helper` (`runner`, `io`, `lister`) on helper containers, which also carry `protected_owner: "docker_manager"` (the UI checks `aurago_helper` first) |

### Open questions

1. Does the SSE stream send `done` (after `snapshot`) for an operation that has already finished? The UI handles both: a finished snapshot closes the stream itself.
2. Does `created` of a `StackSummary` stay the oldest container's creation time? The pane shows "Up <age>" from it.
3. Part B must keep the `Params` names of deviation 3 exactly; a renamed key makes the UI show the English `message` of that diagnostic.
4. Closing the window with unsaved edits is not intercepted (the desktop offers `setWindowBeforeClose` to some apps, but `ctx` of Docker Manager does not carry it, and `menus-and-routing.js` stays untouched here). Leaving a stack, switching hosts and closing the new-stack view do ask.

```go
// The shared CodeMirror bundle keeps every export the other editors use and adds YAML and the lint pieces of the Docker Manager.
func TestCodeMirrorBundleExportsYAMLAndLint(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	bundle, err := Content.ReadFile("js/vendor/codemirror-bundle.esm.js")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CodeMirror bundle missing from embedded UI: %v", err)
	}
	text := string(bundle)
	start := strings.LastIndex(text, "\nexport {")
	if start < 0 {
		t.Fatal("CodeMirror bundle has no export list")
	}
	list := strings.TrimSpace(text[start:])
	list = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(list, "export {"), "};")
	exported := map[string]bool{}
	for _, name := range strings.Split(list, ",") {
		exported[strings.TrimSpace(name)] = true
	}
	for _, want := range []string{
		"EditorView", "EditorState", "Compartment", "keymap", "lineNumbers", "history", "defaultKeymap", "indentWithTab", "javascript", "python", "go", "rust", "cpp", "json", "html", "css", "markdown",
		"oneDark", "syntaxHighlighting", "defaultHighlightStyle", "autocompletion", "closeBrackets", "lintKeymap",
		"yaml", "linter", "lintGutter", "setDiagnostics",
	} {
		if !exported[want] {
			t.Errorf("CodeMirror bundle does not export %q", want)
		}
	}
}
```

### Task D2: The model knows helper containers and keeps the answer body

**Files:**

- Modify (test): `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-model.js`

The server marks the runner, IO and lister containers (`aurago_helper`: `runner`, `io`, `lister`) and answers a remove with 409 `container_protected_confirmation_required` (owner `docker_manager`). The model treats them as protected: the server reports such a container with both `aurago_helper` and `protected_owner: "docker_manager"`, so the role is checked first and the lock says "Docker Manager helper" instead of "belongs to docker_manager". `normalizeError` keeps the whole answer body in `data`: the stack routes put more in it than the phase 1 routes (`file` and `current` of a `revision_conflict`, `operation_id` of a busy stack, `helpers` of an unprepared host, `command` of a missing runner image).

### Task D3: The stack model (pure helpers)

**Files:**

- Modify (test): `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`
- Create: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-stack-model.js`

`docker-manager-stack-model.js` is the pure part of the Stacks section and has no DOM and no network: stack status and tone, rows and groups of the list, host states, port links, ages and clocks, the lint helpers (which file a diagnostic belongs to, the localized text with a fallback to the server message, line ranges), the `.env` helpers and the random value, dropped-file classification, the line diff of the conflict dialog, the command palette ranking, and the reducer that folds the events of an operation's stream into one entry.

```js
// ---- stack model: names, status, rows, groups --------------------------------------------------------------------------
const sm = window.DockerManagerStackModel;
assert.ok(sm, 'the stack model publishes its global');
{
    eq(sm.validateName('immich'), null);
    eq(sm.validateName(''), { code: 'empty' });
    eq(sm.validateName('Immich'), { code: 'invalid' });
    eq(sm.validateName('-x'), { code: 'invalid' });
    eq(sm.validateName('a'.repeat(63)), null);
    eq(sm.validateName('a'.repeat(64)), { code: 'invalid' });
    eq(sm.validateName('shop', ['shop', 'media']), { code: 'taken' });
    assert.equal(sm.sanitizeName('My App v2!'), 'my-app-v2');
    assert.equal(sm.sanitizeName('--nginx'), 'nginx');
    assert.equal(sm.firstServiceName('services:\n  immich-server:\n    image: x\n  db:\n    image: y\n'), 'immich-server');
    assert.equal(sm.firstServiceName('version: "3"\nservices:\n  # first\n\n  Web:\n    image: x'), 'web');
    assert.equal(sm.firstServiceName('image: x'), '');

    const stack = (name, extra = {}) => ({ name, host_id: 'local', dir: '/opt/stacks/' + name, compose_file: 'compose.yaml', has_env: false, status: 'running', services: { total: 2, running: 2 }, ports: [], container_ids: [], created: 1760000000, ...extra });
    const listing = (stacks, extra = {}) => ({ host_id: 'local', stacks_dir: '/opt/stacks', stacks, external: [], ignored: [], ...extra });
    const stacksByHost = {
        local: { loaded: true, listing: listing([stack('shop'), stack('blog', { status: 'draft', services: { total: 0, running: 0 } })], { external: [{ name: 'legacy', working_dir: '/srv/legacy', status: 'partial', services: { total: 2, running: 1 }, ports: [], container_ids: [] }] }) },
        h_nas: { loaded: true, listing: listing([stack('media', { host_id: 'h_nas', ports: [{ service: 'plex', public_port: 32400, private_port: 32400, protocol: 'tcp' }] })]) }
    };
    const hs = [hostA, hostB];
    eq(sm.stackRows(hs, stacksByHost, 'all').map(row => row.key), ['local/shop', 'local/blog', 'h_nas/media']);
    eq(sm.stackRows(hs, stacksByHost, 'h_nas').map(row => row.key), ['h_nas/media'], 'a host scope shows only that host');
    eq(sm.externalRows(hs, stacksByHost, 'all').map(row => row.key), ['x:local/legacy']);
    const containerRows = model.buildRows(hs, { local: { containers: [container('shop-web', { compose_project: 'shop' }), container('tools')] }, h_nas: { containers: [container('loose')] } }, 'all');
    const groups = sm.stackGroups(hs, stacksByHost, containerRows, { scope: 'all', query: '' });
    eq(groups.stacks.map(row => row.stack.name), ['blog', 'media', 'shop'], 'own stacks sort by name across hosts');
    eq(groups.singles.map(row => model.containerName(row.c)), ['loose', 'tools'], 'only containers without a compose project are single');
    eq(sm.stackGroups(hs, stacksByHost, containerRows, { scope: 'all', query: 'nas plex' }).stacks.length, 0, 'the search words must all match (plex is a service, not a stack field)');
    eq(sm.stackGroups(hs, stacksByHost, containerRows, { scope: 'all', query: '32400' }).stacks.map(row => row.stack.name), ['media'], 'a published port matches');
    eq(sm.stackGroups(hs, stacksByHost, containerRows, { scope: 'all', query: 'legacy' }).external.length, 1);
    eq(plain(sm.stackCounts(hs, stacksByHost, 'all')), { stacks: 3, external: 1, total: 4 });
    assert.equal(sm.stackTone({ status: 'running' }), 'ok');
    assert.equal(sm.stackTone({ status: 'partial' }), 'warn');
    assert.equal(sm.stackTone({ status: 'error' }), 'bad');
    assert.equal(sm.stackTone({ status: 'draft' }), 'idle');
    assert.equal(sm.stackStatusId({ status: 'weird' }), 'stopped', 'an unknown status reads as stopped');
    assert.equal(sm.hostStacksState(undefined), 'loading');
    assert.equal(sm.hostStacksState({ loaded: true, error: null }), 'ok');
    assert.equal(sm.hostStacksState({ error: { code: 'host_not_prepared' } }), 'not_prepared');
    assert.equal(sm.hostStacksState({ error: { code: 'api_too_old' } }), 'api_too_old');
    assert.equal(sm.hostStacksState({ loaded: true, error: { code: 'host_unreachable' } }), 'unreachable');
    assert.equal(sm.hostStacksState({ error: { code: 'stacks_dir_unavailable' } }), 'unavailable');
    assert.equal(sm.hostStacksState({ error: { code: 'docker_error' }, loaded: false }), 'error');
    eq(plain(sm.stackActions({ status: 'running' })), { primary: 'update', restart: true, stop: true, pull: true, down: true, remove: true });
    eq(plain(sm.stackActions({ status: 'draft' })), { primary: 'deploy', restart: false, stop: false, pull: false, down: false, remove: true });
    assert.equal(sm.stackActions({ status: 'stopped' }).primary, 'deploy');

// ---- stack model: port links, time, bytes ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
    const ports = [
        { service: 'web', ip: '0.0.0.0', public_port: 8080, private_port: 80, protocol: 'tcp' },
        { service: 'web', ip: '::', public_port: 8080, private_port: 80, protocol: 'tcp' },
        { service: 'dns', ip: '', public_port: 53, private_port: 53, protocol: 'udp' },
        { service: 'admin', ip: '127.0.0.1', public_port: 9000, private_port: 9000, protocol: 'tcp' },
        { service: 'db', private_port: 5432, protocol: 'tcp' }
    ];
    eq(sm.portLinks(ports, '192.0.2.20').map(link => [link.label, link.url]), [['53', ''], ['8080', 'http://192.0.2.20:8080'], ['9000', '']], 'IPv4 and IPv6 bindings show once; UDP and loopback-only ports are not links; unpublished ports are skipped');
    assert.equal(sm.portLinks([ports[0]], '2001:db8::1')[0].url, 'http://[2001:db8::1]:8080', 'an IPv6 address is bracketed');
    assert.equal(sm.portLinks([ports[0]], '')[0].url, '', 'no address, no link');
    assert.equal(sm.linkAddress({ kind: 'local', address: 'unix:///var/run/docker.sock' }, 'desk.lan'), 'desk.lan', 'the local engine is reached under the name of the page');
    assert.equal(sm.linkAddress({ kind: 'ssh', address: '[2001:db8::1]' }, 'desk.lan'), '2001:db8::1');
    assert.equal(sm.linkAddress({ kind: 'tcp', address: 'docker.lan:2375' }, 'desk.lan'), 'docker.lan');
    const now = 1760000000 * 1000 + 3 * 86400 * 1000 + 5000;
    eq(sm.age(1760000000, now), { unit: 'days', n: 3 });
    eq(sm.age(1760000000, 1760000000 * 1000 + 2 * 3600 * 1000), { unit: 'hours', n: 2 });
    eq(sm.age(1760000000, 1760000000 * 1000 + 90 * 1000), { unit: 'minutes', n: 1 });
    eq(sm.age(1760000000, 1760000000 * 1000 + 5000), { unit: 'seconds', n: 5 });
    assert.equal(sm.age(0, now), null, 'a draft has no age');
    assert.equal(sm.clock(75), '1:15');
    assert.equal(sm.clock(3725), '1:02:05');
    assert.equal(sm.elapsed({ started_at: '2026-10-27T10:00:00Z', finished_at: '2026-10-27T10:01:05Z' }, 0), '1:05');
    assert.equal(sm.elapsed({ created_at: '2026-10-27T10:00:00Z' }, Date.parse('2026-10-27T10:00:09Z')), '0:09', 'a running operation counts from created_at');
    assert.equal(sm.elapsed({}, 0), '');
    eq([sm.formatBytes(0), sm.formatBytes(1536), sm.formatBytes(15 * 1024 * 1024), sm.formatBytes(-1), sm.formatBytes(3 * 1024 ** 3)], ['0 B', '1.5 KB', '15 MB', '', '3.0 GB']);
}

// ---- stack model: lint, .env, dropped files ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
    const diags = [
        { line: 5, severity: 'hint', code: 'image_latest', message: 'English', service: 'web' },
        { line: 2, severity: 'error', code: 'service_no_image', message: 'English', service: 'db' },
        { line: 2, severity: 'warning', code: 'variable_missing', message: 'English', params: { variable: 'DB_PASSWORD' }, fix: { kind: 'env_random', variable: 'DB_PASSWORD' } },
        { line: 3, severity: 'warning', code: 'env_syntax', message: 'English', params: { file: '.env', detail: 'expected KEY=value' } },
        { line: 7, severity: 'warning', code: 'brand_new_code', message: 'Only the server knows this' }
    ];
    eq(sm.sortDiagnostics(diags).map(d => d.code), ['service_no_image', 'variable_missing', 'env_syntax', 'image_latest', 'brand_new_code'], 'by line, then severity');
    eq(sm.splitDiagnostics(diags).env.map(d => d.code), ['env_syntax'], 'env_syntax belongs to the .env editor');
    eq(sm.splitDiagnostics(diags).compose.length, 4);
    eq(plain(sm.lintCounts(diags)), { error: 1, warning: 3, hint: 1 });
    assert.equal(sm.worstSeverity(diags), 'error');
    assert.equal(sm.worstSeverity([]), '');
    const t = (key, params) => key.replace('lint_', 'L:') + (params ? JSON.stringify(params) : '');
    assert.equal(sm.diagnosticText(diags[1], t), 'L:service_no_image{"service":"db"}', 'the service of the diagnostic fills {{service}}');
    assert.equal(sm.diagnosticText(diags[2], t), 'L:variable_missing{"variable":"DB_PASSWORD"}', 'the params of the diagnostic fill the text');
    assert.equal(sm.diagnosticText(diags[4], t), 'Only the server knows this', 'an unknown code keeps the server message');
    assert.equal(sm.diagnosticText(diags[0], key => 'Pin the tag of {{service}}'), 'English', 'a text whose placeholder stayed open falls back to the server message');
    eq(sm.randomFixes(diags), ['DB_PASSWORD']);
    eq(sm.randomFixes([{ fix: { kind: 'env_random', variable: 'bad name' } }]), [], 'a variable name that is no valid env name is never offered');
    const index = sm.lineIndex('a: 1\n  b: 2\r\n\nlast');
    eq(plain(sm.lineRange(index, 1)), { line: 1, from: 0, to: 4 });
    eq(plain(sm.lineRange(index, 2)), { line: 2, from: 7, to: 11 }, 'the range starts at the first non-blank character and ends before the line break');
    eq(plain(sm.lineRange(index, 2, 4)), { line: 2, from: 8, to: 11 }, 'a column moves the start');
    eq(plain(sm.lineRange(index, 99)), { line: 4, from: 14, to: 18 }, 'a line beyond the end is the last line');
    eq(plain(sm.lineRange(index, 0)), { line: 1, from: 0, to: 4 }, 'line 0 (the whole file) is the first line');
    assert.equal(sm.envHas('A=1\nexport DB_PASSWORD = x\n', 'DB_PASSWORD'), true);
    assert.equal(sm.envHas('#DB_PASSWORD=1\n', 'DB_PASSWORD'), false, 'a comment defines nothing');
    assert.equal(sm.appendEnvVariable('A=1', 'B', 'x'), 'A=1\nB=x\n');
    assert.equal(sm.appendEnvVariable('', 'B', 'x'), 'B=x\n');
    assert.equal(sm.appendEnvVariable('B=old\n', 'B', 'x'), 'B=old\n', 'an existing variable is never overwritten');
    assert.equal(sm.appendEnvVariable('A=1\n', 'bad name', 'x'), 'A=1\n');
    const fake = { getRandomValues: bytes => { for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) bytes[i] = (i * 37 + 11) % 256; return bytes; } };
    const value = sm.randomValue(32, fake);
    assert.match(value, /^[A-Za-z0-9]{32}$/);
    assert.equal(sm.randomValue(200, fake).length, 128, 'the length is capped');
    eq([sm.classifyDroppedFile('compose.yaml'), sm.classifyDroppedFile('docker-compose.yml'), sm.classifyDroppedFile('C:\\x\\immich.YML'), sm.classifyDroppedFile('.env'), sm.classifyDroppedFile('prod.env'), sm.classifyDroppedFile('notes.txt')], ['compose', 'compose', 'compose', 'env', 'env', '']);
    const preview = { services: [{ name: 'db', volumes: [{ kind: 'named', source: 'pg', target: '/var/lib/postgresql' }, { kind: 'relative', source: './data', target: '/data', read_only: true }] }, { name: 'web', volumes: [{ kind: 'tmpfs', target: '/tmp' }] }] };
    eq(plain(sm.storageGroups(preview)), { named: [{ service: 'db', source: 'pg', target: '/var/lib/postgresql', readOnly: false }], bind: [], relative: [{ service: 'db', source: './data', target: '/data', readOnly: true }], anonymous: [], tmpfs: [{ service: 'web', source: '', target: '/tmp', readOnly: false }] });
}

// ---- stack model: line diff ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
    const rows = sm.lineDiff('a\nb\nc\nd\n', 'a\nB\nc\nd\ne\n');
    eq(rows.map(row => row.type + ':' + row.text), ['same:a', 'del:b', 'add:B', 'same:c', 'same:d', 'add:e']);
    eq(rows.map(row => [row.oldNo, row.newNo]), [[1, 1], [2, 0], [0, 2], [3, 3], [4, 4], [0, 5]]);
    assert.equal(sm.diffChanged(rows), true);
    assert.equal(sm.diffChanged(sm.lineDiff('x\ny', 'x\ny\n')), false, 'a final line break alone is no difference');
    assert.equal(sm.diffChanged(sm.lineDiff('', '')), false);
    eq(sm.lineDiff('', 'a').map(row => row.type), ['add']);
    const long = Array.from({ length: 30 }, (unused, index) => 'line' + index).join('\n');
    const collapsed = sm.collapseDiff(sm.lineDiff(long, long.replace('line15', 'LINE15')), 2);
    eq(collapsed.map(row => row.type), ['skip', 'same', 'same', 'del', 'add', 'same', 'same', 'skip']);
    assert.equal(collapsed[0].count, 13);
    const big = Array.from({ length: 2500 }, (unused, index) => 'a' + index).join('\n'), other = Array.from({ length: 2500 }, (unused, index) => 'b' + index).join('\n');
    assert.equal(sm.lineDiff(big, other).length, 5000, 'a huge middle falls back to "all removed, all added" instead of a slow table');
}

// ---- stack model: palette --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
{
    assert.ok(sm.fuzzyScore('Restart immich', 'rest imm') > sm.fuzzyScore('Deploy my-immich', 'imm'), 'a hit at the start of a word ranks higher');
    assert.equal(sm.fuzzyScore('Restart immich', 'zzz'), 0);
    assert.ok(sm.fuzzyScore('Restart immich', 'rsti') > 0, 'a subsequence of two or more letters matches');
    assert.equal(sm.fuzzyScore('Restart immich', 'r z'), 0, 'every word must match');
    assert.equal(sm.fuzzyScore('anything', ''), 1);
    const items = [{ label: 'Deploy shop' }, { label: 'Open shop' }, { label: 'Restart shopping-list' }, { label: 'Prepare NAS' }];
    eq(sm.rankItems(items, 'shop').map(item => item.label), ['Deploy shop', 'Open shop', 'Restart shopping-list'], 'equal scores keep the original order');
    eq(sm.rankItems(items, 'open sh').map(item => item.label), ['Open shop']);
    assert.equal(sm.rankItems(items, '', 2).length, 2, 'the limit applies');
    eq(sm.highlight('Restart immich', 'imm'), [{ text: 'Restart ', hit: false }, { text: 'imm', hit: true }, { text: 'ich', hit: false }]);
    const hs2 = [{ id: 'local', name: 'Local' }, { id: 'h_nas', name: 'NAS' }];
    const row = (hostId, name, status) => ({ key: hostId + '/' + name, hostId, hostName: hostId === 'local' ? 'Local' : 'NAS', stack: { name, status } });
    const label = (action, params) => action + ':' + (params.stack || params.host || '');
    const data = { hosts: hs2, stackRows: [row('local', 'shop', 'running'), row('h_nas', 'blog', 'stopped'), row('local', 'wip', 'partial')], multi: true, hostStates: { local: 'ok', h_nas: 'not_prepared' }, scope: 'all', canMutate: true, label };
    eq(sm.paletteItems(data).map(item => item.id), [
        'open:local/shop', 'deploy:local/shop', 'restart:local/shop', 'stop:local/shop', 'open:h_nas/blog', 'deploy:h_nas/blog',
        'open:local/wip', 'deploy:local/wip', 'update:local/wip', 'restart:local/wip', 'stop:local/wip',
        'new:local', 'switch:local', 'new:h_nas', 'prepare:h_nas', 'switch:h_nas', 'refresh'
    ], 'actions follow the status; an unprepared host offers Prepare');
    assert.equal(sm.paletteItems(data)[1].action, 'update', 'a running stack offers Update, not Deploy');
    assert.equal(sm.paletteItems(data)[0].label, 'open:shop (Local)', 'several hosts: the host is part of the name');
    eq(sm.paletteItems(Object.assign({}, data, { canMutate: false })).map(item => item.action), ['open', 'open', 'open', 'switch_host', 'switch_host', 'refresh'], 'a read-only window gets no mutating command');
    const inside = sm.paletteItems(Object.assign({}, data, { scope: 'h_nas', stackRows: [], multi: false })).map(item => item.id);
    eq(inside.slice(-2), ['switch:all', 'refresh'], 'inside one host there is a way back to all hosts');
    assert.ok(inside.includes('switch:local') && !inside.includes('switch:h_nas'), 'and a way to the other host, but not to the one already shown');
}

// ---- stack model: folding the stream of an operation -------------------------------------------------------------------
{
    const op = { id: 'op_1', host_id: 'local', stack: 'shop', kind: 'up', state: 'running', output: 'hello\n', created_at: '2026-10-27T10:00:00Z' };
    const entry = sm.newOpEntry(op, 1000);
    assert.equal(entry.output, 'hello\n');
    sm.applyOpEvent(entry, { type: 'output', text: 'world\n' });
    assert.equal(entry.output, 'hello\nworld\n');
    sm.applyOpEvent(entry, { type: 'progress', progress: { id: 'db Pulling', status: 'Downloading', current: 50, total: 200 } });
    sm.applyOpEvent(entry, { type: 'progress', progress: { id: 'web Pulling', status: 'Waiting' } });
    sm.applyOpEvent(entry, { type: 'progress', progress: { id: 'db Pulling', current: 100 } });
    eq(sm.progressBars(entry).map(item => [item.id, item.percent]), [['db Pulling', 50]], 'only items with a total get a bar; a later event updates its item');
    assert.equal(entry.progress.length, 2);
    sm.applyOpEvent(entry, { type: 'state', operation: { id: 'op_1', state: 'health_wait' } });
    assert.equal(entry.op.state, 'health_wait');
    assert.equal(entry.op.stack, 'shop', 'a state event updates, it does not replace');
    assert.equal(entry.output, 'hello\nworld\n', 'a state event carries no output');
    assert.equal(sm.isActiveOp(entry.op), true);
    sm.applyOpEvent(entry, { type: 'done', operation: { id: 'op_1', state: 'failed', output: 'full output\n', error: 'boom', error_line: 4 } });
    assert.equal(sm.isActiveOp(entry.op), false);
    assert.equal(entry.output, 'full output\n', 'done carries the whole output');
    sm.applySnapshot(entry, { id: 'op_1', state: 'running', output: 'again\n' });
    eq([entry.output, entry.progress.length], ['again\n', 0], 'a snapshot replaces the output and the progress seen so far');
    const huge = sm.capOutput('x'.repeat(70 * 1024) + '\nlast line');
    assert.ok(huge.length <= sm.OUTPUT_CAP && huge.endsWith('last line'), 'the output keeps its tail');
    const e = n => ({ op: { state: n } });
    eq(sm.trimEntries([e('running'), e('succeeded'), e('failed'), e('queued'), e('succeeded')], 1).map(x => x.op.state), ['running', 'succeeded', 'queued'], 'active entries stay, finished ones are cut to the newest few');
    eq(plain(sm.parseJSON('{"a":1}')), { a: 1 });
    assert.equal(sm.parseJSON('not json'), null);
    assert.equal(sm.draftDirty({ text: 'a' }, { content: 'a' }), false);
    assert.equal(sm.draftDirty({ text: 'a' }, { content: 'b' }), true);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-stack-model.js`.**

```js
/* Docker Manager stack model: pure helpers for the Stacks section, no DOM and no network. A classic script
   (window.DockerManagerStackModel) so that scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs can run it in a Node vm. It owns the stack
   status and tone, the rows and groups of the stack list, the compose lint helpers, the line diff of the conflict dialog,
   the command palette ranking, the random .env value and the reducer that folds an operation's stream events into one
   entry. Everything that needs the host list, the translator or the clock takes it as an argument. */
(function () {
    'use strict';

    const SECTIONS = ['stacks', 'containers'];
    const STACK_TABS = ['overview', 'compose', 'env'];
    const STACK_STATUSES = ['running', 'partial', 'stopped', 'error', 'draft'];
    const STACK_TONE = { running: 'ok', partial: 'warn', error: 'bad', stopped: 'idle', draft: 'idle' };
    const OP_KINDS = ['prepare', 'config', 'up', 'down', 'stop', 'restart', 'pull', 'update', 'delete'];
    const OP_STATES = ['queued', 'running', 'health_wait', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'interrupted'];
    const ACTIVE_STATES = ['queued', 'running', 'health_wait'];
    const OP_TONE = { queued: 'idle', running: 'info', health_wait: 'info', succeeded: 'ok', failed: 'bad', interrupted: 'warn' };
    const SERVICE_STATES = ['running', 'exited', 'created', 'restarting', 'paused', 'dead', 'missing'];
    const LINT_CODES = ['yaml_syntax', 'not_a_mapping', 'no_services', 'service_no_image', 'invalid_port', 'port_duplicate', 'port_conflict',
        'variable_missing', 'image_latest', 'image_no_tag', 'privileged', 'docker_socket', 'network_mode_host', 'restart_missing', 'cap_add', 'env_syntax'];
    const SEVERITY_RANK = { error: 3, warning: 2, hint: 1 };
    const VOLUME_KINDS = ['named', 'bind', 'relative', 'anonymous', 'tmpfs'];
    const CONVERT_WARNINGS = ['flag_unsupported', 'flag_ignored', 'flag_value_invalid'];
    const NAME_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$/;
    const OUTPUT_CAP = 64 * 1024;
    const DIFF_CELL_LIMIT = 4000000;
    const ENV_NAME = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/;
    const ALPHABET = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';

    const text = value => (value == null ? '' : String(value));
    const lower = value => text(value).toLowerCase();
    const array = value => (Array.isArray(value) ? value : []);
    const objects = value => array(value).filter(item => item && typeof item === 'object');
    const compareText = (a, b) => text(a).localeCompare(text(b), undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' });

    // ---- names -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    // Mirrors dockerstacks.ValidateName: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$. `taken` lists the stack names already on the host.
    function validateName(name, taken) {
        const value = text(name);
        if (!value) return { code: 'empty' };
        if (!NAME_PATTERN.test(value)) return { code: 'invalid' };
        if (array(taken).includes(value)) return { code: 'taken' };
        return null;
    }

    // A folder-safe suggestion from a service name or an image: lower case, other characters become "-".
    function sanitizeName(value) {
        const cleaned = lower(value).replace(/[^a-z0-9_-]+/g, '-').replace(/^[^a-z0-9]+/, '').replace(/-+$/, '');
        return cleaned.slice(0, 63);
    }

    // The first key under `services:` of a pasted compose file, or ''.
    function firstServiceName(compose) {
        const match = /^services:[ \t]*(?:#.*)?\r?\n(?:[ \t]*(?:#.*)?\r?\n)*[ \t]+([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)[ \t]*:/m.exec(text(compose));
        return match ? sanitizeName(match[1]) : '';
    }

    // ---- stack status, rows and groups -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    const stackStatusId = stack => (STACK_STATUSES.includes(stack && stack.status) ? stack.status : 'stopped');
    const stackTone = stack => STACK_TONE[stackStatusId(stack)];

    function stackRows(hosts, byHost, scope) {
        const rows = [];
        for (const host of objects(hosts)) {
            if (scope && scope !== 'all' && host.id !== scope) continue;
            const listing = byHost && byHost[host.id] && byHost[host.id].listing;
            for (const stack of objects(listing && listing.stacks)) {
                rows.push({ key: host.id + '/' + stack.name, hostId: host.id, hostName: text(host.name), hostColor: host.color, stack });
            }
        }
        return rows;
    }

    function externalRows(hosts, byHost, scope) {
        const rows = [];
        for (const host of objects(hosts)) {
            if (scope && scope !== 'all' && host.id !== scope) continue;
            const listing = byHost && byHost[host.id] && byHost[host.id].listing;
            for (const project of objects(listing && listing.external)) {
                rows.push({ key: 'x:' + host.id + '/' + project.name, hostId: host.id, hostName: text(host.name), hostColor: host.color, project });
            }
        }
        return rows;
    }

    // Containers without a compose project (helper containers included: the Containers view shows them with a lock).
    const singleContainerRows = containerRows => objects(containerRows).filter(row => row.c && !text(row.c.compose_project));

    function stackHaystack(row) {
        const s = row.stack || row.project || {};
        const ports = objects(s.ports).map(port => port.public_port).filter(Boolean).join(' ');
        return lower([s.name, row.hostName, s.status, s.working_dir, s.dir, ports].join(' '));
    }

    function matchesStackQuery(row, query) {
        const terms = lower(query).split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
        if (!terms.length) return true;
        const hay = stackHaystack(row);
        return terms.every(term => hay.includes(term));
    }

    const byNameThenHost = hostOrder => (a, b) => {
        const nameA = (a.stack || a.project).name, nameB = (b.stack || b.project).name;
        const rank = id => { const index = array(hostOrder).indexOf(id); return index < 0 ? 999 : index; };
        return compareText(nameA, nameB) || rank(a.hostId) - rank(b.hostId);
    };

    // The three groups of the stack list, filtered by the search words. `containerRows` are the rows of model.buildRows.
    function stackGroups(hosts, byHost, containerRows, options) {
        const o = options || {}, order = objects(hosts).map(host => host.id);
        const sorter = byNameThenHost(order);
        const stacks = stackRows(hosts, byHost, o.scope).filter(row => matchesStackQuery(row, o.query)).sort(sorter);
        const external = externalRows(hosts, byHost, o.scope).filter(row => matchesStackQuery(row, o.query)).sort(sorter);
        const singles = singleContainerRows(containerRows).filter(row => {
            const c = row.c;
            const hay = lower([c.names && c.names[0], c.image, c.id, row.hostName, c.state].join(' '));
            return lower(o.query).split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).every(term => hay.includes(term));
        });
        singles.sort((a, b) => compareText(a.c.names && a.c.names[0], b.c.names && b.c.names[0]) || compareText(a.hostName, b.hostName));
        return { stacks, external, singles };
    }

    // What one host contributes to the stack list: ok | loading | not_prepared | api_too_old | unreachable | unavailable | error.
    function hostStacksState(entry) {
        if (!entry) return 'loading';
        const code = entry.error && entry.error.code;
        if (code === 'host_not_prepared') return 'not_prepared';
        if (code === 'api_too_old') return 'api_too_old';
        if (code === 'host_unreachable') return 'unreachable';
        if (code === 'stacks_unavailable' || code === 'stacks_dir_unavailable') return 'unavailable';
        if (entry.error && !entry.loaded) return 'error';
        return entry.loaded ? 'ok' : 'loading';
    }

    function stackCounts(hosts, byHost, scope) {
        const rows = stackRows(hosts, byHost, scope), external = externalRows(hosts, byHost, scope);
        return { stacks: rows.length, external: external.length, total: rows.length + external.length };
    }

    // The accent button of a stack: Deploy while nothing (or only part) runs, Update for a running stack.
    function primaryAction(stack) {
        const status = stackStatusId(stack);
        return status === 'running' ? 'update' : 'deploy';
    }

    // Which operations the detail header and the palette offer for a status. `deploy` runs kind up.
    function stackActions(stack) {
        const status = stackStatusId(stack), up = status === 'running' || status === 'partial';
        return { primary: primaryAction(stack), restart: up, stop: up, pull: status !== 'draft', down: status !== 'draft', remove: true };
    }

    const OP_FOR_ACTION = { deploy: 'up', update: 'update', restart: 'restart', stop: 'stop', pull: 'pull', down: 'down' };

    // ---- services, ports, time ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    function serviceTone(service) {
        const s = service || {}, state = lower(s.state), health = lower(s.health);
        if (state === 'running') return health === 'unhealthy' ? 'warn' : 'ok';
        if (state === 'restarting') return 'warn';
        if (state === 'dead') return 'bad';
        if (state === 'exited') return Number(s.exit_code) > 0 ? 'bad' : 'idle';
        return 'idle';
    }
    const serviceStateId = service => (SERVICE_STATES.includes(lower(service && service.state)) ? lower(service.state) : 'missing');

    const isLoopback = ip => ip === '127.0.0.1' || ip === '::1' || /^127\./.test(ip);

    // The address a browser can use for a host: the page's own host name for the local engine, else the host's address
    // without port and brackets.
    function linkAddress(host, pageHost) {
        const h = host || {};
        if (h.kind === 'local') return text(pageHost);
        let address = text(h.address).trim().replace(/^\[|\]$/g, '');
        if (/^[^:]+:\d+$/.test(address)) address = address.slice(0, address.lastIndexOf(':'));
        return address;
    }

    // One entry per published port (IPv4 and IPv6 bindings of the same port show once). `url` is empty for UDP and for
    // ports bound to the loopback of the engine host, which a browser elsewhere cannot reach.
    function portLinks(ports, address) {
        const seen = new Set(), out = [];
        const bare = text(address).includes(':') && !text(address).startsWith('[') ? '[' + address + ']' : text(address);
        for (const port of objects(ports)) {
            const published = Number(port.public_port) || 0;
            if (!published) continue;
            const protocol = text(port.protocol || 'tcp'), id = published + '/' + protocol + '/' + text(port.service);
            if (seen.has(id)) continue;
            seen.add(id);
            const reachable = protocol === 'tcp' && !isLoopback(text(port.ip)) && bare !== '';
            out.push({ key: id, label: String(published), service: text(port.service), protocol, container: Number(port.private_port) || 0, url: reachable ? 'http://' + bare + ':' + published : '' });
        }
        return out.sort((a, b) => Number(a.label) - Number(b.label));
    }

    // {unit, n}: the largest whole unit of the age of `createdSeconds` at `nowMs`; null for a draft (no containers).
    function age(createdSeconds, nowMs) {
        const created = Number(createdSeconds);
        if (!created) return null;
        const seconds = Math.max(0, Math.floor((Number(nowMs) || 0) / 1000 - created));
        if (seconds >= 86400) return { unit: 'days', n: Math.floor(seconds / 86400) };
        if (seconds >= 3600) return { unit: 'hours', n: Math.floor(seconds / 3600) };
        if (seconds >= 60) return { unit: 'minutes', n: Math.floor(seconds / 60) };
        return { unit: 'seconds', n: seconds };
    }

    const pad = n => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
    // 1536 -> "1.5 KB"; a negative or unknown size is ''.
    function formatBytes(bytes) {
        let value = Number(bytes);
        if (!(value >= 0)) return '';
        const units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB'];
        let unit = 0;
        while (value >= 1024 && unit < units.length - 1) { value /= 1024; unit += 1; }
        return (unit === 0 || value >= 10 ? String(Math.round(value)) : value.toFixed(1)) + ' ' + units[unit];
    }

    // m:ss, or h:mm:ss from one hour on.
    function clock(seconds) {
        const s = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(seconds) || 0));
        return s >= 3600 ? Math.floor(s / 3600) + ':' + pad(Math.floor(s / 60) % 60) + ':' + pad(s % 60) : Math.floor(s / 60) + ':' + pad(s % 60);
    }
    function elapsed(op, nowMs) {
        const o = op || {}, start = Date.parse(o.started_at || o.created_at || '');
        if (!Number.isFinite(start)) return '';
        const end = o.finished_at ? Date.parse(o.finished_at) : Number(nowMs) || Date.now();
        return clock(((Number.isFinite(end) ? end : start) - start) / 1000);
    }

    // ---- compose lint ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    // The file of a diagnostic is decided by its code: env_syntax belongs to .env (the server also sets params.file to ".env"),
    // everything else to the compose file.
    const diagnosticFile = d => (d && d.code === 'env_syntax' ? 'env' : 'compose');
    const severityOf = d => (SEVERITY_RANK[d && d.severity] ? d.severity : 'hint');

    function sortDiagnostics(list) {
        return objects(list).slice().sort((a, b) => (Number(a.line) || 0) - (Number(b.line) || 0) || SEVERITY_RANK[severityOf(b)] - SEVERITY_RANK[severityOf(a)]);
    }
    function splitDiagnostics(list) {
        const out = { compose: [], env: [] };
        for (const d of sortDiagnostics(list)) out[diagnosticFile(d)].push(d);
        return out;
    }
    function lintCounts(list) {
        const out = { error: 0, warning: 0, hint: 0 };
        for (const d of objects(list)) out[severityOf(d)] += 1;
        return out;
    }
    function worstSeverity(list) {
        const counts = lintCounts(list);
        return counts.error ? 'error' : counts.warning ? 'warning' : counts.hint ? 'hint' : '';
    }

    // The localized sentence of a diagnostic. Unknown codes and texts whose placeholders the server did not fill keep the
    // English message of the server.
    function diagnosticText(d, t) {
        if (!d) return '';
        if (!LINT_CODES.includes(d.code)) return text(d.message || d.code);
        const params = Object.assign(d.service ? { service: d.service } : {}, d.params || {});
        const out = t('lint_' + d.code, params);
        return /\{\{\w+\}\}/.test(out) ? text(d.message || out) : out;
    }

    // Offsets of every line start of `source`, for mapping diagnostics onto a plain textarea.
    function lineIndex(source) {
        const value = text(source), starts = [0];
        for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i += 1) if (value.charCodeAt(i) === 10) starts.push(i + 1);
        return { source: value, starts };
    }
    // {from, to} of a 1-based line (0 or out of range = the first or last line); a column starts the range there, else it
    // starts at the first non-blank character.
    function lineRange(index, line, column) {
        const count = index.starts.length, n = Math.min(Math.max(Number(line) || 1, 1), count);
        const from = index.starts[n - 1];
        let to = n < count ? index.starts[n] - 1 : index.source.length;
        if (index.source.charCodeAt(to - 1) === 13) to -= 1;
        const rowText = index.source.slice(from, to);
        const offset = Number(column) > 0 ? Number(column) - 1 : rowText.length - rowText.trimStart().length;
        return { line: n, from: Math.min(from + offset, to), to };
    }

    // The compose-side facts the new-stack preview shows.
    function storageGroups(preview) {
        const out = { named: [], bind: [], relative: [], anonymous: [], tmpfs: [] };
        for (const service of objects(preview && preview.services)) {
            for (const volume of objects(service.volumes)) {
                if (out[volume.kind]) out[volume.kind].push({ service: service.name, source: text(volume.source), target: text(volume.target), readOnly: !!volume.read_only });
            }
        }
        return out;
    }
    const randomFixes = list => [...new Set(objects(list).filter(d => d.fix && d.fix.kind === 'env_random' && ENV_NAME.test(text(d.fix.variable))).map(d => d.fix.variable))];

    // ---- .env --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    const escapeRe = value => value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
    function envHas(envText, name) {
        return ENV_NAME.test(text(name)) && new RegExp('^[ \\t]*(?:export[ \\t]+)?' + escapeRe(text(name)) + '[ \\t]*=', 'm').test(text(envText));
    }
    // Adds NAME=value on its own line; an existing definition is never overwritten.
    function appendEnvVariable(envText, name, value) {
        const base = text(envText);
        if (!ENV_NAME.test(text(name)) || envHas(base, name)) return base;
        return base + (base === '' || base.endsWith('\n') ? '' : '\n') + name + '=' + text(value) + '\n';
    }
    // A random value of letters and digits (safe unquoted in an .env file). `source` is a crypto-like object.
    function randomValue(length, source) {
        const wanted = Math.max(1, Math.min(Number(length) || 32, 128)), out = [];
        while (out.length < wanted) {
            const bytes = source.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(wanted * 2));
            for (const byte of bytes) {
                if (byte < 248 && out.length < wanted) out.push(ALPHABET[byte % 62]);
            }
        }
        return out.join('');
    }

    // ---- dropped files -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    // 'compose' for compose.yaml, docker-compose.yml and any other .yml/.yaml; 'env' for .env and *.env; else ''.
    function classifyDroppedFile(name) {
        const file = lower(name).split(/[\\/]/).pop();
        if (file === '.env' || file.endsWith('.env')) return 'env';
        if (/\.ya?ml$/.test(file)) return 'compose';
        return '';
    }

    // ---- line diff ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    function splitLines(value) {
        const source = text(value).replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');
        if (source === '') return [];
        const lines = source.split('\n');
        if (lines[lines.length - 1] === '') lines.pop();
        return lines;
    }

    // Rows {type: same|add|del, text, oldNo, newNo}. A common start and end are cut off first; the middle uses a longest
    // common subsequence, or a plain "all removed, all added" when it would be too large to compute.
    function lineDiff(before, after) {
        const a = splitLines(before), b = splitLines(after);
        let start = 0;
        while (start < a.length && start < b.length && a[start] === b[start]) start += 1;
        let endA = a.length, endB = b.length;
        while (endA > start && endB > start && a[endA - 1] === b[endB - 1]) { endA -= 1; endB -= 1; }
        const rows = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < start; i += 1) rows.push({ type: 'same', text: a[i], oldNo: i + 1, newNo: i + 1 });
        const midA = a.slice(start, endA), midB = b.slice(start, endB), n = midA.length, m = midB.length;
        let oldNo = start + 1, newNo = start + 1;
        const del = line => rows.push({ type: 'del', text: line, oldNo: oldNo++, newNo: 0 });
        const add = line => rows.push({ type: 'add', text: line, oldNo: 0, newNo: newNo++ });
        if (n * m > DIFF_CELL_LIMIT) {
            midA.forEach(del);
            midB.forEach(add);
        } else {
            const table = Array.from({ length: n + 1 }, () => new Uint32Array(m + 1));
            for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) for (let j = m - 1; j >= 0; j -= 1) {
                table[i][j] = midA[i] === midB[j] ? table[i + 1][j + 1] + 1 : Math.max(table[i + 1][j], table[i][j + 1]);
            }
            let i = 0, j = 0;
            while (i < n && j < m) {
                if (midA[i] === midB[j]) { rows.push({ type: 'same', text: midA[i], oldNo: oldNo++, newNo: newNo++ }); i += 1; j += 1; }
                else if (table[i + 1][j] >= table[i][j + 1]) { del(midA[i]); i += 1; }
                else { add(midB[j]); j += 1; }
            }
            while (i < n) { del(midA[i]); i += 1; }
            while (j < m) { add(midB[j]); j += 1; }
        }
        for (let k = endA; k < a.length; k += 1) rows.push({ type: 'same', text: a[k], oldNo: oldNo++, newNo: newNo++ });
        return rows;
    }

    const diffChanged = rows => objects(rows).some(row => row.type !== 'same');

    // Long unchanged runs become one {type: 'skip', count} row; `context` lines stay around every change.
    function collapseDiff(rows, context) {
        const keep = new Array(rows.length).fill(false), c = Math.max(0, context == null ? 3 : context);
        rows.forEach((row, index) => {
            if (row.type === 'same') return;
            for (let k = Math.max(0, index - c); k <= Math.min(rows.length - 1, index + c); k += 1) keep[k] = true;
        });
        const out = [];
        let skipped = 0;
        rows.forEach((row, index) => {
            if (keep[index]) {
                if (skipped) { out.push({ type: 'skip', count: skipped }); skipped = 0; }
                out.push(row);
            } else skipped += 1;
        });
        if (skipped) out.push({ type: 'skip', count: skipped });
        return out;
    }

    // ---- command palette ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    // Every word must appear in the label (a hit at the start of a word scores more); a word that is not a substring may
    // still match as a subsequence of at least two letters. 0 means no match.
    function fuzzyScore(label, query) {
        const words = lower(query).split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean), hay = lower(label);
        if (!words.length) return 1;
        let score = 0;
        for (const word of words) {
            const at = hay.indexOf(word);
            if (at >= 0) { score += at === 0 ? 3 : /[\s/_-]/.test(hay[at - 1]) ? 2 : 1; continue; }
            let k = 0;
            for (const ch of hay) if (ch === word[k]) k += 1;
            if (word.length >= 2 && k === word.length) score += 0.5; else return 0;
        }
        return score;
    }

    function rankItems(items, query, limit) {
        const ranked = array(items).map((item, order) => ({ item, order, score: fuzzyScore(item.label, query) })).filter(entry => entry.score > 0);
        ranked.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score || a.order - b.order);
        return ranked.slice(0, limit || 50).map(entry => entry.item);
    }

    // Segments {text, hit} of a label with the query words marked (substring hits only).
    function highlight(label, query) {
        const value = text(label), hay = lower(value), marks = new Array(value.length).fill(false);
        for (const word of lower(query).split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) {
            const at = hay.indexOf(word);
            if (at >= 0) for (let k = at; k < at + word.length; k += 1) marks[k] = true;
        }
        const out = [];
        for (let k = 0; k < value.length; k += 1) {
            const last = out[out.length - 1];
            if (last && last.hit === marks[k]) last.text += value[k]; else out.push({ text: value[k], hit: marks[k] });
        }
        return out;
    }

    // The commands for the current data. `label(action, params)` returns the translated label. Own stacks come first.
    function paletteItems(data) {
        const d = data || {}, label = d.label, items = [];
        const add = (id, action, params, extra) => items.push(Object.assign({ id, action, label: label(action, params || {}) }, extra));
        for (const row of objects(d.stackRows)) {
            const name = d.multi ? row.stack.name + ' (' + row.hostName + ')' : row.stack.name, base = { stackKey: row.key, hostId: row.hostId };
            const params = { stack: name };
            add('open:' + row.key, 'open', params, base);
            if (!d.canMutate) continue;
            const a = stackActions(row.stack);
            add('deploy:' + row.key, a.primary, params, base);
            if (stackStatusId(row.stack) === 'partial') add('update:' + row.key, 'update', params, base);
            if (a.restart) add('restart:' + row.key, 'restart', params, base);
            if (a.stop) add('stop:' + row.key, 'stop', params, base);
        }
        for (const host of objects(d.hosts)) {
            const params = { host: text(host.name) };
            if (d.canMutate) add('new:' + host.id, 'new_stack', params, { hostId: host.id });
            if (d.canMutate && d.hostStates && d.hostStates[host.id] === 'not_prepared') add('prepare:' + host.id, 'prepare', params, { hostId: host.id });
            if (d.scope !== host.id) add('switch:' + host.id, 'switch_host', params, { hostId: host.id });
        }
        if (d.scope !== 'all' && objects(d.hosts).length > 1) add('switch:all', 'switch_all', {}, { hostId: 'all' });
        add('refresh', 'refresh', {});
        return items;
    }

    // ---- operations: folding stream events into one entry ------------------------------------------------------------

    const isActiveState = state => ACTIVE_STATES.includes(state);
    const isActiveOp = op => isActiveState(op && op.state);

    function capOutput(value) {
        const source = text(value);
        if (source.length <= OUTPUT_CAP) return source;
        const cut = source.slice(source.length - OUTPUT_CAP), newline = cut.indexOf('\n');
        return newline >= 0 && newline < 512 ? cut.slice(newline + 1) : cut;
    }

    function newOpEntry(op, now) {
        const o = Object.assign({}, op);
        return { id: text(o.id), op: o, output: capOutput(o.output), progress: [], stream: 'idle', local: Number(now) || 0, shown: false };
    }

    // A fresh snapshot (first connect or reconnect) replaces the output and the progress seen so far.
    function applySnapshot(entry, op) {
        entry.op = Object.assign({}, op);
        entry.output = capOutput(op && op.output);
        entry.progress = [];
        return entry;
    }

    function mergeProgress(list, item) {
        if (!item || !item.id) return;
        let current = list.find(entry => entry.id === item.id);
        if (!current) { current = { id: text(item.id), parent: '', status: '', text: '', current: 0, total: 0, percent: 0 }; list.push(current); }
        for (const key of ['parent', 'status', 'text']) if (item[key] !== undefined) current[key] = text(item[key]);
        for (const key of ['current', 'total', 'percent']) if (item[key] !== undefined) current[key] = Number(item[key]) || 0;
        if (current.total > 0) current.percent = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, (current.current / current.total) * 100));
    }

    // Folds one stream event {type, text, progress, operation} into the entry. Returns the entry.
    function applyOpEvent(entry, event) {
        const e = event || {};
        if (e.type === 'output') entry.output = capOutput(entry.output + text(e.text));
        else if (e.type === 'progress') mergeProgress(entry.progress, e.progress);
        else if (e.type === 'state' && e.operation) entry.op = Object.assign({}, entry.op, e.operation, { output: entry.op.output });
        else if (e.type === 'done' && e.operation) {
            entry.op = Object.assign({}, e.operation);
            if (e.operation.output) entry.output = capOutput(e.operation.output);
        }
        return entry;
    }

    // Per-image bars: progress items that carry a total, in the order they were first seen.
    const progressBars = entry => objects(entry && entry.progress).filter(item => item.total > 0);

    // Newest first in, newest first out: every active entry stays, finished ones only up to `keep`.
    function trimEntries(entries, keep) {
        let finished = 0;
        return array(entries).filter(entry => isActiveOp(entry.op) || finished++ < keep);
    }

    function parseJSON(data) {
        try { const value = JSON.parse(data); return value && typeof value === 'object' ? value : null; } catch (error) { return null; }
    }

    // A draft is dirty when its text differs from the file as last loaded or saved.
    const draftDirty = (draft, file) => !!draft && text(draft.text) !== text(file && file.content);

    window.DockerManagerStackModel = {
        SECTIONS, STACK_TABS, STACK_STATUSES, STACK_TONE, OP_KINDS, OP_STATES, ACTIVE_STATES, OP_TONE, SERVICE_STATES, LINT_CODES, VOLUME_KINDS, CONVERT_WARNINGS,
        OUTPUT_CAP, OP_FOR_ACTION,
        validateName, sanitizeName, firstServiceName, stackStatusId, stackTone, stackRows, externalRows, singleContainerRows, matchesStackQuery, stackGroups,

        envHas, appendEnvVariable, randomValue, classifyDroppedFile, lineDiff, diffChanged, collapseDiff, fuzzyScore, rankItems, highlight, paletteItems,
        isActiveState, isActiveOp, capOutput, newOpEntry, applySnapshot, applyOpEvent, progressBars, trimEntries, parseJSON, draftDirty
    };
})();
```

### Task D4: The store lists stacks, saves files and follows operations

**Files:**

- Modify (test): `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-store.js`

New in the store: `state.section`, `state.stacks` (one listing per host, with the failure that host answered), `state.stack` (the open stack), `state.ops` (one entry per operation, newest first). Calls: `loadStacks`, `openStack`/`closeStack`/`setStackTab`/`loadStack`, `saveFiles` (with the revision), `createStack`, `loadHelpers`, `loadVolumes`, `lint` (a newer request of the same slot cancels the older one), `convertDockerRun`, `projectAction`, `startOp`, `prepareHost`, `deleteStack`, `loadOperations`, `loadOperation`, `loadActiveOperations`, `attachOperation`, `trackOperation`, `onOperationDone`. An operation is followed through one `EventSource` (the `eventSource` option, default `window.EventSource`) that is closed on `done`; after an error the operation is read again and the stream reopened with a growing delay (the `reconnectMs` option makes the Node test fast). The Refresh button passes `{force: true}` and only then is `?refresh=1` sent. `trackOperation` never lets a list answer replace live data: `GET /operations` blanks every `output`, so for an operation that is already followed it only updates the state, the times and the error; the output and the progress come from the stream (`snapshot`, `output`, `progress`, `done`) and from the re-read after a broken stream. `createStack` answers `{stack, operation?, deploy_error?}`: a deploy that could not start is a 201 with `deploy_error` and no operation, and nothing is followed.

```js
        ['POST ' + B + '/hosts/local/projects/legacy/restart']: {},

    FakeEventSource.all = [];
    const store = Store.create({ api, eventSource: url => new FakeEventSource(url) });
    await store.loadHosts();

    assert.equal(api.calls.find(call => call.method === 'DELETE').url, B + '/hosts/local/stacks/shop?volumes=1');

    assert.equal(api.calls.filter(call => call.method === 'GET' && call.key === 'GET ' + B + '/operations').pop().url, B + '/operations?host=local&stack=shop&active=1&limit=5');
```
